claims.quote: The Inuit on Baffin Island held great feasts, lasting several days, in which Sedna was ritually killed. These calendar feasts took place in the autumn when sealing was prevented by storms that broke the ice open.

statement.id: Orang Inuit di Pulau Baffin menggelar pesta besar berhari-hari yang di dalamnya Sedna dibunuh secara ritual. Pesta kalender ini berlangsung pada musim gugur ketika badai memecahkan es sehingga perburuan anjing laut terhalang.
statement.en: The Inuit on Baffin Island held great multi-day feasts in which Sedna was ritually killed; these calendar feasts took place in autumn, when storms breaking the ice prevented sealing.

claims.quote: Seals and other sea animals were the basis of the existence of nearly all Inuit. The relationship with the Sea Woman was therefore important but very sensitive: she not only controlled these animals, they originated from her.

statement.id: Anjing laut dan hewan laut lain menjadi dasar kehidupan hampir semua orang Inuit. Karena itu hubungan dengan Wanita Laut penting tetapi sangat peka: ia tidak hanya menguasai hewan-hewan itu, mereka berasal darinya.
statement.en: Seals and other sea animals were the basis of nearly all Inuit existence, so the relationship with the Sea Woman was important but very sensitive: she not only controlled these animals, they originated from her.

claims.quote: Variants of this myth have been recorded from many localities in Greenland and Canada, but from Alaska only a single reference exists. In some variants an orphan girl is thrown overboard, but more often the myth begins with the story of a girl who was fooled into marrying a petrel that had taken on human form.

statement.id: Varian mitos ini tercatat dari banyak tempat di Greenland dan Kanada, tetapi dari Alaska hanya ada satu rujukan. Dalam sebagian varian seorang gadis yatim dilempar dari kapal, tetapi lebih sering mitos dimulai dengan gadis yang ditipu menikahi seekor petrel yang berwujud manusia.
statement.en: Variants of the myth have been recorded from many localities in Greenland and Canada but from Alaska only one reference exists; in some an orphan girl is thrown overboard, but more often a girl is fooled into marrying a petrel that had taken human form.

claims.quote: The father tried to pacify the petrel by throwing his daughter overboard. When she tried to cling to the side of the boat, her father cut off her fingers at the first joint. Her fingertips fell into the sea and became small seals. When she again grasped the side of the boat, her father cut off her fingers at the next joint; these segments fell into the sea and became big, bearded seals.

statement.id: Sang ayah berusaha menenangkan petrel dengan melempar putrinya ke laut. Ketika ia berpegangan pada sisi perahu, ayahnya memotong jarinya pada ruas pertama; ujung jarinya jatuh ke laut dan menjadi anjing laut kecil. Ketika ia kembali berpegangan, ayahnya memotong pada ruas berikutnya; potongan itu menjadi anjing laut besar berjanggut.
statement.en: The father tried to pacify the petrel by throwing his daughter overboard; when she clung to the boat he cut off her fingers at the first joint, and the fingertips became small seals, and at the next joint the segments became big, bearded seals.

claims.quote: When she still clung to the side of the boat with the stumps of her fingers, her father cut them off at the last joint, and these segments turned into walruses. Sometimes the order of the creation of the sea animals is different, with whales being created first (the girl's nails are associated with baleen), followed by small seals and bearded seals.

statement.id: Ketika ia masih berpegangan dengan sisa-sisa jarinya, ayahnya memotongnya pada ruas terakhir dan potongan itu menjadi walrus. Kadang urutan terciptanya hewan laut berbeda: paus tercipta lebih dulu (kuku sang gadis dikaitkan dengan balin), disusul anjing laut kecil dan anjing laut berjanggut.
statement.en: When she still clung with the stumps of her fingers, her father cut them off at the last joint and these segments turned into walruses; sometimes the order differs, with whales created first (the girl's nails are linked to baleen), then small seals and bearded seals.

claims.quote: Traditional Inuit tattoos often include lines across a woman's fingers, knuckles, or wrists, alluding to the story of where Sedna's fingers were cut. Some say Sedna denies access to the afterlife to women whose fingers weren’t tattooed.

statement.id: Tato tradisional Inuit sering memuat garis melintang di jari, buku jari, atau pergelangan tangan perempuan, merujuk pada kisah tempat jari Sedna dipotong. Sebagian orang mengatakan Sedna menolak jalan ke alam baka bagi perempuan yang jarinya tidak bertato.
statement.en: Traditional Inuit tattoos often include lines across a woman's fingers, knuckles, or wrists, alluding to the story of where Sedna's fingers were cut, and some say Sedna denies access to the afterlife to women whose fingers were not tattooed.

claims.quote: in art Sedna is usually depicted with the head and upper body of a woman and the tail of a marine mammal, similar to a mermaid.

statement.id: Dalam seni, Sedna biasanya digambarkan berkepala dan berbadan atas perempuan dengan ekor mamalia laut, mirip putri duyung.
statement.en: In art Sedna is usually depicted with the head and upper body of a woman and the tail of a marine mammal, similar to a mermaid.

claims.quote: 90377 Sedna, a trans-Neptunian object discovered by ... on November 14, 2003, is named after her.

statement.id: Objek trans-Neptunus 90377 Sedna, yang ditemukan pada 14 November 2003, dinamai menurut namanya.
statement.en: The trans-Neptunian object 90377 Sedna, discovered on November 14, 2003, is named after her.

short_description.id: Set animal, atau sha, adalah hewan yang berkaitan dengan dewa Set dalam seni Mesir kuno; identitasnya sebagai hewan nyata tidak pasti.
short_description.en: The Set animal, or sha, is the animal associated with the god Set in ancient Egyptian art; its identity as a real animal is uncertain.

long_description.id: Dalam seni Mesir kuno, Set animal atau sha adalah hewan yang dikaitkan dengan dewa Set. Karena Set disamakan dengan monster Yunani Typhon, hewan ini juga dikenal sebagai hewan Typhon. Hieroglif hewan ini menjadi salah satu cara menggambarkan Set, dan hieroglif umum lainnya berupa dewa duduk yang berkepala hewan tersebut.
long_description.en: In ancient Egyptian art, the Set animal, or sha, is the animal linked to the god Set. Since Set was equated with the Greek monster Typhon, the animal is also known as the Typhonian animal. Its hieroglyph is one way of portraying Set, and the other common hieroglyph is a seated god with the head of that animal.

long_description.id: Sha biasanya digambarkan sebagai canid ramping dengan ekor kaku, telinga tegak, dan moncong panjang. Hieroglifnya menjadi penentu kata yang berhubungan dengan penderitaan, kekerasan, dan badai. Gambarnya muncul dalam seni Mesir dari Naqada III sampai sekurang-kurangnya Kerajaan Baru, dan penggunaan paling awal yang diketahui terdapat pada Kepala Gada Scorpion.
long_description.en: The sha is usually depicted as a slender canid with a stiff tail, erect ears and a long muzzle. Its hieroglyph is a determinative for words connected with suffering, violence and storms. Its image appears in Egyptian art from Naqada III until at least the New Kingdom, and its first known use is on the Scorpion Macehead.

long_description.id: Identitas hewan ini tidak jelas. Ia mungkin sepenuhnya mitologis atau gabungan ciri hewan nyata, sedangkan Ken Moss mengusulkan bahwa ia Saluki. Di luar kaitannya dengan Set, sha tidak memiliki mitologi mandiri yang dapat membantu identifikasinya.
long_description.en: The identity of the animal is unclear. It may be fully mythological or based on a combination of real animals, while Ken Moss proposed that it is the Saluki. Outside its association with Set, the sha has no independent mythology that could aid its identification.

long_description.id: World History Encyclopedia menyebut Set kadang digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip anjing berbulu lebat berwarna merah yang dikenal sebagai sha, dan menyatakan para sarjana berbeda pendapat apakah ia dimodelkan pada Saluki atau makhluk mitologis murni. Tongkat was, yang dibawa dewa, firaun, dan pendeta, melambangkan Set animal atau Khnum.
long_description.en: World History Encyclopedia says Set is sometimes depicted as a shaggy red dog-like beast known as a sha, and states that scholars disagree whether it was modelled on the Saluki or was a purely mythological creature. The was-sceptre, carried by gods, pharaohs and priests, represents the Set animal or Khnum.

short_description.id: Aligator saluran air adalah legenda urban tentang aligator yang dikatakan hidup di saluran air di luar wilayah aslinya, terutama New York City, meski tidak pernah terbukti.
short_description.en: The sewer alligator is an urban legend about alligators said to live in sewers outside their native range, above all in New York City, though never proven.

long_description.id: Aligator saluran air adalah legenda urban tentang aligator yang dikatakan hidup di saluran air di luar wilayah aslinya. Kota yang konon pernah menemukannya antara lain New York City dan Paris. Laporan tentang aligator dewasa tidak terbukti, tetapi aligator kecil kadang diselamatkan dari saluran, dan kisahnya berasal dari akhir 1920-an dan awal 1930-an.
long_description.en: The sewer alligator is an urban legend about alligators said to live in sewers outside their native range. Cities where they have supposedly been found include New York City and Paris. Reports of full-grown sewer alligators are unproven, though small alligators are sometimes rescued from sewers, and the stories date to the late 1920s and early 1930s.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, aligator menyusuri saluran New York City, memangsa tikus dan sampah, dan mengancam pekerja saluran yang konon membawa senjata api. Mereka sering digambarkan besar dan buas, kadang disebut albino, buta, dan putih, atau bahkan mutan akibat limbah kimia. Asal-usulnya sering dikaitkan dengan bayi aligator yang dibeli turis sebagai suvenir dari Florida lalu dibuang ke toilet; teori yang paling masuk akal menyebut orang tua membuang aligator yang dibeli untuk anak-anak mereka.
long_description.en: In the legend, alligators roam New York City's sewers, preying on rats and refuse and threatening sewer workers who are said to carry firearms. They are often described as large and vicious, sometimes as albino, blind, and white, or even as mutants from chemical waste. The origin is often linked to baby alligators that tourists bought as souvenirs in Florida and then flushed down the toilet; the most plausible theory has parents dumping alligators bought for their children.

long_description.id: Pada 10 Februari 1935 New York Times memuat laporan bahwa beberapa remaja menyeret aligator hidup sepanjang delapan kaki keluar dari saluran air di Harlem; warga menduga hewan itu jatuh dari perahu di Sungai Harlem. Menurut buku The World Beneath the City (1959), mantan pengawas saluran Teddy May mengaku melihat koloni aligator sepanjang sekitar dua kaki dan memerintahkan pemusnahannya. Setelah laporan 1930-an, kisahnya berkembang selama puluhan tahun menjadi legenda kontemporer.
long_description.en: On February 10, 1935, the New York Times carried a report that teenagers dragged a live eight-foot alligator out of a Harlem sewer; locals speculated that the animal had fallen from a boat in the Harlem River. According to the book The World Beneath the City (1959), former sewer superintendent Teddy May said he saw alligators averaging about two feet long and ordered their extermination. After the reports of the 1930s, the story built up over the decades into a contemporary legend.

long_description.id: Kenyataannya, aligator yang kabur atau dibuang hanya mungkin bertahan sebentar di saluran New York, sebab saluran terlalu dingin dan mengandung bakteri berbahaya dari limbah; pekerja saluran mengatakan tidak ada populasi tersembunyi. Legenda ini muncul dalam film Alligator (1980), yang menampilkan aligator mutan raksasa.
long_description.en: In reality escaped or abandoned alligators can survive only briefly in New York's sewers, which are too cold and contain harmful bacteria from waste; sewer workers say there is no hidden population. The legend appears in the 1980 film Alligator, which features a gigantic mutant alligator.

claims.quote: Some cities in which sewer alligators have supposedly been found are New York City and Paris.

statement.id: Beberapa kota yang konon ditemukan aligator gorong-gorong adalah New York City dan Paris.
statement.en: Some cities in which sewer alligators have supposedly been found are New York City and Paris.

claims.quote: Accounts of fully grown sewer alligators are unproven, but small alligators are sometimes rescued from sewers.

statement.id: Kisah aligator dewasa di gorong-gorong belum terbukti tetapi buaya kecil terkadang diselamatkan.
statement.en: Accounts of fully grown sewer alligators are unproven, but small alligators are sometimes rescued from sewers.

claims.quote: The legend of alligators inhabiting the sewer system of New York City is a widely circulated urban myth. It suggests that alligators navigate the city's sewers, preying on rats and other refuse, and posing a threat to sewer workers, who are said to carry firearms for protection.

statement.id: Legenda tentang aligator yang menghuni sistem saluran air New York City adalah mitos urban yang tersebar luas; ia menyatakan bahwa aligator menyusuri saluran kota, memangsa tikus dan sampah lain, serta mengancam pekerja saluran yang konon membawa senjata api untuk perlindungan.
statement.en: The legend of alligators inhabiting the sewer system of New York City is a widely circulated urban myth; it suggests that alligators navigate the city's sewers, preying on rats and other refuse, and posing a threat to sewer workers, who are said to carry firearms for protection.

claims.quote: Following reports of sewer alligators in the 1930s, the story built up over the decades and became more of a contemporary legend.

statement.id: Setelah laporan tahun 1930-an kisah ini berkembang menjadi legenda kontemporer.
statement.en: Following reports of sewer alligators in the 1930s, the story built up over the decades and became more of a contemporary legend.

claims.quote: The sewer alligator is an urban legend about alligators that are said to live in sewers outside alligators' native range.

statement.id: Aligator saluran air adalah legenda urban tentang aligator yang dikatakan hidup di saluran air di luar wilayah asli aligator.
statement.en: The sewer alligator is an urban legend about alligators that are said to live in sewers outside alligators' native range.

claims.quote: Stories date back to the late 1920s and early 1930s.

statement.id: Kisah-kisahnya berasal dari akhir 1920-an dan awal 1930-an.
statement.en: Stories date back to the late 1920s and early 1930s.

claims.quote: Escaped or abandoned alligators may survive for a short time in New York's sewers. However, they cannot live there long-term because the sewers are too cold and contain harmful bacteria from human waste. Sewer workers say there is no hidden population of alligators living underground.

statement.id: Aligator yang kabur atau dibuang mungkin bertahan sebentar di saluran air New York, tetapi tidak dapat hidup lama di sana karena saluran terlalu dingin dan mengandung bakteri berbahaya dari limbah manusia; pekerja saluran mengatakan tidak ada populasi tersembunyi aligator di bawah tanah.
statement.en: Escaped or abandoned alligators may survive for a short time in New York's sewers but cannot live there long-term because the sewers are too cold and contain harmful bacteria from human waste; sewer workers say there is no hidden population of alligators living underground.

claims.quote: According to the lore, these alligators are often described as large and vicious, with some attributing a lack of pigmentation to their purported status as "albinos."

statement.id: Menurut kisahnya, aligator ini sering digambarkan besar dan buas, dengan sebagian orang mengaitkan kurangnya pigmen dengan status mereka yang konon 'albino'.
statement.en: According to the lore, these alligators are often described as large and vicious, with some attributing a lack of pigmentation to their purported status as 'albinos'.

claims.quote: As late as the middle of the 20th century, souvenir shops in Florida sold live baby alligators (in small fish tanks) as novelty souvenirs. Tourists from New York City would buy a baby alligator and try to raise it as a pet. When the alligator grew too large for comfort, the family would proceed to flush the reptile down the toilet.
claims.locator: Louisiana or Florida to New York City

statement.id: Hingga pertengahan abad ke-20, toko suvenir di Florida menjual bayi aligator hidup sebagai oleh-oleh; turis dari New York City membelinya dan mencoba memeliharanya, dan ketika aligator terlalu besar, keluarga itu membuangnya ke toilet.
statement.en: As late as the middle of the 20th century, souvenir shops in Florida sold live baby alligators as novelty souvenirs; tourists from New York City bought them and tried to raise them as pets, and when the alligator grew too large, the family flushed it down the toilet.

claims.quote: Some people even spoke of mutant alligators living in the sewers which have been exposed to many different types of toxic chemical waste which altered them, making them deformed and sometimes even larger and with strange colouring.

statement.id: Sebagian orang bahkan menyebut aligator mutan yang hidup di saluran air dan terpapar berbagai limbah kimia beracun yang mengubah mereka sehingga cacat, kadang lebih besar, dan berwarna aneh.
statement.en: Some people even spoke of mutant alligators living in the sewers that were exposed to many types of toxic chemical waste, altering them, making them deformed and sometimes larger and strangely coloured.

claims.quote: The New York Times reports that the city rescues several alligators each year.

statement.id: The New York Times melaporkan bahwa kota itu menyelamatkan beberapa aligator setiap tahun.
statement.en: The New York Times reports that the city rescues several alligators each year.

claims.quote: On February 10, 1935, the New York Times carried an astonishing report that several teenagers had dragged a live eight-foot alligator out of a sewer in Harlem the previous evening.

statement.id: Pada 10 Februari 1935, New York Times memuat laporan mengejutkan bahwa beberapa remaja menyeret aligator hidup sepanjang delapan kaki keluar dari saluran air di Harlem malam sebelumnya.
statement.en: On February 10, 1935, the New York Times carried an astonishing report that several teenagers had dragged a live eight-foot alligator out of a sewer in Harlem the previous evening.

claims.quote: The locals at the time speculated that the animal had fallen from a boat passing through the nearby Harlem River and had swum 150 yards up a storm conduit.

statement.id: Warga setempat saat itu menduga hewan itu jatuh dari perahu yang lewat di Sungai Harlem di dekatnya dan berenang 150 yard menyusuri saluran air hujan.
statement.en: The locals at the time speculated that the animal had fallen from a boat passing through the nearby Harlem River and had swum 150 yards up a storm conduit.

claims.quote: According to The World Beneath the City (1959), a book by Robert Daley about New York’s underground utilities, a former sewer superintendent named Teddy May said he had seen alligators with his own eyes during an inspection tour around 1935.

statement.id: Menurut The World Beneath the City (1959), buku Robert Daley tentang utilitas bawah tanah New York, mantan pengawas saluran bernama Teddy May mengaku melihat sendiri aligator saat inspeksi sekitar 1935.
statement.en: According to The World Beneath the City (1959), a book by Robert Daley about New York's underground utilities, a former sewer superintendent named Teddy May said he had seen alligators with his own eyes during an inspection tour around 1935.

claims.quote: May had heard repeated reports of subterranean gators from sewer workers, and was startled to find that his men weren’t kidding. The animals averaged about two feet in length, and apparently hung out in some of the smaller branch pipes where the water flowed relatively slowly.

statement.id: May telah berulang kali mendengar laporan tentang aligator bawah tanah dari para pekerja dan terkejut mendapati mereka tidak bercanda; hewan itu rata-rata sepanjang sekitar dua kaki dan tampaknya berkumpul di pipa cabang kecil tempat air mengalir relatif lambat.
statement.en: May had heard repeated reports of subterranean gators from sewer workers and was startled to find his men weren't kidding; the animals averaged about two feet in length and apparently hung out in some of the smaller branch pipes where the water flowed relatively slowly.

claims.quote: But the pitiless May was no animal lover either, and he ordered the gators exterminated. Sewer workers used poison and a few zealots even tried rifles and pistols. In a few months they were all gone.

statement.id: May tidak berbelas kasihan dan memerintahkan aligator dimusnahkan; para pekerja memakai racun dan beberapa orang bersemangat bahkan mencoba senapan dan pistol, dan dalam beberapa bulan semuanya lenyap.
statement.en: The pitiless May was no animal lover and ordered the gators exterminated; sewer workers used poison and a few zealots even tried rifles and pistols, and in a few months they were all gone.

claims.quote: Though nobody knew for sure how the alligators got there, the most plausible theory was that they had been dumped into the sewers by parents who had originally bought them for their children and later grew tired of them.

statement.id: Meski tak ada yang yakin bagaimana aligator itu sampai di sana, teori paling masuk akal adalah bahwa mereka dibuang ke saluran oleh orang tua yang semula membelinya untuk anak-anak lalu bosan.
statement.en: Though nobody knew for sure how the alligators got there, the most plausible theory was that they had been dumped into the sewers by parents who had bought them for their children and later grew tired of them.

claims.quote: The more rococo versions of the legend claim that the animals are blind and white — blind because it’s too dark to see, and white because they don’t get any sunlight.

statement.id: Versi legenda yang lebih berlebihan menyatakan bahwa hewan itu buta dan putih: buta karena terlalu gelap untuk melihat dan putih karena tak terkena sinar matahari.
statement.en: The more rococo versions of the legend claim that the animals are blind and white: blind because it is too dark to see, and white because they get no sunlight.

short_description.id: Shangyang adalah burung mitologi Tiongkok yang dapat meramalkan hujan.
short_description.en: Shangyang is a Chinese mythological bird capable of predicting rain.

long_description.id: Shangyang adalah burung mitologi Tiongkok yang dapat meramalkan hujan. Makhluk ini dikaitkan dengan Yu Shi, Penguasa Hujan, meski seorang ahli mitografi justru mengaitkan Yu Shi dengan burung Bi Fang. Sebuah kisah menyebutnya menari dengan satu kaki di istana Qi.
long_description.en: Shangyang is a Chinese mythological bird capable of predicting rain. This creature is associated with Yu Shi, the Lord of Rain, although one mythographer links Yu Shi with the Bi Fang bird instead. One account describes it dancing on one leg at the court of Qi.

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah teks klasik, burung berkaki satu itu terbang ke istana Qi dan membuat sang marquis mengirim utusan kepada Konfusius. Konfusius menyebutnya Shangyang, pertanda air, dan mengutip nyanyian anak-anak tentang hujan lebat. Rakyat disuruh membenahi parit dan tanggul, sehingga hanya Qi yang siap ketika banjir datang, sedangkan negara lain rusak.
long_description.en: In a classical text, the one-legged bird flies into the court of Qi and prompts the marquis to send an envoy to Confucius. Confucius names it the Shangyang, a water omen, and cites the children's rhyme about heavy rain. The people are told to repair ditches and dikes, so only Qi is ready when the flood comes while other states suffer.

cultural_context.id: Kisah burung ini sering dipakai sebagai contoh kebodohan orang yang mengabaikan nasihat bijak.

did_you_know.en: According to the classical text, children once sang "Heaven will send great rain, the Shangyang dances" while hopping on one leg.

The Shangyang was particularly associated with the Lord of Rain, Yu Shi. Once, the Shangyang was said to have visited the royal court of Qi, where it danced on one leg.

claims.quote: 齊有一足之鳥，飛集於宮朝，下止於殿前，舒翅而跳。齊侯大怪之，使使聘魯，問孔子。

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik ini, seekor burung berkaki satu (一足之鳥) terbang ke istana negeri Qi (齊), mendarat di depan balai, dan melompat dengan sayap terkembang; Marquis Qi (齊侯) heran lalu mengutus orang ke negeri Lu (魯) untuk bertanya kepada Konfusius (孔子).
statement.en: In this classical text, a one-legged bird (一足之鳥) flies into the court of Qi (齊), lands before the hall, and hops with spread wings; the Marquis of Qi (齊侯) is astonished and sends an envoy to Lu (魯) to ask Confucius (孔子).

claims.quote: 孔子曰：「此鳥名曰商羊，水祥也。昔童兒有屈其一腳，振訊兩眉，而跳且謠曰：『天將大雨，商羊鼓舞。』今齊有之，其應至矣。」

statement.id: Konfusius (孔子) berkata bahwa burung itu bernama Shangyang (商羊), pertanda air (水祥); dulu anak-anak menekuk satu kaki, mengerutkan alis, melompat sambil bernyanyi "Langit akan menurunkan hujan lebat, Shangyang menari", dan kini Qi memilikinya sehingga pertandanya telah tiba.
statement.en: Confucius (孔子) says the bird is named Shangyang (商羊), a water omen (水祥); children once bent one leg, knitted their brows, and hopped singing "Heaven will send great rain, the Shangyang dances", and now that Qi has it, the sign has arrived.

short_description.id: Sheka adalah makhluk mirip kurcaci dalam mitologi Turkik yang tinggal di hutan atau rumah terbengkalai; dalam paganisme Slavia ia dikenal sebagai roh ladang.
short_description.en: Sheka is a dwarf-like being of Turkic mythology that lives in forests or derelict houses; in Slavic paganism it is a field spirit.

long_description.id: Sheka (Sirilik: Шекә) adalah makhluk mirip kurcaci dalam mitologi Turkik yang tinggal di hutan atau rumah terbengkalai; dalam legenda ia cenderung muncul dalam situasi lucu. Artikel Wikipedia bahasa Katalan menyebutnya makhluk mitologi Tatar dengan nama Şekä, dan Çike dalam bahasa Turki.
long_description.en: Sheka (Cyrillic: Шекә) is a small, dwarf-like figure from Turkic mythology, living in woods or in ruined houses, and legends tend to place it in humorous scenes. The Catalan Wikipedia article calls it a being of Tatar mythology named Şekä, and Çike in Turkish.

long_description.id: Dalam paganisme Slavia, Sheka adalah roh ladang berwujud kurcaci cacat dengan mata berbeda warna dan rumput sebagai pengganti rambut. Ia muncul pada tengah hari atau senja dan mengenakan pakaian serba hitam atau serba putih.
long_description.en: In Slavic paganism Sheka is a field spirit in the form of a deformed dwarf with differently coloured eyes and grass instead of hair. It appears at noon or sunset and wears either all black or all white.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan setempat, Sheka menyesatkan orang yang mengembara di ladang, menularkan penyakit, atau melindas orang yang tertidur dengan kuda, dan senang menarik rambut petani yang bekerja di siang hari. Ia juga membuat anak kecil tersesat di ladang jagung dan memaksa orang yang ditangkapnya bernyanyi selama berjam-jam.
long_description.en: According to local beliefs Sheka leads wandering people astray in a field, gives them diseases or rides them over with horses if they are found asleep, and enjoys pulling the hair of peasants working at midday. It also makes little children get lost in cornfields and forces anyone it catches to sing for hours.

short_description.id: Shirime adalah yōkai yang dari jauh tampak seperti manusia, tetapi tak berwajah dan punya mata di bagian pantatnya.
short_description.en: Shirime is a yōkai that looks human from a distance, but has no face and an eye in its butt.

long_description.id: Shirime (尻目, secara harfiah "mata pantat") adalah yōkai yang dari jauh tampak seperti manusia. Ia tidak punya ciri wajah, tetapi memiliki mata di lubang pantatnya. Dalam kisahnya, mata besar yang berkilau terbuka di hadapan seorang pengelana.
long_description.en: Shirime (尻目, literally "buttocks eye") is a yōkai that appears human from a distance. It has no face, yet an eye sits where its anus would be. In its tale, a huge glittering eye opens before a traveler.

long_description.id: Menurut Yokai.com, shirime mendekati pengelana di jalan larut malam dengan rupa pria berkimono dan menanyakan apakah mereka punya waktu sebentar. Sebelum dijawab, ia menjatuhkan kimononya, membungkuk, dan memperlihatkan mata raksasa yang bersinar di lubang pantatnya, yang disebut bersinar seperti kilat.
long_description.en: According to Yokai.com, shirime comes up to travelers on the road in the dead of night, dressed like a man in a kimono, and asks whether they can spare a moment. Before they reply, it lets its kimono fall, bends over, and reveals the giant shining eye in its butt hole, said to shine like lightning.

long_description.id: Selain perilakunya yang mengejutkan, shirime tidak melakukan hal yang merugikan, dan kegembiraannya datang dari menakut-nakuti. Penyair dan pelukis Buson menyukainya dan memasukkannya ke banyak lukisan yōkai. Yokai.com menilai shirime sangat mungkin kerabat dekat noppera-bō, hantu tanpa wajah lainnya.
long_description.en: Shirime does not mean to harm people, and its joy comes from scaring them; Yokai.com notes it does nothing harmful beyond its startling behavior. The haiku poet and artist Buson liked it so much that he included it in many of his yōkai paintings. Yokai.com judges that shirime is very likely a close relative of the noppera-bō, another faceless ghost.

note.id: Yokai.com menilai shirime sangat mungkin kerabat dekat noppera-bō, hantu tanpa wajah lainnya.
note.en: Yokai.com judges shirime to be very likely a close relative of the noppera-bō, another faceless ghost.

short_description.id: Shukra merupakan resi mitologis dan dewa yang memimpin planet Venus dalam Hindu.
short_description.en: Shukra is a mythological sage and presiding god of Venus in Hinduism.

long_description.id: Shukra merupakan resi mitologis dan dewa yang memimpin planet Venus dalam Hindu. Nama lainnya Ushanas dan Kavya.
long_description.en: Shukra is a mythological sage and presiding god of Venus in Hinduism. His other names are Ushanas and Kavya.

long_description.id: Dalam Rigveda ia merupakan resi bijak bernama Kavya Ushanas dan belum dikaitkan dengan Venus. Teks Sanskerta kemudian menyamakan Ushanas, Kavya, Shukra, dan Bhargava sebagai nama tokoh yang sama. Dalam teks kemudian ia disebut putra atau cucu Bhrigu dan putra Kavyamata. Purana belakangan menetapkan perannya sebagai pendeta dan guru para asura.
long_description.en: In the Rigveda he is the wise seer Kavya Ushanas and is not yet associated with Venus. Later Sanskrit texts identify Ushanas, Kavya, Shukra, and Bhargava as names of the same figure. In later texts he is called Bhrigu's son or grandson and Kavyamata's son. Later Puranas establish his role as priest and preceptor of the asuras.

long_description.id: Dalam teks-teks awal ia digambarkan sebagai guru para deva dan para asura, lalu dalam teks yang lebih akhir menjadi purohita (pendeta) para asura saja. Ia dikaitkan dengan Venus dan paling terkenal karena menguasai Mrtasanjivani, keterampilan gaib untuk menghidupkan kembali orang mati. Mahabharata menyebut Ushanas membagi dirinya menjadi dua bagian, satu menjadi sumber pengetahuan bagi para deva dan satu lagi bagi para asura. Dalam Purana, ilmu penghidup itu ia peroleh dari Shiva setelah bertapa. Dalam kisah Vamana, ia mencoba menghalangi aliran air dari kamandalu dengan menutup cerat, lalu Vamana menusuk cerat itu dengan tongkat dan membutakan Shukra.
long_description.en: In earlier texts he is portrayed as teacher of both the devas and the asuras, and in later texts he is established solely as the purohita (priest) of the asuras. He comes to be linked with Venus and is best known for mastering the Mrtasanjivani, a magical skill for restoring the dead to life. The Mahabharata says Ushanas split himself into two halves, one a source of knowledge for the devas and the other for the asuras. In the Puranas he obtains that life-restoring knowledge from Shiva after performing tapas. In the Vamana story he tries to stop the water from flowing out of the kamandalu by blocking its spout, whereupon Vamana pierces the spout with a stick and blinds Shukra.

long_description.id: Pada awal Abad Pertengahan (abad ke-5 sampai ke-12 M), planet Venus dipersonifikasikan sebagai pemuda berkulit putih yang menunggang kuda putih dan memegang kamandalu (bejana air). Bentuk ikonografi ini mungkin atau mungkin tidak sama dengan resi Shukracharya. Sebuah buku pegangan ikonografi menyebut Sukra (Venus) sebagai Brahmana kelahiran Bhrigu dan penduduk asli Bhojakata. Ia disebut duduk di kereta emas yang ditarik delapan kuda atau di kereta perak yang ditarik sepuluh kuda, dan menurut otoritas lain berlengan empat dengan tongkat, tasbih, bejana air, dan sikap varada.
long_description.en: In the early medieval period (5th to 12th century CE), the planet Venus was given a personified form: a young, fair-skinned man on a white horse who holds a kamandalu (water pot). Whether this iconographic form depicts the sage Shukracharya is left open. An iconography handbook describes Sukra (Venus) as a Brahmana born of Bhrigu and a native of Bhojakata. He is also described riding either a golden chariot with eight horses or a silver chariot with ten, and other authorities give him four arms holding the staff, rosary, water-pot and the varada.

literal_meaning.id: Secara harfiah 'jernih' atau 'terang'. Dalam satu kisah, nama itu bermakna "terang" sekaligus "air mani".
literal_meaning.en: Literally 'clear' or 'bright'. In one account the name signifies both "bright" and "semen".

description.id: Keterampilan gaib yang dapat menghidupkan kembali orang mati; dalam Purana ia memperolehnya dari Shiva dan memakainya untuk memulihkan nyawa para asura.
description.en: A magical skill that can bring the dead back to life; in the Puranas he receives it from Shiva and uses it to restore life to the asuras.

description.id: Ushanas dicatat sebagai yogi termasyhur yang memiliki kekuatan gaib luar biasa (siddhi).
description.en: Ushanas is noted as a renowned yogi endowed with extraordinary magical powers (siddhi).

role.en: Guru of the asuras who realises Vamana's identity.

summary.en: Shukra realised who Vamana really was and tried to dam the water from the kamandalu by plugging its spout; Vamana pierced the spout with a stick and blinded Shukra.

title.id: Ushanas dan Kubera dalam Shanti Parva
title.en: Ushanas and Kubera in the Shanti Parva

role.id: Yogi yang memasuki Kubera dan kemudian ditelan Shiva.
role.en: Yogi who enters Kubera and is later swallowed by Shiva.

summary.id: Menurut Shanti Parva dalam Mahabharata, Ushanas memakai kekuatan yogiknya untuk memasuki Kubera dan merampas kekayaan serta kebebasannya. Shiva kemudian membengkokkan trisula, lahirlah busurnya Pinaka, dan ia menelan Ushanas; Ushanas pun kemudian dikenal sebagai Shukra.
summary.en: According to the Shanti Parva of the Mahabharata, Ushanas used his yogic powers to enter Kubera and deprive him of wealth and freedom. Shiva then bent the trident, giving rise to his bow Pinaka, and swallowed Ushanas; Ushanas came to be known as Shukra.

description.id: Dalam Rigveda, Kavya Ushanas tampil sebagai pendeta-penyair bijak yang berhubungan dengan para dewa, terutama Indra.
description.en: In the Rigveda, Kavya Ushanas appears as a wise poet-priest associated with the gods, especially Indra.

note.en: In the Rigveda, Kavya Ushanas is associated with Indra, and some hymns credit him with fashioning Indra's vajra.

short_description.id: Shunfeng'er adalah dewa laut dan pintu Tiongkok yang menjaga kuil Mazu bersama Qianliyan.
short_description.en: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god guarding Mazu temples with Qianliyan.

long_description.id: Shunfeng'er adalah dewa laut dan pintu Tiongkok yang menjaga kuil Mazu bersama Qianliyan. Namanya mengacu pada kemampuan mendengar suara yang dibawa angin. Ia juga disebut 水精將軍 dan, dalam arak-arakan, tampil sebagai salah satu dari dua jenderal pelindung kiri dan kanan Mazu.
long_description.en: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god guarding Mazu temples with Qianliyan. His name refers to hearing sounds carried by the wind. He is also called 水精將軍 and, in processions, appears as one of the two generals protecting Mazu on her left and right.

long_description.id: Shunfeng Er dan Shen Feng Er merupakan ejaan lain namanya. Pada zaman Ming, ia juga dikenal sebagai Shi Kuang. Journey to the West menampilkannya sebagai personifikasi telinga Kaisar Giok. Pendengarannya dipakai membantu pelaut membedakan angin baik dari badai, dan dalam sebagian kisah ia dipuja sebagai saksi sumpah dan kontrak.
long_description.en: Shunfeng Er and Shen Feng Er are alternative spellings of his name. In the Ming period, he was also known as Shi Kuang. Journey to the West presents him as the personified ears of the Jade Emperor. His hearing is used to help sailors tell favorable winds from storms, and in some accounts he is worshipped as a witness to oaths and contracts.

long_description.id: Ia paling sering digambarkan sebagai iblis yang dikalahkan dan dijinakkan oleh Mazu. Menurut satu kisah, selendang sakti Mazu meniupkan pasir ke telinga dan mata mereka; menurut kisah lain, ia dan Qianliyan adalah saudara Gao Jue dan Gao Ming yang menghantui Gunung Peach Blossom; dan sebuah arsip budaya menyebut keduanya semula siluman di gunung itu yang ditaklukkan Mazu. Dalam seni ia biasanya digambarkan berkulit merah atau cokelat dengan tangan di telinga, dan 順風耳 di kuil Mazu memegang senjata di tangan yang lain.
long_description.en: He is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed by Mazu. By one account, Mazu's magical scarf blew sand into their ears and eyes; by another, he and Qianliyan were the brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming who haunted Peach Blossom Mountain; and a cultural archive says the two were originally spirit-monsters on that mountain subdued by Mazu. In art he typically appears red- or brown-skinned with a hand at his ear, and in Mazu temples 順風耳 holds a weapon in his other hand.

long_description.id: Sebuah teks klasik menyebut kedua makhluk itu semula roh persik dan hantu willow dari Gunung Qipan yang meminjam daya gaib utusan tanah liat di kuil Xuanyuan; telinganya dapat mendengar seribu li tetapi tidak lebih jauh, dan daya itu dapat diputus dengan menghancurkan tubuh tanah liatnya serta akar persik dan willow.
long_description.en: A classical text says the two beings were originally the peach spirit and willow ghost of Mount Qipan who borrowed the power of clay attendants in the Xuanyuan temple; the ears can hear a thousand li but no farther, and the power can be cut by destroying the clay bodies and the peach and willow roots.

description.id: Mampu mendengar suara yang dibawa angin dan, dalam sebagian kisah, segala sesuatu di dunia sepelan apa pun.
description.en: Able to hear any sound carried on the wind and, in some accounts, everything in the world however quietly spoken.

description.id: Pendengarannya dipakai untuk membantu pelaut membedakan angin yang baik dari badai.
description.en: His hearing is used to help sailors tell favorable winds from storms.

description.id: Menurut satu kisah, selendang sakti Mazu meniupkan awan pasir ke telinga dan mata mereka sehingga mereka kalah.
description.en: By one account, Mazu's magical scarf blew clouds of sand into their ears and eyes and defeated them.

name.id: Tubuh tanah liat dan akar persik-willow

description.id: Dalam teks klasik, daya gaib mereka dikatakan bergantung pada tubuh tanah liat di kuil dan akar persik serta willow, yang dapat dihancurkan untuk memutusnya.
description.en: In the classical text their spiritual power is said to rest on the clay bodies in the temple and on peach and willow roots, which can be destroyed to cut it.

sources.title: 千里眼、順風耳 - 國家文化記憶庫
sources.author: 王立宜
sources.publisher: 國家文化記憶庫 (National Cultural Memory Bank, Taiwan)

claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god. He usually appears with Qianliyan as a guardian of the temples of the sea goddess Mazu.

statement.id: Shunfeng'er adalah dewa laut dan pintu Tiongkok yang menjaga kuil Mazu bersama Qianliyan.
statement.en: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god guarding Mazu temples with Qianliyan.

claims.quote: The name "Shunfeng'er" literally means "Wind Accompanying Ears" in reference to his ability to hear any sound carried upon the wind.

statement.id: Namanya mengacu pada kemampuan mendengar suara yang dibawa angin.
statement.en: His name refers to hearing sounds carried by the wind.

claims.quote: It also appears as Shunfeng Er and Shen Feng Er. His partner Qianliyan's name similarly means "Sharp-Eyed" or "All-Seeing".

statement.id: Shunfeng Er dan Shen Feng Er merupakan ejaan lain namanya.
statement.en: Shunfeng Er and Shen Feng Er are alternative spellings of his name.

claims.quote: Under the Ming, Shunfeng'er was also known as Shi Kuang. He is also sometimes known as Wanli'er, which has similar meaning, as the Chinese word wàn—like the English "myriad"—simultaneously means the number 10,000 and "innumerable" or "uncountably vast".

statement.id: Pada zaman Ming, ia juga dikenal sebagai Shi Kuang.
statement.en: In the Ming period, he was also known as Shi Kuang.

claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is first attested in the early-16th century novel Journey to the West, where he appears as the personified form of the Taoist Jade Emperor's ears and one of his lieutenants. There is, however, an earlier depiction of him in a Sichuan cave which has been dated to the Southern Song.

statement.id: Journey to the West menampilkannya sebagai personifikasi telinga Kaisar Giok.
statement.en: Journey to the West presents him as the personified ears of the Jade Emperor.

claims.quote: Shunfeng'er's sharp hearing is employed to help sailors distinguish favorable winds from coming storms. In some accounts, he is capable of hearing everything in the world, no matter how quietly spoken, and was therefore also worshipped as a witness and guarantor of oaths and contracts.

statement.id: Pendengaran Shunfeng'er yang tajam dipakai untuk membantu pelaut membedakan angin yang baik dari badai yang akan datang; dalam sebagian kisah ia mampu mendengar segalanya di dunia, sepelan apa pun, sehingga juga dipuja sebagai saksi dan penjamin sumpah dan kontrak.
statement.en: Shunfeng'er's sharp hearing is used to help sailors tell favorable winds from coming storms; in some accounts he can hear everything in the world however quietly spoken, and was therefore also worshipped as a witness and guarantor of oaths and contracts.

claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed or befriended by the sea goddess Mazu.

statement.id: Shunfeng'er paling sering digambarkan sebagai iblis yang dikalahkan dan dijinakkan atau diajak berteman oleh dewi laut Mazu.
statement.en: Shunfeng'er is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed or befriended by the sea goddess Mazu.

claims.quote: By one account, he and Qianliyan appeared off Meizhou Island during a storm and were defeated by Mazu's magical silk scarf, which blew clouds of sand into their ears and eyes. After their submission, they pledged their loyalty when she kindly healed them of the damage she had caused them.

statement.id: Menurut satu kisah, ia dan Qianliyan muncul di lepas pantai Pulau Meizhou saat badai dan dikalahkan oleh selendang sutra sakti Mazu yang meniupkan awan pasir ke telinga dan mata mereka; setelah tunduk, mereka berjanji setia ketika Mazu menyembuhkan luka yang ditimbulkannya.
statement.en: By one account, he and Qianliyan appeared off Meizhou Island during a storm and were defeated by Mazu's magical silk scarf, which blew clouds of sand into their ears and eyes; after submitting they pledged loyalty when she healed the damage she had caused.

claims.quote: In another, the two were the brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming. Ruthless generals, they fell at Peach Blossom Mountain and subsequently haunted it as demons.

statement.id: Dalam kisah lain, keduanya adalah saudara Gao Jue dan Gao Ming, jenderal kejam yang gugur di Gunung Peach Blossom dan kemudian menghantuinya sebagai iblis.
statement.en: In another account the two were the brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming, ruthless generals who fell at Peach Blossom Mountain and subsequently haunted it as demons.

claims.quote: Shunfeng'er typically appears as a red- or brown-skinned demon cupping a hand to one of his ears. He also occasionally appears with three heads and six arms.

statement.id: Shunfeng'er biasanya digambarkan sebagai iblis berkulit merah atau cokelat yang menangkupkan tangan ke salah satu telinganya, dan kadang-kadang bertiga kepala dan berlengan enam.
statement.en: Shunfeng'er typically appears as a red- or brown-skinned demon cupping a hand to one of his ears, and occasionally with three heads and six arms.

claims.quote: 在民間的神話傳說中，替媽祖察聽世情的兩大駕前護衛神分別為千里眼（又稱金精將軍）與順風耳（又稱水精將軍）。

statement.id: Dalam mitos rakyat, dua dewa pengawal yang mengawasi dan mendengar urusan dunia bagi Mazu (媽祖) adalah 千里眼 (juga disebut 金精將軍) dan 順風耳 (juga disebut 水精將軍).
statement.en: In folk myth, the two guardian gods who observe and listen to the affairs of the world for Mazu (媽祖) are 千里眼 (also called 金精將軍) and 順風耳 (also called 水精將軍).

claims.quote: 在媽祖廟裡，千里眼和順風耳分別站立於媽祖的左右兩側 ... 而順風耳則手舉至側耳做聽音狀的姿態，以其無遠弗屆的聽力，為媽祖偵聽世上的一切事物。祂們的另一手則持有兵器。

statement.id: Di kuil Mazu (媽祖), 千里眼 dan 順風耳 berdiri di kiri dan kanan Mazu; 順風耳 mengangkat tangan ke samping telinga dalam sikap mendengar, memakai pendengarannya yang tak terbatas untuk menyelidiki segala hal di dunia bagi Mazu, dan tangan yang lain memegang senjata.
statement.en: In Mazu (媽祖) temples, 千里眼 and 順風耳 stand on Mazu's left and right; 順風耳 raises a hand to his ear in a listening pose, using his boundless hearing to scout everything in the world for Mazu, and the other hand holds a weapon.

claims.quote: 關於千里眼和順風耳的傳說不一，總的來說，祂們原來是在桃花山上的妖精，不僅面貌猙獰，使居民恐懼外，更時常擾亂地方、為害百姓。最後為媽祖收伏，成為隨駕將軍。

statement.id: Legenda tentang 千里眼 dan 順風耳 berbeda-beda, tetapi pada umumnya keduanya semula adalah siluman di Gunung Peach Blossom (桃花山) yang berwajah garang, menakuti penduduk, dan sering mengganggu daerah itu serta merugikan rakyat, hingga akhirnya ditaklukkan Mazu (媽祖) dan menjadi jenderal pengiringnya.
statement.en: Legends about 千里眼 and 順風耳 differ, but generally they were originally spirit-monsters on Peach Blossom Mountain (桃花山) with fierce faces who frightened residents and often disturbed the area and harmed the people, until Mazu (媽祖) subdued them and they became her attendant generals.

claims.quote: 在媽祖出巡的陣頭中，除了媽祖鑾轎外，我們總會看見一綠一紅的大將軍，這就是媽祖的左右護法──千里眼和順風耳。

statement.id: Dalam arak-arakan Mazu (媽祖), selain tandu Mazu selalu tampak dua jenderal besar, satu hijau dan satu merah, yaitu pelindung kiri dan kanan Mazu: 千里眼 dan 順風耳.
statement.en: In Mazu (媽祖) processions, besides Mazu's palanquin one always sees two great generals, one green and one red, who are Mazu's left and right protectors, 千里眼 and 順風耳.

claims.quote: 此業障是棋盤山桃精、柳鬼 ... 今棋盤山有軒轅廟，廟內有泥塑鬼使，名曰千里眼，順風耳；二怪托其靈氣，目能觀看千里，耳能詳聽千里；千里之外，不能視聽也。

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik ini disebut bahwa makhluk jahat itu adalah roh persik dan hantu willow dari Gunung Qipan (棋盤山), dan di kuil Xuanyuan (軒轅廟) di sana ada utusan hantu dari tanah liat bernama 千里眼 dan 順風耳; kedua siluman itu meminjam daya gaibnya sehingga mata dapat melihat seribu li dan telinga dapat mendengar seribu li, tetapi tidak dapat melihat atau mendengar melampaui seribu li.
statement.en: This classical text says the evil creature is the peach spirit and willow ghost of Mount Qipan (棋盤山), and that in the Xuanyuan temple (軒轅廟) there are clay ghost attendants named 千里眼 and 順風耳; the two monsters borrow their spiritual power so that the eyes can see a thousand li and the ears can hear a thousand li, but they cannot see or hear beyond a thousand li.

claims.quote: 你可叫姜子牙著人往棋盤山去，將桃、柳根盤掘挖，用火焚盡；將軒轅廟二鬼泥身打碎，以絕其靈氣之根

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik ini, Jiang Ziya (姜子牙) disarankan mengirim orang ke Gunung Qipan (棋盤山) untuk menggali akar persik dan willow lalu membakarnya, dan menghancurkan tubuh tanah liat kedua hantu di kuil Xuanyuan (軒轅廟) guna memutus akar daya gaib mereka.
statement.en: In this classical text, Jiang Ziya (姜子牙) is advised to send people to Mount Qipan (棋盤山) to dig up and burn the peach and willow roots and to smash the clay bodies of the two ghosts in the Xuanyuan temple (軒轅廟) in order to cut the root of their spiritual power.

summary.id: Saudara Gao Jue dan Gao Ming, jenderal kejam yang gugur di Gunung Peach Blossom.
summary.en: The brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming, ruthless generals who fell at Peach Blossom Mountain.

summary.id: Siluman di Gunung Peach Blossom yang menakuti penduduk.
summary.en: Spirit-monsters on Peach Blossom Mountain who frightened residents.

short_description.id: Shuten-dōji adalah pemimpin oni dalam legenda Jepang yang bersarang di Gunung Ōe dan dibunuh Minamoto no Raikō setelah dibuat mabuk dengan sake pemberian dewa.
short_description.en: Shuten-dōji is an oni leader in Japanese legend who dwelt on Mount Ōe and was killed by Minamoto no Raikō after being made drunk with sake given by a deity.

long_description.id: Shuten-dōji adalah pemimpin oni dalam legenda Jepang yang dibunuh Minamoto no Raikō. Kamus Daijisen menyebutnya pemimpin oni legendaris yang tinggal di Ōeyama dan merampas perempuan serta harta di ibu kota sehingga diburu atas titah kaisar. Dalam versi tertua, banyak orang hilang di Kyoto, terutama perempuan muda.
long_description.en: Shuten-dōji is an oni leader in Japanese legend, killed by Minamoto no Raikō. The Daijisen dictionary calls him a legendary oni leader living on Ōeyama who plundered women and treasure in the capital and was hunted under imperial command. In the oldest version, many people go missing in Kyoto, most of them young women.

long_description.id: Menurut versi Ōeyama Ekotoba, saat tidur ia kembali ke wujud aslinya yang setinggi 50 kaki, bertubuh merah, berkepala bertanduk lima, dan bermata lima belas. Dalam versi tertua itu, Raikō menawarkan sake pemberian salah satu dewa sehingga ia tak berdaya; dalam versi Otogi-zōshi, sake dan helm diberikan oleh tiga dewa yang menjelma sebagai orang tua. Salah satu kisah menyebut kepalanya yang terpenggal masih menggigit Raikō.
long_description.en: According to the Ōeyama Ekotoba version, when asleep he returned to his true form, 50 feet tall, with a red body, a five-horned head and fifteen eyes. In that oldest version Raikō offers sake given by one of the deities, which leaves him incapacitated; in the Otogi-zōshi version the sake and a helmet are given by three gods who appear as old men. One story says his severed head still bit at Raikō.

long_description.id: Sarangnya ditempatkan di Gunung Ōe atau Gunung Ibuki, tergantung versi. Ensiklopedia Heibonsha mencatat bahwa Ōeyama semula tampaknya Oi-no-saka dekat ibu kota, dan menafsirkan gagasan oni yang bersembunyi di sana dengan latar tempat itu sebagai batas antara ibu kota dan dunia luar. Nama Shuten-dōji menurut Ōeyama Ekotoba berasal dari kegemarannya pada sake.
long_description.en: His lair is placed on Mount Ōe or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version. The Heibonsha encyclopedia notes that Ōeyama was apparently originally Oi-no-saka near the capital, and interprets the idea of an oni holed up there against the background of that place being a boundary between the capital and the outside world. According to the Ōeyama Ekotoba his name comes from his love of sake.

long_description.id: Teks tertua legenda ini, Ōeyama Ekotoba dari abad ke-14, adalah gulungan bergambar yang disimpan di Itsuō Art Museum.
long_description.en: The oldest text of the legend, the fourteenth-century Ōeyama Ekotoba, is a picture scroll held by the Itsuō Art Museum.

literal_meaning.id: "anak laki-laki peminum sake"; dalam Ōeyama Ekotoba, nama ini berarti orang yang sangat menyukai sake
literal_meaning.en: "sake-drinking lad"; in the Ōeyama Ekotoba the name refers to someone who deeply loves sake

description.id: Dalam versi tertua, sake pemberian salah satu dewa yang ditawarkan Raikō membuat Shuten-dōji tak berdaya; dalam versi Otogi-zōshi, Raikō menerima sake jinben kidoku dan helm bintang dari para dewa.
description.en: In the oldest version the sake given by a deity and offered by Raikō leaves Shuten-dōji incapacitated; in the Otogi-zōshi version Raikō receives the Jinben kidoku sake and a star helmet from the gods.

role.id: Pemimpin oni yang menculik orang di ibu kota dan akhirnya dipenggal Raikō.
role.en: The oni leader behind the abductions in the capital, who is finally beheaded by Raikō.

summary.id: Dalam versi tertua, banyak orang, terutama perempuan muda, hilang di Kyoto. Raikō menawarkan sake pemberian dewa kepada Shuten-dōji hingga ia tak berdaya, lalu memenggalnya; kepala yang terpenggal masih menggigit, tetapi Raikō selamat karena memakai beberapa helm.
summary.en: In the oldest version many people, mostly young women, go missing in Kyoto. Raikō offers Shuten-dōji sake given by a deity until he is incapacitated, then beheads him; the severed head still bites, but Raikō survives by wearing several helmets.

role.id: Oni yang dihadapi Raikō dengan bantuan tiga dewa.
role.en: The oni whom Raikō confronts with the help of three gods.

summary.id: Raikō dibantu tiga dewa, yang memberinya sake jinben kidoku dan helm bintang. Kepala Shuten-dōji yang terpenggal melayang ke langit dan mengincar Raikō, tetapi Raikō terlindung helm bintang.
summary.en: Raikō is helped by three gods who give him the Jinben kidoku sake and a star helmet. Shuten-dōji's severed head flies into the sky and aims at Raikō, who is protected by the star helmet.

description.id: Sarang Shuten-dōji di barat laut Kyoto, atau Gunung Ibuki, tergantung versi.
description.en: Shuten-dōji's lair northwest of Kyoto, or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version.

description.id: Menurut Heibonsha, Ōeyama semula tampaknya Oi-no-saka yang dekat ibu kota.
description.en: According to the Heibonsha encyclopedia, Ōeyama was apparently originally Oi-no-saka near the capital.

description.id: Legenda tercatat dalam Ōeyama Ekotoba, gulungan bergambar abad ke-14 yang disimpan di Itsuō Art Museum.
description.en: The legend is recorded in the Ōeyama Ekotoba, a fourteenth-century picture scroll held by the Itsuō Art Museum.

note.id: Menurut legenda, Raikō membunuh Shuten-dōji.
note.en: According to legend, Raikō killed Shuten-dōji.

sources.title: 酒呑童子 (デジタル大辞泉, 精選版 日本国語大辞典, 改訂新版 世界大百科事典)

claims.quote: Shuten-dōji (酒呑童子, also sometimes called 酒顛童子, 酒天童子, or 朱点童子) is a mythical oni or demon leader of Japan, who according to legend was killed by the hero Minamoto no Raikō.

statement.id: Shuten-dōji adalah pemimpin oni yang dibunuh Minamoto no Raikō dalam legenda Jepang.
statement.en: Shuten-dōji is an oni leader killed by Minamoto no Raikō in Japanese legend.

claims.quote: Although decapitated, the demon's detached head still took a bite at the hero, who avoided death by wearing multiple helmets stacked on his head.

statement.id: Salah satu kisah menyebut kepalanya yang terpenggal masih menggigit Raikō.
statement.en: One story says his severed head still bit at Raikō.

claims.quote: Shuten-dōji had his lair at Mount Ōe (大江山) northwest of the city of Kyoto, or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version.

statement.id: Berbagai versi menempatkan sarangnya di Gunung Ōe atau Gunung Ibuki.
statement.en: Accounts place his dwelling on Mount Ōe or Mount Ibuki.

claims.quote: The oldest surviving text of the legend is recorded in the 14th century Ōeyama Ekotoba (大江山絵詞 "Tale of Mount Ōe in Pictures and Words"), a picture scroll held by the Itsuō Art Museum.

statement.id: Naskah Ōeyama Ekotoba dari abad ke-14 menyimpan versi awal legenda itu.
statement.en: The fourteenth-century Ōeyama Ekotoba preserves an early form of the legend.

claims.quote: 丹波の大江山に住んでいたという伝説上の鬼の頭目。都に出ては婦女・財宝を奪ったので、勅命により、源頼光が四天王を率いて退治したという。

statement.id: デジタル大辞泉は、酒呑童子を丹波の大江山に住んだという伝説上の鬼の頭目とし、都で婦女や財宝を奪ったため、勅命により源頼光が四天王を率いて退治したと記す。
statement.en: The Digital Daijisen dictionary describes Shuten-dōji as a legendary leader of the oni said to live on Ōeyama in Tanba, who plundered women and treasure in the capital and was said to have been destroyed by Minamoto no Raikō leading his Four Guardian Kings under imperial command.

claims.quote: 酒呑童子の名称は,《大江山絵詞》では〈酒を深く愛する者〉ゆえの名となっている
claims.locator: 世界大百科事典 (平凡社)

statement.id: 世界大百科事典によれば、『大江山絵詞』では酒呑童子の名は「酒を深く愛する者」であることに由来する。
statement.en: According to the Heibonsha World Encyclopedia, in the Ōeyama Ekotoba the name Shuten-dōji comes from his being someone who deeply loves sake.

claims.quote: 大江山は元来は都のあたりにほど近い老ノ坂であったらしいが,《大江山絵詞》では丹波・丹後の千丈ヶ嶽の大江山,《酒伝童子絵巻》では近江伊吹山となっている。
claims.locator: 世界大百科事典 (平凡社)

statement.id: 世界大百科事典は、大江山はもともと都の近くの老ノ坂だったらしいが、『大江山絵詞』では丹波・丹後の千丈ヶ嶽の大江山、『酒伝童子絵巻』では近江の伊吹山になっていると述べる。
statement.en: The Heibonsha World Encyclopedia says Ōeyama was apparently originally Oi-no-saka near the capital, but is the Ōeyama of Senjōgatake in Tanba and Tango in the Ōeyama Ekotoba and Mount Ibuki in Ōmi in the Shuten-dōji Emaki.

claims.quote: 大江山に鬼神がこもるとする観念は,老ノ坂が都(山城国)と外界を隔てる境界の性格をもった場所であったこと,疫神の侵入をさえぎり都の安寧と清浄を確保する四境祭の舞台であったこと,多くの盗賊・強盗が出没し,そのすみかとなったこと,などを背景として分析されるべきであろう。
claims.locator: 世界大百科事典 (平凡社)

statement.id: 世界大百科事典の筆者は、大江山に鬼神がこもるという観念を、老ノ坂が都と外界を隔てる境界であったこと、疫神を防ぐ四境祭の舞台であったこと、盗賊の出没する場所であったことなどを背景に分析すべきだとする。
statement.en: The Heibonsha encyclopedia author says the idea of an oni deity holed up on Ōeyama should be analysed against the background of Oi-no-saka being a boundary between the capital and the outside world, the stage of the Shikyō-sai rite that kept plague deities out, and a haunt of bandits.

claims.quote: 御伽草子。江戸時代に〈御伽文庫〉として刊行された渋川版の一つ。 ... 頼光は2丈ばかりの鬼となって臥している酒呑童子に切りかかり,3神も現じて力を貸す。切られた童子の首は天に舞いあがり頼光をねらうが,頼光は星甲に守られる。
claims.locator: 世界大百科事典 (平凡社), 御伽草子の項

statement.id: 御伽草子の『酒呑童子』では、頼光は二丈ほどの鬼となって伏す酒呑童子に斬りかかり、三神も現れて力を貸す。斬られた首は天に舞い上がって頼光を狙うが、頼光は星甲に守られる。
statement.en: In the Otogi-zōshi Shuten-dōji, Raikō strikes the sleeping Shuten-dōji, who has become an oni about two jō tall, with the three gods appearing to lend their strength; the severed head flies up into the sky and aims at Raikō, who is protected by his star helmet (星甲).

claims.quote: 御伽草子。江戸時代に〈御伽文庫〉として刊行された渋川版の一つ。 ... 三社の神の現じた3人の翁からもてなされ,神便鬼毒(じんべんきどく)酒と星甲(ほしかぶと)とを授けられ
claims.locator: 世界大百科事典 (平凡社), 御伽草子の項

statement.id: 御伽草子の筋では、頼光一行は三社の神が姿を現した三人の翁にもてなされ、神便鬼毒酒と星甲を授けられる。
statement.en: In the Otogi-zōshi plot, Raikō's party is hosted by three old men in whom the gods of three shrines have appeared and is given the Jinben kidoku sake and a hoshi kabuto helmet.

claims.quote: Raikō then offered Shuten-dōji the sake given to him by one of the deities, which rendered him incapacitated.

statement.id: Dalam versi tertua, Raikō menawarkan sake pemberian salah satu dewa kepada Shuten-dōji, yang membuatnya tak berdaya.
statement.en: In the oldest version Raikō offers Shuten-dōji the sake given to him by one of the deities, which renders him incapacitated.

claims.quote: a large number of missing people were being reported in the capital city of Kyoto, most of the victims being young women.

statement.id: Dalam versi tertua, banyak orang dilaporkan hilang di ibu kota Kyoto, kebanyakan korbannya perempuan muda.
statement.en: In the oldest version, many people were reported missing in the capital city of Kyoto, most of the victims being young women.

claims.quote: According to the Ōeyama Ekotoba version, Shuten-dōji returned to his true form when he slept. He was 50 feet in height, had a red body and a five-horned head, with fifteen eyes

statement.id: Menurut versi Ōeyama Ekotoba, Shuten-dōji kembali ke wujud aslinya saat tidur: setinggi 50 kaki, bertubuh merah, berkepala bertanduk lima, dan bermata lima belas.
statement.en: According to the Ōeyama Ekotoba version, Shuten-dōji returned to his true form when he slept: 50 feet tall, with a red body and a five-horned head with fifteen eyes.

claims.quote: The oldest text (Ōeyama Ekotoba or Ōeyama Emaki) version the legend can be summarized as follows: During the reign of Emperor Ichijō (r. 986-1011)

statement.id: Wikipedia meringkas versi teks tertua (Ōeyama Ekotoba atau Ōeyama Emaki) sebagai kisah pada masa pemerintahan Kaisar Ichijō (986–1011).
statement.en: Wikipedia summarises the oldest text version (Ōeyama Ekotoba or Ōeyama Emaki) as a story set in the reign of Emperor Ichijō (r. 986-1011).

summary.id: Wikipedia: Gunung Ōe di barat laut Kyoto atau Gunung Ibuki, tergantung versi.
summary.en: Wikipedia: Mount Ōe northwest of Kyoto or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version.

summary.id: Ensiklopedia Heibonsha: semula tampaknya Oi-no-saka; Ōeyama di Tanba/Tango dalam Ōeyama Ekotoba, dan Gunung Ibuki di Ōmi dalam Shuten-dōji Emaki.
summary.en: Heibonsha encyclopedia: apparently originally Oi-no-saka; Ōeyama in Tanba/Tango in the Ōeyama Ekotoba and Mount Ibuki in Ōmi in the Shuten-dōji Emaki.

short_description.id: Sihuhata adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Lanna Thailand utara, biasanya memiliki empat telinga dan lima mata.
short_description.en: Sihuhata is a creature of Northern Thailand's Lanna folklore, usually having four ears and five eyes.

long_description.id: Sihuhata adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Lanna Thailand utara, biasanya memiliki empat telinga dan lima mata. Satu versi naskah menggambarkan makhluk mirip beruang yang makan arang menyala dan menghasilkan kotoran emas.
long_description.en: Sihuhata is a creature of Northern Thailand's Lanna folklore, usually having four ears and five eyes. One manuscript version describes a bearlike creature eating burning charcoal and producing gold as excrement.

long_description.id: Sebagian tradisi menyebutnya sebagai Indra yang menguji kebajikan manusia. Kisahnya disimpan dalam naskah daun lontar Tham Sihuhata dari Wat Chae Chang. Seorang anak menangkap makhluk itu dan membawanya pulang; ia menolak rumput dan daun. Emas itu memungkinkan anak tersebut membangun saluran air emas dan menikahi putri raja.
long_description.en: Some traditions identify it as Indra testing a person's virtue. Its story is preserved in the palm-leaf manuscript Tham Sihuhata from Wat Chae Chang. A boy catches the creature and brings it home; it refuses grass and leaves. The gold enables the boy to build a golden water channel and marry the king's daughter.

long_description.id: Dalam penceritaan ulang legenda di sebuah artikel jurnal, seorang anak laki-laki menangkap hewan aneh seperti beruang berbulu hitam dengan empat telinga dan lima mata. Keesokan harinya ia mendapati hewan itu telah mencerna bara menjadi emas. Dengan bantuan Indra, ia membangun talang air emas dan menikahi sang putri, sedangkan raja yang meminta makhluk itu dibawa kepadanya mendapati makhluk itu lari ketakutan.
long_description.en: In the legend as retold in a journal article, a boy catches a strange animal like a bear, with black hair, four ears and five eyes. The next day he finds the animal has digested the coals into gold. With the help of Indra he builds the gold water gutter and marries the princess, while the king who asks for the creature to be brought finds that it is frightened and runs away.

short_description.id: Kura-kura roh (靈龜) adalah kura-kura dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang menyebar ke budaya Asia Timur, melambangkan umur panjang dan dianggap pemimpin makhluk bercangkang.
short_description.en: The spirit turtle (靈龜) is a turtle of Chinese mythology that spread across East Asian culture, representing longevity and regarded as chief of shelled creatures.

long_description.id: Kura-kura roh adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang menyebar bersama lingkup budaya Asia Timur. Ia melambangkan umur panjang dalam tradisi Asia Timur dan dianggap pemimpin makhluk bercangkang. Istilah ini juga dipakai untuk cangkang kura-kura yang dipakai dalam ramalan tradisional.
long_description.en: The spirit turtle is a creature of Chinese mythology that spread with the East Asian cultural sphere. It represents longevity in East Asian traditions and is regarded as chief of shelled creatures. The term is also used for turtle shells used in traditional divination.

long_description.id: Ia termasuk dalam Empat Hewan Cerdas, daftar hewan pertanda baik. Teks klasik Liji menyebut kura-kura bersama qilin, burung hong, dan naga sebagai empat roh, dan sebuah ensiklopedia sejarah menulis bahwa kura-kura melambangkan umur panjang dan kestabilan. Erya memuat entri untuk "kura-kura ilahi" dan "kura-kura roh".
long_description.en: It belongs to the Four Intelligent Beasts, a list of auspicious animals. The classical Liji names the turtle with the qilin, phoenix and dragon as the four spirits, and a history encyclopedia writes that the tortoise symbolizes longevity and stability. The Erya has entries for the "divine turtle" and the "spirit turtle".

long_description.id: Shuyiji menyebut kura-kura yang berusia lebih dari sepuluh ribu tahun sebagai kura-kura roh. Baopuzi justru menggambarkan kura-kura roh berusia seribu tahun dan berlima warna yang mewakili lima unsur.
long_description.en: The Shuyiji calls a turtle older than ten thousand years a spirit turtle. The Baopuzi instead describes a thousand-year-old spirit turtle with five colors representing the five elements.

long_description.id: Di Jepang makhluk ini dikenal sebagai Reiki, muncul dalam kōan Zenrin-kushū, dan menjadi motif umum di kuil Shintō dan Buddha; gelar sangō "Reigizan" dipakai beberapa kuil. Konon Kuil Kameoka Hachimangū di Sendai dinamai karena kura-kura roh muncul saat kuil dibangun. Di Korea ia dikenal sebagai Yeonggwi.
long_description.en: In Japan the creature is known as Reiki, features in a kōan of the Zenrin-kushū, and is a common motif at Shintō shrines and Buddhist temples; the sangō title "Reigizan" belongs to several temples. The Kameoka Hachimangū shrine in Sendai is said to be so named because a spirit turtle appeared when it was built. In Korea it is known as Yeonggwi.

cultural_context.id: Kura-kura roh melambangkan umur panjang dalam budaya Asia Timur, dan kura-kura secara umum dikaitkan dengan umur panjang dan kestabilan sebagai salah satu Empat Hewan Pertanda Baik.
cultural_context.en: The spirit turtle represents longevity in East Asian cultures, and the tortoise in general is associated with longevity and stability as one of the Four Auspicious Beasts.

learning_questions.en: Why is the turtle often chosen as a symbol of longevity in many cultures?

claims.quote: The spirit turtle (Chinese: 靈龜) or spirit tortoise is a turtle originated from Chinese mythology and spread with East Asian cultural sphere.

statement.id: Kura-kura roh adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
statement.en: The spirit turtle is a creature of Chinese mythology.

claims.quote: It is believed by East Asian cultures, like other turtles in mythology, to represent longevity (壽命).

statement.id: Ia melambangkan umur panjang dalam tradisi Asia Timur.
statement.en: It represents longevity in East Asian traditions.

claims.quote: It is said to be chief among all shelled creatures.

statement.id: Ia dianggap sebagai pemimpin makhluk bercangkang.
statement.en: It is regarded as chief of shelled creatures.

claims.quote: Among the Four Intelligent Beasts (四靈), a list of auspicious animals, the turtle goes by several names.

statement.id: Ia termasuk dalam Empat Hewan Cerdas.
statement.en: It belongs to the Four Intelligent Beasts.

claims.quote: According to the Shuyiji (述異記 Tales of Strange Matters) compiled by Ren Fang, a turtle that has lived for one thousand years has grown hair, a five thousand year old tortoise is called a "divine turtle" (神龜) and an animal older than ten thousand years is called a "spiritual turtle" (靈龜).

statement.id: Shuyiji menyebut kura-kura yang berusia lebih dari sepuluh ribu tahun sebagai kura-kura roh.
statement.en: The Shuyiji calls a turtle older than ten thousand years spiritual.

claims.quote: The Baopuzi gives a slightly different account, describing the spirit turtle as one thousand years old.

statement.id: Baopuzi justru menggambarkan kura-kura roh berusia seribu tahun.
statement.en: The Baopuzi instead describes a thousand-year-old spirit turtle.

claims.quote: 何謂四靈?麟、鳳、龜、龍,謂之四靈。故龍以爲畜,故魚鮪不淰;鳳以爲畜,故鳥不獝;麟以爲畜,故獸不狘;龜以爲畜,故人情不失。

statement.id: Teks klasik Liji bertanya "apa itu empat roh?" dan menjawab bahwa qilin (lin), burung hong (feng), kura-kura (gui), dan naga (long) disebut empat roh (siling); dengan kura-kura sebagai salah satunya, "perasaan manusia tidak hilang".
statement.en: The Liji asks "what are the four spirits?" and answers that the qilin (lin), phoenix (feng), turtle (gui) and dragon (long) are called the four spirits (siling); with the turtle among them, "human feelings are not lost".

claims.quote: In the classic The Book of Rites (also known as the Liji, date uncertain), the qilin is listed as one of the four intelligent creatures along with the phoenix, dragon, and tortoise, often referred to as the Four Auspicious Beasts.
claims.locator: Section: The Qilin in Classical Texts

statement.id: Dalam kitab klasik Book of Rites (Liji), qilin disebut sebagai salah satu dari empat makhluk cerdas bersama burung hong, naga, dan kura-kura, yang sering disebut Empat Hewan Pertanda Baik.
statement.en: In the classic Book of Rites (Liji), the qilin is listed as one of four intelligent creatures along with the phoenix, dragon and tortoise, often called the Four Auspicious Beasts.

claims.quote: Broadly, the dragon symbolizes power and strength, the phoenix renewal and grace, the tortoise longevity and stability, and the qilin prosperity and righteousness.
claims.locator: Section: The Qilin in Classical Texts

statement.id: Secara umum, naga melambangkan kekuatan, burung hong pembaruan dan keanggunan, kura-kura umur panjang dan kestabilan, dan qilin kemakmuran dan kebenaran.
statement.en: Broadly, the dragon symbolizes power and strength, the phoenix renewal and grace, the tortoise longevity and stability, and the qilin prosperity and righteousness.

claims.quote: The latter is sometimes understood as being synonymous with "divine turtle" (神龜 shénguī) although distinctions are made. The term is also used in reference to the turtle shells used in traditional divination.

statement.id: Istilah kura-kura roh kadang dianggap sinonim "kura-kura ilahi" meski ada pembedaan, dan juga dipakai untuk cangkang kura-kura yang dipakai dalam ramalan tradisional.
statement.en: The term spirit turtle is sometimes understood as synonymous with "divine turtle" although distinctions are made, and is also used for the turtle shells used in traditional divination.

claims.quote: The Erya  provides entries on the terms "divine turtle" (神龜) and "spirit turtle" (靈龜). The former term includes an annotation which simply reads "the most sacred of turtles" (亀之最神明).

statement.id: Erya memuat entri untuk istilah "kura-kura ilahi" dan "kura-kura roh"; keterangan istilah pertama berbunyi "yang paling suci di antara kura-kura".
statement.en: The Erya provides entries on the terms "divine turtle" and "spirit turtle"; the annotation to the former simply reads "the most sacred of turtles".

claims.quote: The Baopuzi gives a slightly different account, describing the spirit turtle as one thousand years old. ... The text continues to describe the turtle as having five colors: blue, red, yellow, white, and black; together representing the five elements.

statement.id: Baopuzi menggambarkan kura-kura roh berusia seribu tahun dan berlanjut menyebut kura-kura itu berlima warna, biru, merah, kuning, putih, dan hitam, yang bersama-sama mewakili lima unsur.
statement.en: The Baopuzi describes the spirit turtle as one thousand years old and goes on to describe the turtle as having five colors, blue, red, yellow, white and black, together representing the five elements.

claims.quote: In Japanese mythology, the creature is identified as the Reiki (霊亀 "spirit turtle").

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Jepang, makhluk ini dikenal sebagai Reiki ("kura-kura roh").
statement.en: In Japanese mythology the creature is identified as the Reiki ("spirit turtle").

claims.quote: The spirit turtle is an endemic motif at Shintō shrines and Buddhist temples in Japan. The sangō title "Reigizan" (霊亀山 "Spirit Turtle Mountain") belongs to several temples across the country, including Tenryū-ji and Rinsen-ji in Kyōto, Hontoku-ji in Himeji, Daichō-ji in Uwajima, and others.

statement.id: Kura-kura roh adalah motif yang umum di kuil Shintō dan kuil Buddha di Jepang; gelar sangō "Reigizan" ("Gunung Kura-kura Roh") dipakai beberapa kuil, termasuk Tenryū-ji dan Rinsen-ji di Kyōto.
statement.en: The spirit turtle is an endemic motif at Shintō shrines and Buddhist temples in Japan; the sangō title "Reigizan" ("Spirit Turtle Mountain") belongs to several temples, including Tenryū-ji and Rinsen-ji in Kyōto.

claims.quote: It is said the Kameoka Hachimangū shrine in Sendai is so-called because a spirit turtle appeared at the time of its construction. Stone statues of the creature can be found at Zenyōmitsu-ji and Kameoka Hachimangū in Mashiko, Tochigi.

statement.id: Konon Kuil Kameoka Hachimangū di Sendai dinamai demikian karena seekor kura-kura roh muncul saat kuil itu dibangun; patung batu makhluk ini terdapat di Zenyōmitsu-ji dan Kameoka Hachimangū di Mashiko, Tochigi.
statement.en: It is said the Kameoka Hachimangū shrine in Sendai is so named because a spirit turtle appeared when it was built; stone statues of the creature are found at Zenyōmitsu-ji and at Kameoka Hachimangū in Mashiko, Tochigi.

claims.quote: Reiki is also the name of the first era of the Nara period.

statement.id: Reiki juga nama era pertama zaman Nara.
statement.en: Reiki is also the name of the first era of the Nara period.

claims.quote: The Zenrin-kushū provides a kōan that reads Reiki o o hiku (靈龜曵尾 "The spirit turtle sweeps its tail"). It is described as a variant of the phrase Ato o haratte ato shōzu (拂跡跡生 "Erasing traces creates traces").

statement.id: Zenrin-kushū memuat kōan berbunyi Reiki o o hiku ("Kura-kura roh menyapu ekornya"), yang dikatakan varian ungkapan "Menghapus jejak menciptakan jejak".
statement.en: The Zenrin-kushū provides a kōan reading Reiki o o hiku ("The spirit turtle sweeps its tail"), described as a variant of the phrase "Erasing traces creates traces".

claims.quote: In Korean mythology, it is known as Yeonggwi (Korean: 영귀; Hanja: 靈龜).

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Korea, makhluk ini dikenal sebagai Yeonggwi.
statement.en: In Korean mythology it is known as Yeonggwi.

short_description.id: Suijin atau Mizugami adalah nama umum untuk dewa air dalam mitologi Jepang, pelindung air tawar, nelayan, dan petani sawah, yang dipuja di kuil dan di tepi mata air.
short_description.en: Suijin, also called Mizugami, is the umbrella name for the Japanese water deity, a protector of fresh water, fishermen and rice farmers who is honoured at shrines and beside springs.

long_description.id: Suijin atau Mizugami ("dewa air") adalah nama umum untuk dewa air dalam mitologi Jepang. Istilah ini merujuk pada perwujudan surgawi dan duniawi dewa air Shinto yang baik hati, terutama air tawar, serta beragam makhluk gaib di danau, kolam, mata air, dan sumur, termasuk ular, naga, belut, ikan, kura-kura, dan kappa pemakan daging. Ia sering dikacaukan dengan Ryūjin dan juga dikenal sebagai Suiten atau Suiō.
long_description.en: Suijin or Mizugami ("water god") serves as the umbrella name for the Japanese water deity in myth. It covers the heavenly and earthly forms of Shinto's kindly water divinity, chiefly of freshwater, as well as many legendary beings living in lakes, ponds, springs and wells, among them serpents, dragons, eels, fish, turtles and the flesh-eating kappa. It is often conflated with Ryūjin and is also known as Suiten or Suiō.

long_description.id: Dewa air Shinto dipercaya sebagai pelindung nelayan serta pelindung kesuburan, keibuan, dan persalinan tanpa rasa sakit. Orang memujanya dengan persembahan demi air yang bersih untuk minum, pertanian, dan sanitasi. Menurut ensiklopedia Jepang, bentuk yang paling khas adalah pelindung petani sawah yang membawa kesuburan dan dipuja di bendungan atau kuil batu di tepi sawah; di sumber air pegunungan ia disamakan dengan dewa gunung.
long_description.en: Believers hold that Shinto's water deity watches over fishermen and over fertility, motherhood and painless childbirth. People worship it with offerings for clean water for drinking, agriculture and sanitation. According to a Japanese encyclopedia, its most typical form is the guardian of rice-paddy farmers that brings fertility and is enshrined at irrigation weirs or stone shrines beside paddies; at mountain water sources it is identified with the mountain deity.

long_description.id: Lambang khas dewa air adalah kappa, dan dewa air dipercaya juga berwujud naga, ular, belut, monyet, atau laba-laba. Dewa air sering digambarkan sebagai dewi, yaitu ibu yang memiliki anak kecil. Suijin juga tampil sebagai lempeng batu atau batu kecil yang ditegakkan di dekat mata air, dan terus dimuliakan serta memengaruhi budaya Jepang.
long_description.en: The typical emblem of the water deity is the kappa, and the water deity is believed also to take the form of a dragon, snake, eel, monkey or spider. The water deity is often represented as a goddess, a mother with a young child. Suijin also appears as a stone plaque or small upright stone near a spring, and continues to be revered and to influence Japanese culture.
