claims.quote: Suijin or Mizugami ... lit. "water god/deity") is a general name for the god of water in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Suijin atau Mizugami ("dewa air") adalah nama umum untuk dewa air dalam mitologi Jepang.
statement.en: Suijin or Mizugami ("water god/deity") is a general name for the god of water in Japanese mythology.

claims.quote: The term refers to the heavenly and earthly manifestations of the benevolent Shinto divinity of water (mainly freshwater), as well as to a wide variety of mythical and magical creatures found in lakes, ponds, springs, and wells, including serpents (snakes, dragons, eels, fish, turtles), and the flesh-eating kappa.

statement.id: Istilah ini merujuk pada perwujudan surgawi dan duniawi dewa air Shinto yang baik hati (terutama air tawar), serta beragam makhluk gaib di danau, kolam, mata air, dan sumur, termasuk ular, naga, belut, ikan, kura-kura, dan kappa pemakan daging.
statement.en: The term refers to the heavenly and earthly manifestations of the benevolent Shinto divinity of water (mainly freshwater) and to many mythical creatures in lakes, ponds, springs and wells, including serpents, dragons, eels, fish, turtles and the flesh-eating kappa.

claims.quote: Mizu-no-kamisama, Mizugami, or Suijin is popularly revered and worshipped in temples and continues to influence Japanese culture.

statement.id: Mizu-no-kamisama, Mizugami, atau Suijin dimuliakan secara populer dan disembah di kuil, serta terus memengaruhi budaya Jepang.
statement.en: Mizu-no-kamisama, Mizugami or Suijin is popularly revered and worshipped in temples and continues to influence Japanese culture.

claims.quote: Other names of Suijin include Suiten ... lit. "water heaven") and Suiō ... lit. "water lord/king").

statement.id: Nama lain Suijin mencakup Suiten ("langit air") dan Suiō ("raja air").
statement.en: Other names of Suijin include Suiten ("water heaven") and Suiō ("water lord/king").

claims.quote: Shrines devoted to the worship of the Water God are called Suitengū Shrines.

statement.id: Kuil yang dipersembahkan bagi dewa air disebut kuil Suitengū.
statement.en: Shrines devoted to the water god are called Suitengū Shrines.

claims.quote: 水神の実態は複雑多様であるが，もっとも典型的なのは農耕社会における水田稲作民にとっての守護神である。水神は豊穣をもたらす神であり，田の神と同一視されている。一般には，水田の用水堰か水田のほとりの石祠に祭られている。また山中の水源地に水分（みくまり）神として祭られる場合は，山の神と同一視される。
claims.locator: Bagian 日本 (世界大百科事典)

statement.id: Wujud dewa air beragam, tetapi yang paling khas adalah pelindung petani sawah; ia dewa yang membawa kesuburan, disamakan dengan dewa sawah, dan dipuja di bendungan atau kuil batu di tepi sawah; bila dipuja di sumber air pegunungan sebagai dewa pembagi air (mikumari), ia disamakan dengan dewa gunung.
statement.en: The water deity takes many forms, but the most typical is the guardian of rice-paddy farmers; it brings fertility, is identified with the rice-field deity, and is enshrined at irrigation weirs or stone shrines beside paddies; when enshrined at mountain water sources as the water-distributing deity (mikumari), it is identified with the mountain deity.

claims.quote: 水神の表徴として代表的なのは河童である。水の妖怪であるが，水神が河童の姿をとったと想像される民間伝承は多い。また水神は，竜やヘビ，ウナギ，サル，クモなどの姿をとると信じられている。
claims.locator: Bagian 日本 (世界大百科事典)

statement.id: Lambang khas dewa air adalah kappa; banyak cerita rakyat membayangkan dewa air berwujud kappa, dan ia dipercaya juga berwujud naga, ular, belut, monyet, atau laba-laba.
statement.en: The typical emblem of the water deity is the kappa; many folk tales imagine the water deity taking kappa form, and it is believed also to take the form of a dragon, snake, eel, monkey or spider.

claims.quote: The Shinto water god is believed to be the guardian of fishermen and the patron saint of fertility, motherhood, and painless childbirth.

statement.id: Dewa air Shinto dipercaya sebagai pelindung nelayan dan pelindung kesuburan, keibuan, dan persalinan tanpa rasa sakit.
statement.en: The Shinto water god is believed to be the guardian of fishermen and the patron of fertility, motherhood and painless childbirth.

claims.quote: People worship Suijin with offerings, believing that doing so will ensure pure and unpolluted water for drinking, agriculture, and sanitation, and will bring success in fishing trips, fertility, motherhood, and easy childbirth.

statement.id: Orang memuja Suijin dengan persembahan, percaya hal itu menjamin air yang bersih untuk minum, pertanian, dan sanitasi, serta membawa keberhasilan melaut, kesuburan, keibuan, dan persalinan mudah.
statement.en: People worship Suijin with offerings, believing this ensures pure and unpolluted water for drinking, agriculture and sanitation and brings success in fishing, fertility, motherhood and easy childbirth.

claims.quote: Suijin is often conflated with Ryūjin, the Japanese dragon god associated with water.

statement.id: Suijin sering dikacaukan dengan Ryūjin, dewa naga Jepang yang terkait dengan air.
statement.en: Suijin is often conflated with Ryūjin, the Japanese dragon god associated with water.

claims.quote: 水神はしばしば女神しかも少童をもつ母神として表現されており，水辺にあって水神に奉仕した巫女の姿を想定する考え方がされている。すなわち水神は，世界的な母子神信仰の問題に関連しているのである。
claims.locator: Bagian 日本 (世界大百科事典)

statement.id: Dewa air sering digambarkan sebagai dewi, yaitu ibu yang memiliki anak kecil; ada pandangan yang membayangkan sosok miko yang melayani dewa air di tepi air, dan dewa air dikaitkan dengan kepercayaan dewa ibu dan anak yang mendunia.
statement.en: The water deity is often represented as a goddess, a mother deity with a young child; one view imagines a shrine maiden serving the water deity by the water, and the water deity is linked to the worldwide belief in mother-and-child deities.

claims.quote: すい‐じん【水神】 水をつかさどる神。飲み水や田の水などを支配する神。水伯。
claims.locator: Entri 水神 (デジタル大辞泉)

statement.id: Kamus Jepang mendefinisikan suijin sebagai dewa yang menguasai air, termasuk air minum dan air sawah; disebut juga suihaku.

short_description.id: Taniwha adalah makhluk gaib besar dalam mitologi Māori yang tinggal di kolam sungai yang dalam, gua gelap, atau laut; ada yang dihormati sebagai kaitiaki (penjaga), ada yang dianggap pemangsa berbahaya.
short_description.en: Taniwha are large supernatural beings in Māori mythology living in deep river pools, dark caves or the sea; some are revered as kaitiaki (guardians), others regarded as dangerous predators.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Māori, taniwha adalah makhluk gaib besar yang tinggal di kolam sungai yang dalam, gua gelap, atau laut, terutama di tempat dengan arus berbahaya atau ombak yang menipu. Mereka dapat dianggap kaitiaki (penjaga pelindung) orang dan tempat yang sangat dihormati, atau dalam beberapa tradisi sebagai pemangsa berbahaya yang, misalnya, menculik perempuan untuk dijadikan istri.
long_description.en: In Māori mythology, taniwha are great supernatural beings dwelling in deep river pools, dark caves or the sea, particularly where currents are dangerous or breakers deceptive. Some regard them as honoured kaitiaki, protectors of people and places, while other traditions see dangerous predators who, for instance, abduct women to be their wives.

long_description.id: Di laut, taniwha sering tampak sebagai paus atau hiu besar; di perairan pedalaman mereka tampak lebih mirip cicak atau tuatara dengan deretan duri di punggung, atau batang kayu apung yang bertingkah mengganggu, dan sebagian dapat menerobos tanah sambil mencabut pohon. Legenda menganggap taniwha tertentu memahat pelabuhan, seperti Te Whanganui-a-Tara di Wellington, serta Danau Waikaremoana, dan menyebabkan tanah longsor di tepi danau atau sungai. Taniwha dapat jantan atau betina; Āraiteuru, misalnya, konon tiba bersama kano-kano pelayaran awal dan putra-putranya menciptakan cabang-cabang Pelabuhan Hokianga.
long_description.en: At sea a taniwha often appears as a whale or large shark; in inland waters they look more like a gecko or tuatara with a row of spines along the back, or like a floating log that behaves disconcertingly, and some can tunnel through the earth uprooting trees. Legends credit certain taniwha with carving harbours, such as Wellington's Te Whanganui-a-Tara, and Lake Waikaremoana, and with causing landslides beside lakes or rivers. Taniwha can be male or female; Āraiteuru, for example, is said to have arrived with the early voyaging canoes and her sons created the branches of the Hokianga Harbour.

long_description.id: Banyak taniwha terkenal tiba dari Hawaiki sebagai penjaga kano leluhur dan, di Aotearoa, melindungi keturunan awak kano itu. Bila dihormati, mereka biasanya bersikap baik: memperingatkan datangnya musuh lewat imam yang menjadi medium dan kadang menyelamatkan orang dari tenggelam. Orang menenangkan mereka dengan persembahan, sering ranting hijau dengan mantra, dan taniwha memastikan larangan tapu dihormati serta pelanggarnya dihukum, terutama terhadap orang dari suku lain.
long_description.en: Many well-known taniwha arrived from Hawaiki as guardians of ancestral canoes and, in Aotearoa, protected the descendants of the canoe crews. When respected they usually acted well: warning of approaching enemies through a priest who was a medium and sometimes saving people from drowning. People placated them with offerings, often a green twig with an incantation, and taniwha made sure the restrictions of tapu were respected and violations punished, especially towards people from other tribes.

long_description.id: Ada banyak legenda pertempuran melawan taniwha; manusia selalu berhasil mengakali dan mengalahkannya. Ketika Hotu-puku di Rotorua dibunuh, perutnya berisi jasad manusia yang belum tercerna; Ngārara Huarau memakan beberapa penduduk desa dan menawan seorang perempuan di gua tepi laut; dan Tāmure dipahami memiliki mere/pounamu ajaib yang berkuasa mengalahkan taniwha. Dua sumber lain juga mencatat taniwha sebagai "monster roh" atau "monster laut" dan sebagai makhluk di gua jeram yang menelan pemberani.
long_description.en: There are many legends of battles with taniwha, and the humans always manage to outwit and defeat them. When Hotu-puku of Rotorua was killed his stomach held undigested human bodies; Ngārara Huarau ate several villagers and captured a woman in a cave by the sea; and Tāmure was understood to have a magical mere/pounamu with power to defeat taniwha. Two other sources also record taniwha as a "spirit monster" or "sea monster" and as a creature in the caves of a rapid that swallowed the brave.

long_description.id: Sebagian orang yang berurusan dengan taniwha dapat menjadi taniwha setelah meninggal, dan kata itu juga dapat menyebut kepala suku dengan nada memuji. Dalam beberapa tahun terakhir, taniwha tampil di berita Selandia Baru karena disebut dalam perkara pengadilan dan perundingan hukum; pada 2002 Ngāti Naho berhasil membuat sebagian State Highway 1 dialihkan demi melindungi tempat tinggal pelindung legendaris mereka, dan Ranginui Walker menyebut taniwha di zaman modern sebagai mekanisme penanggulangan.
long_description.en: A person who had dealings with taniwha might turn into a taniwha after death, and the word can also refer in a complimentary way to chiefs. In recent years taniwha have featured in New Zealand news because they were referenced in court cases and legal negotiations; in 2002 Ngāti Naho ensured part of State Highway 1 was rerouted to protect the abode of their legendary protector, and Ranginui Walker described the taniwha in the modern age as a coping mechanism.

cultural_context.id: Taniwha berfungsi sebagai kaitiaki (penjaga pelindung) orang dan tempat, dan kata itu dapat menyebut kepala suku dengan nada memuji.
cultural_context.en: Taniwha serve as kaitiaki (protective guardians) of people and places, and the word can refer in a complimentary way to chiefs.

short_description.id: Tata Duende, atau El Dueño del Monte, adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Belize dan budaya Maya, dipandang sebagai roh kuat yang melindungi hewan dan hutan. Ia digambarkan tidak berjempol dan berkaki menghadap ke belakang.
short_description.en: Tata Duende, or El Dueño del Monte, is a supernatural being in Belizean folklore and Maya culture, regarded as a powerful spirit that protects animals and the forest. He is described as thumbless with backward-facing feet.

long_description.id: Tata Duende, juga dikenal sebagai El Dueño del Monte, adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat yang paling tampak dalam budaya Kreol. Ia dianggap roh kuat yang melindungi hewan dan hutan. Di kalangan Maya Yukatek di Belize ia dikenal sebagai Nukuch Tat atau Tata Balam, roh penjaga yang baik bagi hutan, hewan, dan manusia. Makhluk ini juga pernah tampil pada perangko Belize dalam seri cerita rakyat Belize.
long_description.en: Tata Duende, also known as El Dueño del Monte, is a supernatural being in folklore most evident in Creole cultures. He is considered a powerful spirit that protects animals and the forest. Among the Yucatec Maya of Belize he is known as Nukuch Tat or Tata Balam, a good guardian spirit of the forest, animals and humans. The creature has also appeared on a postage stamp of Belize in a series on Belizean folklore.

long_description.id: Rupanya digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua kerdil berjanggut, tanpa jempol, berkaki menghadap ke belakang, dan bertopi tinggi. Konon kehadirannya dapat dikenali dari siulan keras yang menyeramkan. Bila bertemu dengannya di hutan, orang harus menyembunyikan ibu jari agar tidak dipatahkan; ia juga dikenal suka mengepang surai kuda dan sering berubah menjadi hewan kecil atau orang yang dikenal.
long_description.en: His appearance is described as a bearded, dwarfed old man with no thumbs, backward-facing feet and a tall hat. His presence is said to be recognizable by a loud, eerie whistle. If you meet him in the forest you must hide your thumbs so he does not break them off; he is also known for braiding horses' manes and for often changing into a small animal or someone you know.

long_description.id: Pandangan tentangnya berbeda. Sebagian orang menyebutnya makhluk menakutkan yang menculik anak dan mencuri jempol mereka, dan ia dipakai untuk menakuti anak agar patuh; yang lain memandangnya entitas spiritual pelindung hutan yang harus dihormati. Seorang penggiat budaya Belize menyatakan bahwa dalam budaya Maya Yukatek ia bukan sosok teror, melainkan pelindung.
long_description.en: Views of him differ. Some call him a fearful creature that kidnaps children and steals their thumbs, and he has been used to scare children into behaving; others see a spiritual entity that protects the forest and deserves respect. A Belizean cultural activist states that in Yucatec Maya culture he is not a terror figure but a protector.

literal_meaning.id: "Tata" (Maya Yukatek) berarti kakek atau tua, dan "duende" (Spanyol) berarti goblin.
literal_meaning.en: "Tata" (Yucatec Maya) means grandfather or old, and "duende" (Spanish) means goblin.

short_description.id: Tezcatlipoca ('Cermin Berasap') adalah dewa penting bangsa Aztec dan Toltec: dewa pencipta dan pelindung prajurit yang membawa kebaikan sekaligus kejahatan, dikaitkan dengan langit malam, badai, obsidian, dan konflik.
short_description.en: Tezcatlipoca ('Smoking Mirror') is an important god of the Aztecs and Toltecs: a creator god and patron of warriors who brings both good and evil, associated with the night sky, hurricanes, obsidian, and conflict.

long_description.id: Tezcatlipoca adalah salah satu dewa terpenting dalam budaya Mesoamerika Pascaklasik, terutama bagi bangsa Toltec dan Aztec. Ia dipandang sebagai dewa pencipta yang tak terlihat dan mahakuasa serta pelindung prajurit, dan sebagai pembawa kebaikan sekaligus kejahatan ia adalah perwujudan perubahan melalui konflik. Ia dikaitkan dengan langit malam, badai topan, obsidian, dan konflik.
long_description.en: Tezcatlipoca was one of the most important gods in Postclassical Mesoamerican culture, particularly for the Toltecs and the Aztecs. He was regarded as an invisible and omnipotent creator god and patron of warriors, and because he brought both good and evil he embodied change through conflict. He is associated with the night sky, hurricanes, obsidian, and conflict.

long_description.id: Ia dianggap salah satu dari empat putra Ometecuhtli dan Omecihuatl, dewa ganda purba, dan dalam mitologi Aztec saudara Quetzalcoatl, Huizilopochtli, dan Xipe Totec. Dalam mitos penciptaan ia menguasai dunia pertama Matahari lalu digulingkan Quetzalcóatl, dan keduanya kemudian bekerja sama menciptakan Matahari ke-5. Nagual atau roh hewannya adalah jaguar, dan ia dikaitkan dengan burung hantu bertanduk dalam kalender.
long_description.en: He was counted among the four sons of Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl, the primordial dual deity, and in Aztec mythology was brother to Quetzalcoatl, Huizilopochtli and Xipe Totec. In the creation myth he ruled the first world of the Sun and was overthrown by Quetzalcóatl, and the two later cooperated to create the 5th Sun. His nagual or animal counterpart was the jaguar, and he is associated with the horned owl in the calendar.

long_description.id: Ia dapat campur tangan langsung dalam urusan manusia untuk membawa kebahagiaan maupun kesedihan, dan dalam wujud yang lebih suram dikenal sebagai penguasa bayang-bayang atau malam, penyihir ilmu hitam, dan pembawa kejahatan, kematian, dan kehancuran. Sebagai pelindung prajurit ia tidak selalu melindungi mereka: kadang ia menunggu di persimpangan jalan tengah malam untuk menantang prajurit yang lengah.
long_description.en: He could step directly into human affairs, bringing joy or grief, and in a darker guise was called lord of the shadows or night, a black-magic sorcerer who brought evil, death and destruction. As patron of warriors he was not always protective of them: sometimes he waited at crossroads at the dead of night to challenge unsuspecting warriors.

long_description.id: Perayaan utamanya adalah Toxcatl yang, seperti kebanyakan perayaan keagamaan Aztec, melibatkan pengorbanan manusia. Seorang peniru sang dewa, paling sering tawanan perang yang paling tampan dan berani, menikahi empat dewi secara simbolis lalu dikorbankan dengan pisau obsidian. Dalam penggambaran yang lebih belakangan ia memiliki cermin obsidian hitam sebagai pengganti kaki kirinya, merujuk pada luka dalam pertempurannya dengan Tlaltecuhtli.
long_description.en: His chief festival was Toxcatl, which, like most Aztec religious festivals, included human sacrifice. An impersonator of the god, most often the best looking and most courageous prisoner of war, symbolically married four goddesses and was then sacrificed with an obsidian knife. In later depictions he has a black obsidian mirror instead of a left foot, referring to a wound in his battle with Tlaltecuhtli.

who.id: Dewa pencipta yang mahakuasa dan pelindung prajurit, pembawa kebaikan dan kejahatan.
who.en: An omnipotent creator god and patron of warriors, bringer of both good and evil.

origin.id: Budaya Mesoamerika Pascaklasik, terutama Toltec dan Aztec.
origin.en: Postclassical Mesoamerican culture, especially the Toltecs and the Aztecs.

role.id: Penguasa dunia pertama Matahari dan, bersama Quetzalcóatl, pencipta Matahari ke-5.
role.en: Ruler of the first world of the Sun and, with Quetzalcóatl, creator of the 5th Sun.

famous_for.id: Julukan 'Cermin Berasap', festival Toxcatl, dan wujud nagual jaguar.
famous_for.en: The epithet 'Smoking Mirror', the Toxcatl festival, and his jaguar nagual.

did_you_know.id: Salah satu benda seni paling terkenal tentang Tezcatlipoca adalah tengkorak berhias mosaik pirus dan lignit hitam yang kini ada di British Museum di London.
did_you_know.en: One of the most famous art objects of Tezcatlipoca is a decorated skull covered in turquoise and black lignite mosaic, now in the British Museum in London.

description.id: Dalam wujud suram ia dikenal sebagai penyihir ilmu hitam dan pembawa kejahatan, kematian, dan kehancuran.
description.en: In a darker guise he was known as a sorcerer of black magic who brought evil, death and destruction.

name.id: Campur tangan langsung dalam urusan manusia

description.id: Sang dewa dapat campur tangan langsung untuk membawa kebahagiaan maupun kesedihan.
description.en: The god could step directly into human affairs to bring joy or grief.

description.id: Kadang ia membawa empat anak panah di tangan kanan, senjata untuk menghukum pelaku kejahatan.
description.en: He sometimes holds four arrows in his right hand, which he uses to punish wrongdoers.

description.id: 'Penyihir Kolibri', dewa Tenochtitlán, dikaitkan dengan matahari dan dewa perang Huitzilopochtli.
description.en: The 'Hummingbird Sorcerer', god of Tenochtitlán, associated with the sun and the war god Huitzilopochtli.

description.id: 'Si Terkuliti', dikaitkan dengan dewa Camaxtli dan Xipe Totec (dewa bangsa Tlaxcaltec).
description.en: The 'Flayed One', linked with the gods Camaxtli and Xipe Totec (the god of the Tlaxcaltecans).

title.en: The origin of the first dogs

role.id: Dewa yang diadukan para bintang dan menghukum pasangan itu.
role.en: The god to whom the stars complained, who punished the couple.

summary.id: Asap api sepasang penyintas banjir mengganggu bintang-bintang; atas keluhan mereka, Tezcatlipoca memenggal kepala pasangan itu dan memasangnya di belakang tubuh mereka, sehingga lahirlah anjing-anjing pertama.
summary.en: The smoke from the fire of a couple who survived the flood disturbed the stars; on their complaint, Tezcatlipoca lopped off the couple's heads and reattached them to their backsides, creating the first dogs.

role.id: Penguasa dunia pertama yang kemudian bekerja sama dengan Quetzalcóatl.
role.en: Ruler of the first world who later cooperated with Quetzalcóatl.

summary.id: Tezcatlipoca menguasai dunia pertama Matahari tetapi digulingkan Quetzalcóatl; keduanya kemudian bekerja sama menciptakan Matahari ke-5 dan memotong-motong monster Tlaltecuhtli.
summary.en: Tezcatlipoca ruled the first world of the Sun but was overthrown by Quetzalcóatl; the two later cooperated to create the 5th Sun and dismembered the monster Tlaltecuhtli.

description.id: Tempat tengkorak berhias mosaik pirus yang menjadi salah satu benda seni paling terkenal tentang Tezcatlipoca.
description.en: Home of the turquoise-mosaic decorated skull, one of the most famous art objects of Tezcatlipoca.

note.id: Tezcatlipoca diyakini putra dewa purba androgini ini.
note.en: Tezcatlipoca was believed to be the son of this primordial androgynous god.

note.id: Saudara Tezcatlipoca; ia menggulingkannya di dunia pertama dan kemudian bekerja sama dengannya menciptakan Matahari ke-5.
note.en: Tezcatlipoca's brother; he overthrew him in the first world and later cooperated with him to create the 5th Sun.

note.id: Saudara Tezcatlipoca dalam mitologi Aztec.
note.en: Tezcatlipoca's brother in Aztec mythology.

note.id: Saudara Tezcatlipoca dalam mitologi Aztec.
note.en: Tezcatlipoca's brother in Aztec mythology.

note.id: Monster yang diserang dan dipotong-potong Tezcatlipoca bersama Quetzalcóatl, dan yang melukainya dalam pertempuran saat Penciptaan.
note.en: The monster Tezcatlipoca attacked and dismembered with Quetzalcóatl, and who wounded him in battle during the Creation.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa sebuah dewa bisa dipuja sekaligus sebagai pembawa kebaikan dan kejahatan?
learning_questions.en: Why could one god be worshipped as a bringer of both good and evil?

sources.title: Tezcatlipoca: The Greatest of Aztec Gods
sources.author: Mark Cartwright

claims.quote: He is associated with a variety of concepts, including the night sky, hurricanes, obsidian, and conflict.

statement.id: Ia diasosiasikan dengan langit malam, badai angin topan, obsidian, dan konflik.
statement.en: He is associated with a variety of concepts, including the night sky, hurricanes, obsidian, and conflict.

claims.quote: He was considered one of the four sons of Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl, the primordial dual deity.

statement.id: Ia dianggap sebagai salah satu dari empat putra dewata primordial Ometecuhtli dan Omecihuatl.
statement.en: He was considered one of the four sons of Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl, the primordial dual deity.

claims.quote: His main festival was Toxcatl, which, like most religious festivals of Aztec culture, involved human sacrifice.

statement.id: Festival utamanya adalah Toxcatl yang melibatkan pengorbanan manusia dalam budaya Aztec.
statement.en: His main festival was Toxcatl, which, like most religious festivals of Aztec culture, involved human sacrifice.

claims.quote: Tezcatlipoca's nagual, his animal counterpart, was the jaguar.

statement.id: Nagual atau rekan hewani Tezcatlipoca adalah seekor jaguar.
statement.en: Tezcatlipoca's nagual, his animal counterpart, was the jaguar.

claims.quote: Tezcatlipoca (pron. Tez-ca-tli-po-ca) or 'Smoking Mirror' in Nahuatl was one of the most important gods in Postclassical Mesoamerican culture and particularly important for the Toltecs and the Aztecs, especially at Texcoco.

statement.id: Tezcatlipoca atau 'Cermin Berasap' dalam bahasa Nahuatl adalah salah satu dewa terpenting dalam budaya Mesoamerika Pascaklasik dan sangat penting bagi bangsa Toltec dan Aztec, terutama di Texcoco.
statement.en: Tezcatlipoca, or 'Smoking Mirror' in Nahuatl, was one of the most important gods in Postclassical Mesoamerican culture and particularly important for the Toltecs and the Aztecs, especially at Texcoco.

claims.quote: Tezcatlipoca ... He was an invisible and omnipotent creator god, patron deity of warriors, and, as the bringer of both good and evil, he was the very embodiment of change through conflict.

statement.id: Tezcatlipoca adalah dewa pencipta yang tak terlihat dan mahakuasa, dewa pelindung para prajurit, dan sebagai pembawa kebaikan sekaligus kejahatan ia adalah perwujudan perubahan melalui konflik.
statement.en: Tezcatlipoca was an invisible and omnipotent creator god, patron deity of warriors, and, as the bringer of both good and evil, the very embodiment of change through conflict.

claims.quote: Tezcatlipoca was the 10th of the 13 Lords of the Day and associated with the horned owl in the Mesoamerican calendar whilst his nagual or animal spirit was the jaguar.

statement.id: Tezcatlipoca adalah yang ke-10 dari 13 Penguasa Hari dan dikaitkan dengan burung hantu bertanduk dalam kalender Mesoamerika, sedangkan nagual atau roh hewannya adalah jaguar.
statement.en: Tezcatlipoca was the 10th of the 13 Lords of the Day and associated with the horned owl in the Mesoamerican calendar, while his nagual or animal spirit was the jaguar.

claims.quote: The Mesoamerican deity Tezcatlipoca was believed to be the son of the primordial androgynous god Ometeotl. In Aztec mythology he was the brother of Quetzalcoatl, Huizilopochtli and Xipe Totec.

statement.id: Tezcatlipoca diyakini putra dewa purba androgini Ometeotl; dalam mitologi Aztec ia saudara Quetzalcoatl, Huizilopochtli, dan Xipe Totec.
statement.en: The Mesoamerican deity Tezcatlipoca was believed to be the son of the primordial androgynous god Ometeotl; in Aztec mythology he was the brother of Quetzalcoatl, Huizilopochtli and Xipe Totec.

claims.quote: In the complex Mesoamerican and Aztec creation myth, Tezcatlipoca ruled the first world of the Sun but was then overthrown by Quetzalcóatl. The two later cooperated, however, to create the 5th Sun. Transformed into giant snakes, the two gods attacked and dismembered the female reptilian monster known as Tlaltecuhtli (or Cipactli)

statement.id: Dalam mitos penciptaan Mesoamerika dan Aztec, Tezcatlipoca menguasai dunia pertama Matahari tetapi digulingkan Quetzalcóatl. Keduanya kemudian bekerja sama menciptakan Matahari ke-5 dan, dengan berubah menjadi ular raksasa, menyerang dan memotong-motong monster reptil betina Tlaltecuhtli (atau Cipactli).
statement.en: In the Mesoamerican and Aztec creation myth, Tezcatlipoca ruled the first world of the Sun but was overthrown by Quetzalcóatl; the two later cooperated to create the 5th Sun and, transformed into giant snakes, attacked and dismembered the female reptilian monster Tlaltecuhtli (or Cipactli).

claims.quote: In the month of Tóxcatl, the sixth month (or 5th) of the Aztec solar year, Tezcatlipoca was worshipped in special ceremonies. As with other Aztec religious rites an important part of the ceremony was the impersonation of the god, most often by a prisoner of war, typically the best looking and most courageous one.

statement.id: Pada bulan Tóxcatl, bulan keenam (atau kelima) tahun surya Aztec, Tezcatlipoca dipuja dalam upacara khusus; bagian penting upacara itu adalah peniruan sang dewa, paling sering oleh tawanan perang yang biasanya paling tampan dan paling berani.
statement.en: In the month of Tóxcatl, the sixth (or 5th) month of the Aztec solar year, Tezcatlipoca was worshipped in special ceremonies; an important part was the impersonation of the god, most often by a prisoner of war, typically the best looking and most courageous one.

claims.quote: When the special month finally came around the impersonator was handsomely dressed in a warrior costume and in a symbolic wedding festival he married his four goddesses. Honoured with flowers and dances the man-god was then ferried to a dedicated temple where he was promptly sacrificed and his heart removed using an obsidian knife in order to honour the real Tezcatlipoca.

statement.id: Ketika bulan khusus itu tiba, sang peniru berpakaian prajurit dan dalam pesta pernikahan simbolis menikahi empat dewinya. Dihormati dengan bunga dan tarian, ia lalu dibawa ke kuil khusus tempat ia segera dikorbankan dan jantungnya diambil dengan pisau obsidian untuk menghormati Tezcatlipoca yang sejati.
statement.en: When the month came, the impersonator was dressed in a warrior costume and in a symbolic wedding festival married his four goddesses; honoured with flowers and dances, the man-god was then ferried to a dedicated temple where he was sacrificed and his heart removed with an obsidian knife to honour the real Tezcatlipoca.

claims.quote: He is also known as Blue Tezcatlipoca, the 'Hummingbird Sorcerer', god of Tenochtitlán, where he was associated with the sun and the war god Huitzilopochtli. He could be known as Red Tezcatlipoca, the 'Flayed One' and associated with the gods Camaxtli and Xipe Totec (god of the Tlaxcaltecans)

statement.id: Ia juga dikenal sebagai Tezcatlipoca Biru, 'Penyihir Kolibri', dewa Tenochtitlán, tempat ia dikaitkan dengan matahari dan dewa perang Huitzilopochtli; ia bisa dikenal sebagai Tezcatlipoca Merah, 'Si Terkuliti', yang dikaitkan dengan dewa Camaxtli dan Xipe Totec (dewa bangsa Tlaxcaltec).
statement.en: He is also known as Blue Tezcatlipoca, the 'Hummingbird Sorcerer', god of Tenochtitlán, where he was associated with the sun and the war god Huitzilopochtli; he could be known as Red Tezcatlipoca, the 'Flayed One', associated with the gods Camaxtli and Xipe Totec (god of the Tlaxcaltecans).

claims.quote: Ever-present, the god could intervene directly in human affairs to bring both happiness and sorrow. Tezcatlipoca could take on more sinister connotations when he was known as lord of the shadows or night, a sorcerer of black magic and the bringer of evil, death and destruction

statement.id: Sang dewa selalu hadir dan dapat campur tangan langsung dalam urusan manusia untuk membawa kebahagiaan maupun kesedihan; Tezcatlipoca bisa bermakna lebih suram ketika dikenal sebagai penguasa bayang-bayang atau malam, penyihir ilmu hitam, dan pembawa kejahatan, kematian, dan kehancuran.
statement.en: The ever-present god could intervene directly in human affairs to bring both happiness and sorrow; Tezcatlipoca could take on more sinister connotations as lord of the shadows or night, a sorcerer of black magic and the bringer of evil, death and destruction.

claims.quote: Also associated with conflict he was known as Yaotl or 'Enemy' and was patron of warriors and their training camps (telpochcalli). He was not always protective to soldiers, though, for sometimes he could be found at crossroads at the dead of night, ready to challenge any unsuspecting warriors.

statement.id: Dikaitkan dengan konflik, ia dikenal sebagai Yaotl atau 'Musuh' dan menjadi pelindung prajurit serta kamp pelatihan mereka (telpochcalli); namun ia tidak selalu melindungi prajurit, sebab kadang ia dapat ditemui di persimpangan jalan pada tengah malam, siap menantang prajurit yang lengah.
statement.en: Associated with conflict, he was known as Yaotl or 'Enemy' and was patron of warriors and their training camps (telpochcalli); he was not always protective to soldiers, for sometimes he could be found at crossroads at the dead of night, ready to challenge any unsuspecting warriors.

claims.quote: in later depictions of the god he has a polished black obsidian mirror instead of a left foot. This replacement of the foot is a reference to a wound he received in his famous battle with Tlaltecuhtli during the Creation.

statement.id: Dalam penggambaran yang lebih belakangan, sang dewa memiliki cermin obsidian hitam mengilap sebagai pengganti kaki kiri; pergantian kaki itu merujuk pada luka yang ia terima dalam pertempuran terkenalnya dengan Tlaltecuhtli saat Penciptaan.
statement.en: In later depictions of the god he has a polished black obsidian mirror instead of a left foot, a reference to a wound he received in his famous battle with Tlaltecuhtli during the Creation.

claims.quote: He is often in the company of a turquoise snake ... Sometimes he carries four arrows in his right hand, weapons he uses to punish wrongdoers.

statement.id: Ia sering ditemani ular pirus dan kadang membawa empat anak panah di tangan kanannya, senjata yang ia pakai untuk menghukum pelaku kejahatan.
statement.en: He is often in the company of a turquoise snake and sometimes carries four arrows in his right hand, weapons he uses to punish wrongdoers.

claims.quote: Then they decided to cook a fish but the smoke from their fire disturbed the stars, especially Citlallatonac and Citlalicue. These gods complained vociferously to Tezcatlipoca who, perhaps a little harshly, lopped off the heads of the couple and reattached them to their backsides, thus, the very first dogs were created.

statement.id: Asap api pasangan penyintas banjir mengganggu bintang-bintang, terutama Citlallatonac dan Citlalicue, yang mengeluh keras kepada Tezcatlipoca; ia memenggal kepala pasangan itu dan memasangnya di belakang tubuh mereka, sehingga lahirlah anjing-anjing pertama.
statement.en: The smoke from the couple's fire disturbed the stars, especially Citlallatonac and Citlalicue, who complained to Tezcatlipoca; he lopped off the heads of the couple and reattached them to their backsides, thus creating the very first dogs.

claims.quote: one of the most famous art objects of the god is the decorated skull now in the British Museum in London. The skull is covered in turquoise and black lignite mosaic with red thorny oyster shell in the nasal cavity.

statement.id: Salah satu benda seni paling terkenal tentang sang dewa adalah tengkorak berhias yang kini ada di British Museum di London, dilapisi mosaik pirus dan lignit hitam dengan cangkang tiram berduri merah di rongga hidung.
statement.en: One of the most famous art objects of the god is the decorated skull now in the British Museum in London, covered in turquoise and black lignite mosaic with red thorny oyster shell in the nasal cavity.

short_description.id: Gagak berkaki tiga adalah makhluk mitologis Asia Timur yang mewakili matahari.
short_description.en: The three-legged crow is an East Asian mythological creature representing the sun.

long_description.id: Gagak berkaki tiga adalah makhluk mitologis Asia Timur yang mewakili matahari. Dalam kisah Tiongkok, nama Yangwu dan Jinwu merujuk pada gagak matahari.
long_description.en: The three-legged crow is an East Asian mythological creature representing the sun. Chinese tales use Yangwu and Jinwu for the sun crow.

long_description.id: Shanhaijing memuat penyebutan gagak berkaki tiga. Gagak dalam cakram matahari muncul pada lambang pakaian resmi kekaisaran. Gagak matahari sering diberi warna merah meski disebut gagak emas. Gagak ini juga digambarkan bersama Ibu Suri dari Barat.
long_description.en: The Shanhaijing includes a reference to the three-legged crow. The crow in a solar disc appears among symbols on formal imperial garments. The sun crow is often colored red despite the name golden crow. This crow is also portrayed with the Queen Mother of the West.

long_description.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Lunheng bahwa kaum sarjana menyebut ada gagak berkaki tiga di dalam matahari, dan Zhang Heng menulis bahwa matahari menumpuk menjadi gagak yang bertiga jari kaki. Shanhaijing menyebut satu matahari tiba dan satu keluar, semuanya dibawa gagak, sedangkan Huainanzi menceritakan bahwa setelah Yi memanah sembilan matahari, semua gagak mati.
long_description.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Lunheng saying that scholars place a three-legged crow in the sun, and Zhang Heng writes that the sun accumulates into a crow with three toes. The Shanhaijing says one sun arrives while another goes out, all carried by crows, while the Huainanzi tells that after Yi shot nine suns the crows all died.

long_description.id: Kuodi tu yang dikutip Taiping Yulan menyebut gagak berkaki tiga mengambilkan makanan bagi Xiwangmu, dan Sima Xiangru menulis bahwa gagak itu menjadi suruhannya. Tang shu mencatat seekor gagak berkaki tiga yang dipersembahkan pada tahun pertama Tianshou; Ruizong berkata kaki depannya palsu, dan tak lama kemudian satu kaki jatuh.
long_description.en: The Kuodi tu quoted in the Taiping Yulan says the three-legged crow fetches food for Xiwangmu, and Sima Xiangru writes that it served as her messenger. The Tang shu records a three-legged crow presented in the first year of Tianshou; Ruizong said its front foot was false, and shortly afterwards one foot fell.

role.id: Gagak-gagak yang mati ketika matahari dipanah
role.en: The crows that die when the suns are shot

summary.id: Menurut Huainanzi yang dikutip Taiping Yulan, pada zaman Yao sepuluh matahari muncul bersamaan dan Yi memanah sembilan di antaranya; semua gagak mati dan sayapnya jatuh.
summary.en: According to the Huainanzi as quoted in the Taiping Yulan, ten suns appeared together in Yao's time and Yi shot nine of them; the crows all died and their wings fell.

note.id: Gagak berkaki tiga digambarkan bersama Ibu Suri dari Barat dan disebut suruhannya; Kuodi tu menyebutnya mengambilkan makanan baginya.
note.en: The three-legged crow is depicted with the Queen Mother of the West and called her messenger; the Kuodi tu says it fetches food for her.

claims.quote: The three-legged (or tripedal) crow is a mythological creature in various mythologies and arts of East Asia. It is believed to inhabit and represent the Sun.

statement.id: Gagak berkaki tiga adalah makhluk mitologis Asia Timur yang mewakili matahari.
statement.en: The three-legged crow is an East Asian mythological creature representing the sun.

claims.quote: The Chinese have several versions of crow and crow-Sun tales. But the most popular depiction and myth of the Sun crow is that of the Yangwu or Jinwu, the "golden crow". It has also been found figured on ancient coins from Lycia and Pamphylia.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Tiongkok, nama Yangwu dan Jinwu merujuk pada gagak matahari.
statement.en: Chinese tales use Yangwu and Jinwu for the sun crow.

claims.quote: It is also mentioned in the Shanhaijing. The earliest known depiction of a three-legged crow appears in Neolithic pottery of the Yangshao culture.

statement.id: Shanhaijing memuat penyebutan gagak berkaki tiga.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing includes a reference to the three-legged crow.

claims.quote: The sanzuwu in a disc represents the sun and is also one of the Twelve Ornaments that is used in the decoration of formal imperial garments in ancient China.

statement.id: Gagak dalam cakram matahari muncul pada lambang pakaian resmi kekaisaran.
statement.en: The crow in a solar disc appears among symbols on formal imperial garments.

claims.quote: The most popular depiction and myth of a sanzuwu is of a sun crow called the Yangwu (陽烏), more commonly referred to as the Jinwu (金烏; 'golden crow') or "golden crow". Even though it is described as a corvid, it is usually coloured red instead of black.

statement.id: Gagak matahari sering diberi warna merah meski disebut gagak emas.
statement.en: The sun crow is often colored red despite the name golden crow.

claims.quote: The sanzuwu is also depicted with the Queen Mother of the West who are believed to be her messengers.

statement.id: Gagak ini juga digambarkan bersama Ibu Suri dari Barat.
statement.en: This crow is also portrayed with the Queen Mother of the West.

claims.quote: 《論衡》曰：儒者言：日中有三足烏。日，火也。烏入火中燋爛，安得立？然烏，日氣也。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan (太平御覽) mengutip Lunheng (論衡): kaum sarjana (儒者) mengatakan di dalam matahari ada burung gagak berkaki tiga (三足烏); matahari adalah api, dan gagak yang masuk ke dalam api akan hangus, tetapi gagak adalah "qi matahari" (日氣).
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan (太平御覽) quotes the Lunheng (論衡): the scholars (儒者) say there is a three-legged crow (三足烏) in the sun; the sun is fire and a crow entering fire would be scorched, yet the crow is the "qi of the sun" (日氣).

claims.quote: 張衡《靈憲》曰：日，陽精之宗，積而成烏。烏有三趾，陽之數類竒。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Lingxian (靈憲) karya Zhang Heng (張衡): matahari adalah induk esensi "yang" (陽精之宗), yang menumpuk dan menjadi gagak; gagak punya tiga jari kaki (三趾), dan angka itu tergolong ganjil seperti bilangan "yang" (陽之數類竒).
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Lingxian (靈憲) of Zhang Heng (張衡): the sun is the ancestor of the yang essence (陽精之宗), which accumulates and becomes a crow; the crow has three toes (三趾), and the number is of the odd kind belonging to yang.

claims.quote: 《括地圗》曰：崑崙之弱水中，非乘龍不得至。有三足神烏，為西王母取食。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Kuodi tu (括地圗): di perairan Ruoshui di Kunlun, yang tak bisa dicapai tanpa menunggang naga, ada gagak gaib berkaki tiga (三足神烏) yang mengambilkan makanan bagi Xiwangmu (西王母).
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Kuodi tu (括地圗): in the Ruoshui waters of Kunlun, which cannot be reached without riding a dragon, there is a divine three-legged crow (三足神烏) that fetches food for Xiwangmu (西王母, Queen Mother of the West).

claims.quote: 司馬相如《大人賦》曰：吾乃覩西王母，皜然白首母，戴勝而穴處，有三足烏為之使。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Daren fu (大人賦) karya Sima Xiangru (司馬相如): sang penyair melihat Xiwangmu (西王母) beruban putih, bermahkota sheng (戴勝), tinggal di gua, dan seekor gagak berkaki tiga (三足烏) menjadi suruhannya (為之使).
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Daren fu (大人賦) of Sima Xiangru (司馬相如): the poet sees Xiwangmu (西王母), white-haired, wearing a sheng headdress (戴勝) and living in a cave, with a three-legged crow (三足烏) serving as her messenger (為之使).

claims.quote: 《淮南子》曰：堯時，十日並出。堯命羿仰射十日，中其九。烏皆死，墮其翼。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Huainanzi (淮南子): pada zaman Yao (堯) sepuluh matahari muncul bersamaan; Yao menyuruh Yi (羿) memanah sepuluh matahari itu dan mengenai sembilan di antaranya, lalu semua gagak (烏) mati dan sayapnya jatuh.
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Huainanzi (淮南子): in the time of Yao (堯) ten suns appeared together; Yao ordered Yi (羿) to shoot at the ten suns and he hit nine of them, whereupon the crows (烏) all died and their wings fell.

claims.quote: 《唐書》曰： 天授元年，有進三足烏者，天后以為周室嘉應。睿宗時為皇嗣，言曰：「烏前足偽也。」天后不恱。須臾，一足墮地，果如其言。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan mengutip Tang shu (唐書): pada tahun pertama Tianshou (天授) seseorang mempersembahkan gagak berkaki tiga dan Tianhou (天后) menganggapnya pertanda baik bagi dinasti Zhou (周室嘉應); Ruizong (睿宗), yang kala itu putra mahkota (皇嗣), berkata kaki depan gagak itu palsu (偽), dan tak lama kemudian satu kaki jatuh ke tanah.
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan quotes the Tang shu (唐書): in the first year of Tianshou (天授) someone presented a three-legged crow, and Tianhou (天后) took it as an auspicious response for the Zhou house (周室嘉應); Ruizong (睿宗), then the imperial heir (皇嗣), said the crow's front foot was false (偽), and shortly afterwards one foot fell to the ground.

claims.quote: 大荒之中，有山名曰孽搖頵羝，上有扶木，柱三百里，其葉如芥。有谷曰溫源谷。湯谷上有扶木。一日方至，一日方出，皆載于烏。

statement.id: Shanhaijing (山海經), Dahuang dong jing, menyebut di Tanggu (湯谷) ada pohon fusang (扶木); ketika satu matahari tiba, satu matahari lain keluar, dan semuanya dibawa oleh gagak (載于烏).
statement.en: The Shanhaijing (山海經), Dahuang dong jing, says that at Tanggu (湯谷) there is a fusang tree (扶木); as one sun arrives another goes out, and all are carried by crows (載于烏).

gaps.searched: Ilustrasi dalam artikel tidak dipakai tanpa pemeriksaan berkas Commons, kecocokan subjek, dan lisensinya; belum ada gambar yang terverifikasi untuk entri ini.

Sumber tambahan dari Wikisource Mandarin: Taiping Yulan juan 920 (memuat kutipan Lunheng, Zhang Heng, Kuodi tu, Sima Xiangru, Huainanzi, Tang shu) dan Shanhaijing Dahuang dong jing. Huainanzi Jingshen xun (踆烏) dibuka tetapi tidak menyebut tiga kaki, sehingga tidak dipakai.
Bagian lain (kemampuan, kelemahan, penggambaran modern) tidak diisi karena belum ada kutipan yang mendukungnya.

short_description.id: Tinirau adalah dewa pelindung ikan dalam mitologi Polinesia, putra Tangaroa menurut Tregear, yang bertempat tinggal di Pulau Suci Motutapu dan dalam sebagian tradisi bersifat ganda.
short_description.en: Tinirau is a guardian deity of fish in Polynesian mythology, a son of Tangaroa according to Tregear, who dwelt on the Holy Island of Motutapu and in some traditions has a dual nature.

long_description.id: Kisah tentang Tinirau ditemukan di seluruh kepulauan Polinesia, dan ia adalah penjaga ikan. Tregear menyebutnya dewa pelindung ikan dan putra Tangaroa, Penguasa Samudra. Nama lainnya dalam bahasa Polinesia antara lain Kinilau, Sinilau, Tigilau, dan Tinilau.
long_description.en: Stories about Tinirau are found throughout the islands of Polynesia, and he is a guardian of fish. Tregear calls him the tutelary deity of fishes and a son of Tangaroa, the Lord of Ocean. His other names in Polynesian languages include Kinilau, Sinilau, Tigilau and Tinilau.

long_description.id: Menurut Tregear, Tinirau tinggal di Pulau Suci (Motutapu), yang disepakati semua orang Polinesia, dan rumahnya berupa cagar ikan yang dikelilingi kolam pembiakan. Dalam tradisi Mangaia ia setengah ikan, mewarisi Motu-tapu, dan menjadi penguasa semua ikan. Dalam sebagian tradisi lain ia memiliki dua sisi: yang merusak sebagai penjaga hiu dan yang ramah sebagai pemuda tampan, atau sisi kanan manusia dan sisi kiri ikan.
long_description.en: According to Tregear, Tinirau dwelt on the Holy Island (Motutapu), as all Polynesians agree, and his home was a fish preserve ringed by breeding pools. In the Mangaian tradition he is half a fish, inherits Motu-tapu and is lord of all fish. In some other traditions he has two sides: a destructive one as guardian of sharks and a kind one as a handsome youth, or a human right side and a fish left side.

long_description.id: Tregear mencatat bahwa Tinirau meminjamkan seekor paus peliharaannya kepada penyihir Kae, yang membunuhnya. Tinirau murka dan mengirim Hina bersama sekelompok perempuan untuk menjebak Kae. Hina menjadi istri Tinirau. Di Samoa, kisah Tinilau (atau Tigilau) dan istrinya Sina sangat populer.
long_description.en: Tregear records that Tinirau lent a pet whale to the magician Kae, who killed it. Furious, Tinirau sent Hina with a party of women to trap Kae. Hina became Tinirau's wife. In Samoa the stories of Tinilau (or Tigilau) and his wife Sina are very popular.

short_description.id: Tsurube-otoshi adalah yōkai yang dikisahkan di beberapa prefektur Jepang dan dikatakan jatuh dari pohon untuk menyerang, bahkan memangsa, manusia.
short_description.en: Tsurube-otoshi is a yōkai told about in several Japanese prefectures, said to drop from trees to attack and even devour humans.

long_description.id: Tsurube-otoshi adalah yōkai yang diceritakan di Prefektur Kyoto, Shiga, Gifu, Aichi, dan Wakayama, antara lain. Kisah-kisah menyebut ia jatuh dari atas pohon untuk menyerang dan bahkan memangsa manusia. Menurut Yokai.com, namanya berarti "ember sumur yang jatuh" karena ia menjatuhkan diri dengan cepat seperti batu.
long_description.en: Tsurube-otoshi is a yōkai told about in Kyoto, Shiga, Gifu, Aichi and Wakayama Prefectures, among others. Stories say it drops from above the trees to attack and even devour humans. According to Yokai.com, its name means "falling well bucket" because it drops quickly like a stone.

long_description.id: Yokai.com menggambarkannya sebagai kepala raksasa tanpa tubuh milik manusia, tengu, atau oni, kadang diselubungi api, yang mengintai di pucuk pohon larut malam. Di wilayah Kansai ia paling sering berupa kepala tunggal, di Tohoku biasanya berkelompok. Ia juga dikatakan menjatuhkan batu atau ember dari atas.
long_description.en: Yokai.com describes it as a gigantic disembodied head of a human, a tengu or an oni, sometimes wreathed in flames, lurking in the treetops late at night. In the Kansai region it is most often a single head, in Tohoku usually a group. It is also said to drop rocks or buckets from above.

long_description.id: Satu versi daerah menggambarkannya sebagai kepala terpenggal yang jatuh dari pohon pinus tua, dan versi lain menyebut ia memangsa manusia. Dalam tuturan lisan lain, ia jatuh dari pohon kaya sambil terkekeh lalu naik lagi; dalam kisah dari Wakayama, orang yang tergoda oleh benda berkilau diseret ke dalam ember dan dimakan.
long_description.en: One local version describes a severed head dropping from an old pine tree, and another says it devours humans. In another oral legend it drops from a kaya tree with a sniggering laugh and rises again; in a tale from Wakayama, people lured by something shining are dragged into a bucket and devoured.

long_description.id: Dalam kumpulan kaidan zaman Edo, ia digambarkan sebagai roh pohon besar yang berubah menjadi api yang menghujan. Wikipedia juga mencatat teori bahwa tsurube-otoshi dan tsurubebi pada mulanya sama-sama cahaya hantu yang menggantung di pohon.
long_description.en: In an Edo-period kaidan collection it is depicted as the spirit of a large tree turned into flames that rain down. Wikipedia also records a theory that tsurube-otoshi and tsurubebi were originally both ghost lights hanging from trees.

summary.id: Menurut tuturan lisan yang dicatat Wikipedia, sebuah tsurube-oroshi tiba-tiba jatuh dari pohon kaya, terkekeh sambil menanyakan apakah pekerjaan malam sudah selesai dan mengajak menjatuhkan ember, lalu naik lagi ke atas pohon.
summary.en: According to an oral legend recorded by Wikipedia, a tsurube-oroshi suddenly drops from a kaya tree, sniggering and asking whether the night work is done and whether to drop a bucket, then rises above the tree again.

title.id: Koin koban di pangkal pohon tua
title.en: The koban coin at the foot of an old tree

role.id: Pemangsa yang menunggu di atas pohon.
role.en: The predator waiting above the tree.

summary.id: Dalam kisah dari Wakayama, orang yang mengulurkan tangan ke benda berkilau di pangkal pohon tua karena mengira itu koin koban diseret ke dalam ember dan diangkat ke atas pohon, lalu dimakan.
summary.en: In a tale from Wakayama, someone who reaches for something shining at the foot of an old tree, thinking it a koban coin, is dragged into a bucket, lifted above the tree and devoured.

note.id: Wikipedia mencatat teori bahwa tsurube-otoshi dan tsurubebi pada mulanya sama-sama cahaya hantu yang menggantung di pohon.
note.en: Wikipedia notes a theory that tsurube-otoshi and tsurubebi were originally both ghost lights hanging from trees.

claims.quote: Tsurube-otoshi (釣瓶落とし) or tsurube-oroshi (釣瓶下ろし) is a yōkai told about in Kyoto Prefecture, Shiga Prefecture, Gifu Prefecture, Aichi Prefecture, and Wakayama Prefecture, among other places.

statement.id: Tsurube-otoshi adalah yōkai yang diceritakan di beberapa prefektur Jepang.
statement.en: Tsurube-otoshi is a yōkai reported in several Japanese prefectures.

claims.quote: They are said to drop from above the trees and attack, and even devour humans.

statement.id: Kisah-kisah menyebut ia jatuh dari pohon untuk menyerang orang.
statement.en: Stories say it drops from trees to attack people.

claims.quote: Also, in the Tera section of Sogabe village, tsurube-oroshi are said to appear as a severed head that would drop down from an old pine tree and then eat and feed on someone and after that not appear for about two to three days, and then they would appear once again.

statement.id: Salah satu versi daerah menggambarkannya sebagai kepala terpenggal yang jatuh dari atas.
statement.en: One local version describes a severed head falling from above.

claims.quote: In the Tsuchida section of the village of Ōi, it is also said that tsurube-oroshi would devour humans.

statement.id: Versi lain menyebut ia memangsa manusia.
statement.en: Another version says it devours humans.

claims.quote: Tsurube otoshi are a gigantic disembodied heads of either a human, a tengu, or an oni. Sometimes they appear wreathed in flames like large fireballs with facial features.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, tsurube otoshi adalah kepala raksasa tanpa tubuh milik manusia, tengu, atau oni, dan kadang tampak diselubungi api seperti bola api besar berwajah.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, tsurube otoshi are gigantic disembodied heads of a human, a tengu or an oni, sometimes appearing wreathed in flames like large fireballs with facial features.

claims.quote: Tsurube otoshi lurk in the treetops late at night and wait for unsuspecting creatures to pass underneath. When they need to feed, they drop quickly to the ground like a stone.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, tsurube otoshi mengintai di pucuk pohon larut malam, menunggu makhluk yang tak curiga lewat di bawahnya, lalu jatuh cepat ke tanah seperti batu saat perlu makan.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, tsurube otoshi lurk in the treetops late at night, waiting for unsuspecting creatures to pass underneath, and drop to the ground like a stone when they need to feed.

claims.quote: This is the reason for its name, which means "falling well bucket."

statement.id: Yokai.com menyatakan bahwa itulah asal namanya, yang berarti "ember sumur yang jatuh".
statement.en: Yokai.com states that this is the reason for its name, which means "falling well bucket".

claims.quote: They also drop large rocks or even well buckets (they have a sense of humor) on their victims from up high, laughing at the damage they inflict.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, mereka juga menjatuhkan batu besar atau bahkan ember sumur dari ketinggian ke korbannya sambil menertawakan kerusakan yang ditimbulkan.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, they also drop large rocks or even well buckets on their victims from up high, laughing at the damage they inflict.

claims.quote: Tsurube otoshi encountered in the Kansai region are most often solitary, gargantuan heads. In the Tohoku region, tsurube otoshi are usually encountered in larger groups of slightly smaller heads.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, tsurube otoshi di wilayah Kansai paling sering berupa kepala raksasa tunggal, sedangkan di wilayah Tohoku biasanya berupa kelompok kepala yang sedikit lebih kecil.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, tsurube otoshi in the Kansai region are most often solitary gargantuan heads, while in the Tohoku region they usually come in larger groups of slightly smaller heads.

claims.quote: in the Hōki section of the village of Sogabe in Kyoto Prefecture (now Kameoka), a tsurube-oroshi would suddenly drop down from a kaya tree and make a sniggering laugh saying "has your night work ended, how 'bout let's drop a bucket, gii-gii" ("yagyō sunda ka, tsurube oroso ka, gii-gii") and then rise up above the tree again.

statement.id: Dalam tuturan lisan dari bagian Hōki, desa Sogabe (kini Kameoka), Prefektur Kyoto, yang dicatat Wikipedia, sebuah tsurube-oroshi tiba-tiba jatuh dari pohon kaya sambil terkekeh dan berkata "sudah selesai kerja malammu? mau kujatuhkan ember? gii-gii", lalu naik lagi ke atas pohon.
statement.en: In an oral legend from the Hōki section of Sogabe village (now Kameoka), Kyoto Prefecture, recorded by Wikipedia, a tsurube-oroshi suddenly drops from a kaya tree with a sniggering laugh, saying "has your night work ended, how 'bout let's drop a bucket, gii-gii", and then rises above the tree again.

claims.quote: In a Genroku period yōkai tale told about in the Kuroe part of Kainan, Wakayama Prefecture, it is said that a certain old tree would have something shining at its base ... they would get dragged into a bucket and lifted up to above the tree where they would be menaced and then devoured by the tsurube-otoshi living there

statement.id: Dalam kisah zaman Genroku yang dicatat Wikipedia, orang yang mengulurkan tangan ke sesuatu yang berkilau di pangkal pohon tua karena mengira itu koin koban akan diseret ke dalam ember, diangkat ke atas pohon, lalu diteror dan dimakan oleh tsurube-otoshi yang tinggal di sana.
statement.en: In an account recorded by Wikipedia, someone who reaches for something shining at the base of an old tree, thinking it a koban coin, is dragged into a bucket, lifted above the tree, menaced and then devoured by the tsurube-otoshi living there.

claims.quote: In the Edo Period collection of kaidan (mysterious tales), the Kokon Hyakumonogatari Hyōban, they are depicted under the name of "tsurube-oroshi" (釣瓶おろし ) as a yōkai that is a spirit of a large tree that has turned into flames that rain down.

statement.id: Dalam kumpulan kaidan zaman Edo, Kokon Hyakumonogatari Hyōban, yang dicatat Wikipedia, ia digambarkan dengan nama "tsurube-oroshi" sebagai yōkai berupa roh pohon besar yang berubah menjadi api yang menghujan.
statement.en: In the Edo-period kaidan collection Kokon Hyakumonogatari Hyōban, recorded by Wikipedia, they are depicted under the name "tsurube-oroshi" as a yōkai that is the spirit of a large tree turned into flames that rain down.

claims.quote: there is also the theory that originally both the tsurube-otoshi and the tsurubebi were similarly atmospheric ghost lights that dangle from trees like buckets.

statement.id: Wikipedia mencatat teori bahwa pada mulanya tsurube-otoshi dan tsurubebi sama-sama berupa cahaya hantu atmosferik yang menggantung di pohon seperti ember.
statement.en: Wikipedia notes a theory that originally both the tsurube-otoshi and the tsurubebi were similarly atmospheric ghost lights dangling from trees like buckets.

text.id: dilaporkan sejak 1960-an, dengan laporan koran pertama pada 6 Agustus 1963
text.en: reported since the 1960s, with the first newspaper report on 6 August 1963

short_description.id: Tuttle Bottoms Monster adalah makhluk legendaris yang konon mendiami kawasan berawa di utara Harrisburg, Illinois. Biasanya ia digambarkan seperti kera berbulu dengan moncong panjang mirip trenggiling.
short_description.en: The Tuttle Bottoms Monster is a legendary creature said to haunt a swampy area north of Harrisburg, Illinois. It is usually pictured as a hairy, ape-like animal with a long, anteater-like snout.

long_description.id: Tuttle Bottoms Monster adalah makhluk legendaris yang konon mendiami kawasan berawa di utara Harrisburg, Illinois, di daerah aliran Sungai Saline. Biasanya ia digambarkan seperti kera dan berbulu, dengan moncong panjang mirip trenggiling. Legendanya dikenal oleh beberapa generasi warga Saline County.
long_description.en: Local legend places this creature in a swampy stretch of the Saline River watershed north of Harrisburg, Illinois, and usually pictures it as ape-like and hairy, with a long, anteater-like snout. Generations of Saline County residents know the legend.

long_description.id: Menurut mantan kepala polisi Harrisburg Gary Crabtree, kantornya menerima sekitar 50 laporan selama 28 tahun tentang hewan tak dikenal di kawasan itu, sebagian menyebut dua kaki dan sebagian empat kaki. The Harrisburg Daily Register memuat apa yang tampaknya laporan pertama pada 6 Agustus 1963, dan laporan paling awal berasal dari tahun 1960-an. Beberapa laporan menyebut ukurannya delapan kaki, sedangkan remaja setempat dikatakan pernah berburu monster itu dengan senapan pada malam hari.
long_description.en: Former Harrisburg Police Chief Gary Crabtree said his department logged roughly 50 reports across 28 years about an unknown beast in the area, some describing two legs and some four. The Harrisburg Daily Register published what seemed to be the first report on 6 August 1963, and the earliest reports date to the 1960s. Some reports give its size as eight feet, and local teens were said to have gone hunting the monster with rifles at night.

long_description.id: Tentang jati dirinya ada beberapa pendapat. Seorang warga mengatakan makhluk itu bukan monster dari mitos, melainkan hewan sungguhan yang dilepaskan pemerintah federal dan sudah lama mati, sedangkan versi lain menyebut ia dilepas oleh pemilik kebun binatang pedesaan.
long_description.en: There are several views of what it was. One resident said it was never a mythical monster but a real animal that the federal government let loose and that died long ago, while another version says a rural zoo owner set it free.

claims.quote: The Tuttle Bottoms Monster is a legendary creature said to inhabit a swampy area, north of Harrisburg, Illinois, on the Saline River watershed, usually described as ape-like and hairy with a long snout similar to an anteater.

statement.id: Monster Tuttle Bottoms adalah makhluk legenda di daerah rawa utara Harrisburg Illinois dengan wujud mirip kera berbulu dan bermoncong panjang.
statement.en: The Tuttle Bottoms Monster is a legendary creature said to inhabit a swampy area north of Harrisburg, Illinois, described as ape-like and hairy with a long snout.

claims.quote: Former Harrisburg Police Chief Gary Crabtree told the Harrisburg Daily Register that his department received approximately 50 reports over 28 years of an unidentified beast in the area northwest of Harrisburg, some reporting a creature with two legs and some with four.

statement.id: Mantan kepala polisi Harrisburg menyatakan kepolisian menerima sekitar 50 laporan selama 28 tahun tentang makhluk tak dikenal berkaki dua atau empat.
statement.en: The former police chief told the local newspaper that his department received roughly 50 reports over 28 years of an unidentified beast with two or four legs.

claims.quote: Most described it as having a long, almost anteater-like snout.

statement.id: Sebagian besar laporan menggambarkannya memiliki moncong panjang yang mirip pemakan semut.
statement.en: Most described it as having a long, almost anteater-like snout.

claims.quote: On August 6, 1963, The Harrisburg Daily Register reported what seemed to be the first report of the creature.

statement.id: Pada 6 Agustus 1963, The Harrisburg Daily Register memuat apa yang tampaknya laporan pertama tentang makhluk itu.
statement.en: On August 6, 1963, The Harrisburg Daily Register published what seemed to be the first report of the creature.

claims.quote: He said it was eight feet long, four feet high and had a nose like an anteater.

statement.id: Menurut laporan koran 1963 itu, seorang pemuda menyebut makhluk tersebut panjangnya delapan kaki, tingginya empat kaki, dan berhidung seperti trenggiling.
statement.en: In the 1963 newspaper account a youth said the creature was eight feet long, four feet high and had a nose like an anteater.

claims.quote: The earliest reports of the creature date to the 1960s by teenagers who used the area as a local "make-out" spot and by hunters who would make frantic calls to the police after seeing the creature.

statement.id: Laporan paling awal berasal dari tahun 1960-an, dari remaja yang memakai kawasan itu sebagai tempat berpacaran dan dari pemburu yang menelepon polisi dengan panik setelah melihat makhluk itu.
statement.en: The earliest reports date to the 1960s, from teenagers who used the area as a local "make-out" spot and from hunters who made frantic calls to the police after seeing the creature.

claims.quote: A local resident named Virgil Smith told the Register he believes the creature is not a monster out of myth but was an actual animal "released by the federal government" that has long since died.

statement.id: Seorang warga setempat mengatakan kepada koran Register bahwa ia yakin makhluk itu bukan monster dari mitos, melainkan hewan sungguhan yang "dilepaskan oleh pemerintah federal" dan sudah lama mati.
statement.en: A local resident told the Register he believes the creature is not a monster out of myth but an actual animal "released by the federal government" that has long since died.

claims.quote: Smith said the creature was a hairy primate, stood on two legs, and was not scared of humans, adding that one couple reported the animal walked right up to them.

statement.id: Warga itu menyebut makhluk tersebut primata berbulu yang berdiri dengan dua kaki dan tidak takut pada manusia, dan menambahkan bahwa sepasang orang melaporkan hewan itu berjalan tepat mendekati mereka.
statement.en: The resident said the creature was a hairy primate that stood on two legs and was not scared of humans, adding that one couple reported the animal walked right up to them.

claims.quote: The reports have said that it is eight feet long or tall, depending upon whether it is upright on two feet, or down on all fours.

statement.id: Menurut laporan, ukurannya delapan kaki panjang atau tinggi, bergantung pada apakah ia berdiri tegak dengan dua kaki atau berjalan dengan keempat kaki.
statement.en: According to the reports it is eight feet long or tall, depending on whether it is upright on two feet or down on all fours.

claims.quote: Many local teens would wander out into the boggy areas with rifles to hunt the monster, who was known to be active at night.

statement.id: Banyak remaja setempat berkeliaran di area berawa dengan senapan untuk memburu monster itu, yang dikenal aktif pada malam hari.
statement.en: Many local teens would wander into the boggy areas with rifles to hunt the monster, which was known to be active at night.

claims.quote: The Tuttle Bottoms Monster legend is familiar to generations of Saline County residents.

statement.id: Legenda Tuttle Bottoms Monster dikenal oleh beberapa generasi warga Saline County.
statement.en: The Tuttle Bottoms Monster legend is familiar to generations of Saline County residents.

claims.quote: Also, the creature is believed to have been released into the area by either the federal government, or was set loose by a rural zoo owner

statement.id: Makhluk itu juga diyakini dilepas ke kawasan tersebut oleh pemerintah federal, atau dilepaskan oleh pemilik kebun binatang pedesaan.
statement.en: The creature is also believed to have been released into the area either by the federal government or by a rural zoo owner.

text.id: Tradisi mantra Udug Hul tercatat sejak milenium ketiga SM hingga akhir zaman kuno.
text.en: The Udug Hul incantation tradition runs from the third millennium BCE to late antiquity.

short_description.id: Udug adalah golongan iblis yang identitas dan sifatnya ambigu dalam mitologi Mesopotamia.
short_description.en: Udug are an ambiguously defined class of demons in Mesopotamian mythology.

long_description.id: Udug adalah golongan iblis yang identitas dan sifatnya ambigu dalam mitologi Mesopotamia. Dalam bahasa Akkadia, udug kemudian disebut utukku.
long_description.en: Udug are an ambiguously defined class of demons in Mesopotamian mythology. In Akkadian, udug later becomes known as utukku.

long_description.id: Udug dikatakan lahir di dunia bawah Kur. Istilah udug mula-mula tidak menentukan sifat baik atau jahat. Teks pengusiran memanggil udug baik untuk melawan udug jahat. Udug juga dapat menjadi istilah payung, bukan nama satu iblis.
long_description.en: Udug are described as born in the underworld Kur. The term udug originally does not specify good or evil. Exorcism texts invoke good udug against evil udug. Udug can also serve as an umbrella term rather than one demon’s name.

long_description.id: Dalam Epos Gilgamish, menurut sebuah kajian lama, utukku Ea-bani naik dari bumi. Kajian itu menyebut utukku semula adalah roh atau hantu yang mengintai manusia di gurun, atau bertempat di pegunungan, laut, atau pekuburan, dan malapetaka menimpa orang yang hanya dipandangnya. Utukku juga menjadi yang pertama dalam enam golongan roh jahat yang disebut berulang dalam mantra.
long_description.en: In the Epic of Gilgamish, according to an older study, the utukku of Ea-bani rises from the earth. The study says the utukku was originally a spirit or ghost that lurked in the desert awaiting people, or made its home in the mountains, sea, or graveyard, and that evil befell anyone it merely looked upon. The utukku is also the first of six classes of evil spirits named repeatedly in the incantations.

long_description.id: Udug jahat sering menjadi perantara penyakit, dan mantra udug-hul berfokus pada pengusirannya. Tradisi mantra itu mencakup seluruh sejarah Mesopotamia kuno; kanonnya dalam bahasa Akkadia terdiri atas enam belas lempeng. Namun udug juga dapat berperan sebagai pelindung: Gudea meminta "udug yang baik" untuk melindunginya, dan teks pengusiran memanggil udug baik. Deskripsinya sering mengaitkannya dengan bayangan gelap, racun, dan suara memekakkan, meski ada pula yang menyebutnya tak bernama dan tak berbentuk.
long_description.en: The evil udug is often a vector for illness, and the udug-ḫul incantations focus on driving it out. That incantation tradition spans the whole of ancient Mesopotamian history, and its Akkadian canon is in sixteen tablets. Yet the udug can also act as a protector: Gudea asks for a "good udug" to protect him, and exorcism texts invoke the good udug. Descriptions often link it with a dark shadow, poison, and a deafening voice, although it is also said to be nameless and formless.

short_description.id: Wagyl (juga Waugal) adalah perwujudan Ular Pelangi orang Noongar di Australia Barat bagian barat daya, makhluk Dreaming berbentuk ular yang menciptakan sungai Swan dan Canning serta aliran air dan bentang alam lain.
short_description.en: The Wagyl (also Waugal) is the Noongar manifestation of the Rainbow Serpent in south-west Western Australia, a snakelike Dreaming creature that made the Swan and Canning rivers and other waterways and landforms.

long_description.id: Wagyl, juga ditulis Waugal atau Waagal, adalah perwujudan Ular Pelangi dalam agama dan mitologi Aboriginal dari budaya Noongar di barat daya Australia Barat. Orang Noongar menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk Dreaming berbentuk ular yang menciptakan Sungai Swan dan Canning serta aliran air dan bentang alam di sekitar Perth. Dalam dialek Wiilman ia disebut Ngunnunguddy Gnuditj, yang berarti ular berwajah berbulu.
long_description.en: The Wagyl, also written Waugal or Waagal, is the Noongar manifestation of the Rainbow Serpent in Aboriginal religion and mythology from the culture of the south-west of Western Australia. The Noongar portray it as a snakelike Dreaming creature that formed the Swan and Canning rivers and the waterways and landforms around Perth. In the Wiilman dialect it is called Ngunnunguddy Gnuditj, meaning hairy-faced snake.

long_description.id: Kisah tentang Wagyl berbeda-beda di antara kelompok Noongar. Sebagian menyebutnya penguasa bumi dan langit yang tinggal di sumber air, yang lain menyebutnya pencipta dan penjaga air tawar, tetapi di semua kelompok ia adalah tokoh sentral yang memberi hidup. Tumpukan batu dikatakan kotorannya dan tempatnya dianggap keramat. Dalam rekaman perpustakaan negara bagian yang menyebut sungai bagian dari kisah penciptaan Wagyl, seorang tetua Noongar menuturkan bahwa di mana pun ia berbelok ia membuat cekungan sungai, lalu air datang mengisinya.
long_description.en: Stories of the Wagyl vary among Noongar groups. Some call it the ruler of earth and sky living in water sources, others the creator and keeper of fresh water, but in every group it is a central figure that gives life. Piles of rock are said to be its droppings and such places are held sacred. In a state library recording a Noongar elder says that wherever it turned it made a hollow for the river, and then water arrived and filled it.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Nyitting yang dituturkan Trevor Walley, Waugal bertarung dengan Buaya Roh sehingga Derbal Nara (Cockburn Sound) terkeruk dan air laut mengalir masuk. Tubuh buaya itu menjadi Garden Island, dan ekornya diletakkan Waugal di muara Sungai Swan sebagai gosong pasir batu kapur agar air asin tidak naik. Wikipedia menambahkan bahwa kisah-kisah Wagyl mungkin merekam ingatan lisan tentang megafauna Australia yang punah.
long_description.en: In the Nyitting story told by Trevor Walley the Waugal fights the Spirit Crocodile, gouging out Derbal Nara (Cockburn Sound) so that sea water rushes in. The crocodile's body becomes Garden Island and its tail is set by the Waugal at the mouth of the Swan River as a limestone bar to keep salt water out. Wikipedia adds that Wagyl stories may preserve an oral memory of extinct Australian megafauna.

short_description.id: Kaum Qizhong adalah bangsa utara legendaris dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Qizhong people are a legendary northern race in Chinese tradition.

long_description.id: Kaum Qizhong adalah bangsa utara legendaris dalam tradisi Tiongkok. Kitab Gunung dan Laut menempatkan negeri mereka di timur kaum Juying dan menggambarkan kaki besar.
long_description.en: Qizhong people are a legendary northern race in Chinese tradition. The Classic of Mountains and Seas places their land east of the Juying people and describes huge feet.

long_description.id: Komentar menyebut mereka berjalan tanpa menempatkan tumit di tanah. Novel Bunga dalam Cermin menggambarkan mereka berjalan dengan ujung jari kaki.
long_description.en: Commentary says they walk without placing heels on the ground. The novel Flowers in the Mirror portrays them walking on their toes.

long_description.id: Teks Haiwai Beijing menempatkan negeri Qizhong di selatan atau timur Juying dan menyebut kaki penduduknya menopang, atau dalam versi lain bertubuh besar dengan kaki besar; negeri itu juga disebut Fanzhong atau Dazhong. Nama Qizhong juga dipakai untuk seekor burung dalam Shanhaijing, yang berbeda dari bangsa ini.
long_description.en: The Haiwai Beijing text places the Qizhong country south or east of Juying and says its people’s feet are propped, or in another version that they are big with big feet; the country is also called Fanzhong or Dazhong. The name Qizhong is also used in the Shanhaijing for a bird, which is distinct from this people.

claims.quote: 跂踵人（きしょうじん）は中国に伝わる伝説上の人種である。大踵とも。古代中国では北方に位置する国に棲んでいたとされる。

statement.en: The name Qizhong (跂踵) can refer to a bird or to a country, the Qizhong country (跂踵国); both appear in the Shanhaijing (山海经).

short_description.id: 顒 (Yú) adalah burung dalam Shan Hai Jing yang berbentuk seperti burung hantu, berwajah manusia, bermata empat, dan bertelinga; kemunculannya dianggap pertanda kekeringan besar.
short_description.en: 顒 (Yú) is a bird in the Shan Hai Jing shaped like an owl, with a human face, four eyes and ears; its appearance is taken as an omen of great drought.

long_description.id: 顒 adalah burung dalam kitab geografi kuno Shan Hai Jing (bagian 南山經). Bentuknya seperti burung hantu, tetapi ia berwajah manusia dengan empat mata dan telinga. Burung itu bersuara menyebut namanya sendiri, dan kemunculannya dikaitkan dengan kekeringan.
long_description.en: 顒 is a bird in the ancient geographical text Shan Hai Jing (the 南山經 section). It is shaped like an owl, but has a human face with four eyes and ears. The bird cries out its own name, and its appearance is linked to drought.

long_description.id: Menurut teks itu, burung ini berada di lembah bernama 中谷 di sebelah selatan gunung 令丘, gunung yang tanpa tumbuhan dan banyak apinya. Bila burung itu terlihat, seluruh negeri akan dilanda kekeringan besar.
long_description.en: According to the text, the bird lives in a valley called 中谷 south of Lingqiu mountain (令丘), a mountain without plants or trees and with much fire. When the bird is seen, the whole land will suffer a great drought.

long_description.id: Cara membaca aksara 顒 berbeda-beda. Dalam bahasa Jepang ia dibaca ぎょう atau ぐ, kamus Jepang memuat グ (ゴ), catatan pada teks asli (Guo Pu) memberi 娛, dan bacaan Tionghoa modernnya adalah yú.
long_description.en: How to read the character 顒 varies. In Japanese it is read ぎょう or ぐ, Japanese dictionaries give グ (ゴ), the note on the original text (Guo Pu) gives 娛, and its modern Chinese reading is yú.

literal_meaning.id: Nama itu berasal dari suara burung itu sendiri.
literal_meaning.en: The name comes from the bird's own cry.

who.id: Burung berwajah manusia dan bermata empat dalam Shan Hai Jing.
who.en: A human-faced, four-eyed bird in the Shan Hai Jing.

origin.id: Disebut dalam bagian 南山經 dari Shan Hai Jing, di lembah selatan gunung 令丘.
origin.en: Named in the 南山經 section of the Shan Hai Jing, in a valley south of Lingqiu mountain.

role.id: Kemunculannya adalah pertanda kekeringan.
role.en: Its appearance is an omen of drought.

famous_for.id: Dikenal sebagai burung pembawa tanda kekeringan besar.
famous_for.en: Known as the bird that signals a great drought.

description.id: Gunung tanpa tumbuhan dan banyak apinya; burung 顒 berada di lembah di sebelah selatannya.
description.en: A mountain without plants or trees and with much fire; the bird 顒 lives in a valley to its south.

description.id: Lembah di selatan gunung 令丘, tempat angin 條風 keluar dan tempat burung 顒 berada.
description.en: A valley south of Lingqiu mountain from which the tiao wind comes out, where the bird 顒 lives.
