claims.quote: 顒（ぎょう、ぐ）は、中国に伝わるフクロウに似た、四つ目で耳のある人面鳥。その目撃は旱魃の予兆とされる。

statement.id: Yong adalah burung Tiongkok menyerupai burung hantu dengan wajah manusia, telinga, dan empat mata, yang dikaitkan dengan kekeringan.
statement.en: Yong is a Chinese owl-like bird with a human face, ears and four eyes, associated with drought.

claims.quote: 古代中国の地理書「山海経」の南山経によると、令丘（れいきゅう）山という火炎の多く草木が育たない山の南にある中谷（ちゅうこく）と呼ばれる谷に住んでいるという。

statement.id: Shan Hai Jing menempatkannya di lembah selatan Gunung Lingqiu.
statement.en: The Shan Hai Jing places it in a valley south of Lingqiu mountain.

claims.quote: 梟（ふくろう）に似た姿だが、顔は人間のようで、耳と四つの目を持っている。「顒」という名称は、その鳴き声から来ている。

statement.id: Namanya meniru suara burung berwajah manusia dan bermata empat itu.
statement.en: Its name imitates the cry of the human-faced, four-eyed bird.

claims.quote: 又東四百里，曰令丘之山，無草木，多火。其南有谷焉，曰中谷，條風自是出

statement.id: Dalam Shan Hai Jing (南山經), 400 li lebih jauh ke timur terdapat gunung 令丘 yang tanpa tumbuhan dan banyak apinya; di sebelah selatannya ada lembah bernama 中谷, tempat angin 條風 keluar.
statement.en: In the Shan Hai Jing (南山經), a further 400 li to the east lies Lingqiu mountain (令丘之山), without plants or trees and with much fire; to its south is a valley called Zhonggu (中谷), from which the tiao wind (條風) comes out.

claims.quote: 有鳥焉，其狀如梟，人面四目而有耳，其名曰顒〈音娛〉，其鳴自號也

statement.id: Di sana ada seekor burung yang bentuknya seperti 梟 (burung hantu), berwajah manusia, bermata empat, dan bertelinga, bernama 顒 (catatan tafsir: dibaca 娛).
statement.en: There is a bird there shaped like an owl (梟), with a human face, four eyes and ears, named 顒 (the commentary glosses its pronunciation as 娛).

claims.quote: 其狀如梟，人面四目而有耳，其名曰顒〈音娛〉，其鳴自號也，見則天下大旱。

statement.id: Burung bernama 顒 itu bersuara menyebut namanya sendiri, dan bila ia terlihat, seluruh negeri mengalami kekeringan besar.
statement.en: The bird named 顒 cries out its own name, and when it is seen the whole land suffers a great drought.

claims.quote: 顒は「グ」（「ゴ」）と読むと日本の字引にみえる。 また原文注釈で「顒」の音には「娛」が当てられている（郭璞注）。 現代中国読みは「ユウ」（拼音: yú;ウェード式: yü）である。

statement.id: Kamus Jepang memuat bacaan グ (ゴ) untuk 顒. Catatan pada teks asli (Guo Pu) memberi 娛 sebagai bunyi 顒, dan bacaan Tionghoa modernnya adalah yú (ユウ).
statement.en: Japanese dictionaries give the reading グ (ゴ) for 顒. The note on the original text (Guo Pu) gives 娛 as the sound of 顒, and its modern Chinese reading is yú (ユウ).

short_description.id: Nanahiro-nyōbō adalah yōkai perempuan raksasa yang tinggi atau lehernya mencapai tujuh hiro.
short_description.en: Nanahiro-nyōbō is a giant female yōkai whose height or neck reaches seven hiro.

long_description.id: Nanahiro-nyōbō adalah yōkai perempuan raksasa yang tinggi atau lehernya mencapai tujuh hiro. Tradisi Kepulauan Oki menempatkan pertemuannya pada jalan gunung.
long_description.en: Nanahiro-nyōbō is a giant female yōkai whose height or neck reaches seven hiro. An Oki Islands tradition places her encounters on mountain roads.

long_description.id: Batu besar setempat dijelaskan sebagai tubuhnya yang membatu dan konon terus membesar. Versi Matsue memberinya rambut terurai dan gigi hitam ketika membentang pada gunung dan pesisir.
long_description.en: A large local rock is explained as her petrified body and is said to keep growing. A Matsue version gives her hanging hair and black teeth as she spans mountains and the coast.

long_description.id: Ia juga disebut nanahiro-onna atau shichijō-onna dan diceritakan di Shimane timur serta Tottori tengah-barat. Dalam legenda zaman Oda Nobunaga, seorang lelaki menebas wajahnya dan ia berubah menjadi batu besar; keluarga Nakata setempat konon keturunan lelaki itu. Di Yasugi ia dikisahkan sebagai perempuan cantik yang mengemis dengan pakaian sepanjang tujuh hiro, sedangkan di Akasaki ia berambut biru dan berwajah putih, menumbuk padi sambil menyanyi sedih.
long_description.en: She is also called nanahiro-onna or shichijō-onna and is told of in eastern Shimane and central-western Tottori. In a legend from Oda Nobunaga’s time, a man slashed her face and she became a huge rock; the local Nakata family is said to descend from him. In Yasugi she is a beautiful woman begging in clothes seven hiro long, while in Akasaki she has blue hair and a white face and pounds rice while singing sadly.

claims.quote: 島根町（現・松江市）では、浜地区の境の山から海岸の島にまたがって七尋女房が現れ、長い髪を垂らし、黒い歯をむき出し、道を行く人に笑いかけたという。

statement.id: Versi Matsue memberinya rambut terurai dan gigi hitam ketika membentang pada gunung dan pesisir.
statement.en: A Matsue version gives her hanging hair and black teeth as she spans mountains and the coast.

claims.quote: 七尋女房，又稱七尋女、七丈女，是流傳於島根縣東部與鳥取縣中西部，一種巨大的女性妖怪。

statement.id: Nanahiro-nyōbō, juga disebut nanahiro-onna (七尋女) atau shichijō-onna (七丈女), adalah yōkai perempuan raksasa dari Shimane timur dan Tottori tengah-barat (島根縣東部與鳥取縣中西部).
statement.en: Nanahiro-nyōbō, also called nanahiro-onna (七尋女) or shichijō-onna (七丈女), is a giant female yōkai of eastern Shimane and central-western Tottori (島根縣東部與鳥取縣中西部).

claims.quote: 織田信長時代有一個著名的傳說，稱一名男子騎馬行於山道時，被不知從哪來的石頭砸中。 ... 男人一刀斬傷七尋女房的臉，負傷的七尋女房變為一塊巨石。據傳當地的中田氏便是那名男子的後代

statement.id: Dalam legenda zaman Oda Nobunaga, seorang lelaki menebas wajah nanahiro-nyōbō, dan ia yang terluka berubah menjadi batu besar; keluarga Nakata (中田氏) setempat konon keturunan lelaki itu.
statement.en: In a legend from Oda Nobunaga’s time, a man slashed the nanahiro-nyōbō’s face, and, wounded, she turned into a huge rock; the local Nakata family (中田氏) is said to descend from that man.

claims.quote: 在安來市，傳說七尋女房是個美人，身穿七尋長的衣服四處乞討。據說當地有一個名為「乙御前塚」的土丘，與七尋女房有關。

statement.id: Di Yasugi (安來市), nanahiro-nyōbō dikisahkan sebagai perempuan cantik yang berkeliling mengemis dengan pakaian sepanjang tujuh hiro; gundukan tanah bernama Otogozen-zuka (乙御前塚) di sana dikaitkan dengannya.
statement.en: In Yasugi (安來市), the nanahiro-nyōbō is told of as a beautiful woman who went begging in clothes seven hiro long; a mound there called Otogozen-zuka (乙御前塚) is linked with her.

claims.quote: 在東伯郡赤碕町(今琴浦町)，傳說七尋女房是個青髮白臉的女妖怪，會一邊搗米一邊因吟唱歌謠，神色淒苦。

statement.id: Di Akasaki, Distrik Tōhaku (kini Kotoura, 琴浦町), ia dikisahkan sebagai yōkai perempuan berambut biru dan berwajah putih yang menumbuk padi sambil menyanyi dengan wajah sedih.
statement.en: In Akasaki, Tōhaku District (now Kotoura, 琴浦町), she is told of as a blue-haired, white-faced female yōkai who pounds rice while singing with a sorrowful look.

summary.id: Tinggi seluruh tubuh mencapai tujuh hiro.
summary.en: The full body reaches seven hiro.

summary.id: Leher mencapai tujuh hiro.
summary.en: The neck reaches seven hiro.

short_description.id: Shuangjing adalah burung Tiongkok legendaris yang juga disebut burung terang ganda.
short_description.en: Shuangjing is a legendary Chinese bird also called the double-brightness bird.

long_description.id: Shuangjing adalah burung Tiongkok legendaris yang juga disebut burung terang ganda.
long_description.en: Shuangjing is a legendary Chinese bird also called the double-brightness bird.

long_description.id: Ia menyerupai ayam dengan dua pupil dan suara mirip fenghuang, terbang bahkan setelah kehilangan bulu. Kunjungannya yang jarang disambut karena mengusir hewan buas dan mencegah malapetaka.
long_description.en: It resembles a chicken with two pupils and a phoenixlike cry, flying even after losing feathers. Its rare visits are welcomed for driving off beasts and preventing calamities.

long_description.id: Menurut Shiyi ji, burung ini dipersembahkan negeri Zhizhi kepada Yao pada tahun ke-70 pemerintahannya. Ketika burung itu tidak datang, orang membuat patungnya dari kayu atau logam dan menaruhnya di pintu untuk mengusir makhluk jahat; kebiasaan menggambar ayam di jendela pada Tahun Baru disebut berasal dari citra burung ini.
long_description.en: According to the Shiyi ji, the bird was presented to Yao by the country of Zhizhi in the 70th year of his reign. When the bird did not come, people made its image in wood or metal and set it at their doors to drive off evil beings; the custom of painting a chicken on the window at New Year is said to derive from it.

claims.quote: 双睛（そうせい）は、中国に伝わる伝説の鳥。堯の在位70年を記念して献上されたといわれる。別名重明の鳥（ちょうめいのとり）。

statement.id: Shuangjing adalah burung Tiongkok legendaris yang juga disebut burung terang ganda.
statement.en: Shuangjing is a legendary Chinese bird also called the double-brightness bird.

claims.quote: 姿は鶏に似ているが、目の中に瞳が二つあり、鳳凰のような声で鳴く。そして、羽毛が抜け落ちても、羽根のない翼で空を飛んだという。

statement.id: Ia menyerupai ayam dengan dua pupil dan suara mirip fenghuang, terbang bahkan setelah kehilangan bulu.
statement.en: It resembles a chicken with two pupils and a phoenixlike cry, flying even after losing feathers.

claims.quote: 滅多に現れない鳥で、多くても一年に数回、少ない時は数年間も現れなかったという。虎や狼などの猛獣を追い払ったり災害を防いだりしてくれるので、人々は双睛が巣を作ってくれることを願い、家の前を綺麗にしていたという。

statement.id: Kunjungannya yang jarang disambut karena mengusir hewan buas dan mencegah malapetaka.
statement.en: Its rare visits are welcomed for driving off beasts and preventing calamities.

claims.quote: 在尧在位70年时，在他晚年的时候，有个叫秪支国的国家献上一只鸟，名叫重明鸟，又叫双睛鸟。

statement.id: Pada tahun ke-70 pemerintahan Yao (尧), negeri bernama Zhizhi (秪支国) mempersembahkan seekor burung bernama chongming niao (重明鸟), disebut juga burung shuangjing (双睛鸟).
statement.en: In the 70th year of Yao’s (尧) reign, a country called Zhizhi (秪支国) presented a bird named chongming niao (重明鸟), also called the shuangjing bird (双睛鸟).

claims.quote: 其未至之时，国人或刻木，或铸金，为此鸟之状。置于门户之间，则魑魅丑类，自然退伏。

statement.id: Menurut Shiyi ji, ketika burung itu belum datang, orang membuat patung kayu atau logam berbentuk burung ini dan menaruhnya di pintu, sehingga siluman dan makhluk jahat (魑魅) mundur dengan sendirinya.
statement.en: According to the Shiyi ji, when the bird had not come, people carved wood or cast metal in its shape and set it at their doors, so that goblins and evil beings (魑魅) withdrew of themselves.

claims.quote: 自然退伏。今人每岁元日，或刻木铸金，或图画为鸡于牖上，此其遗象也。

statement.id: Kebiasaan orang setiap Tahun Baru (元日) mengukir kayu, menuang logam, atau menggambar ayam di jendela disebut sebagai sisa citra burung ini.
statement.en: The custom of carving wood, casting metal or painting a chicken on the window every New Year’s Day (元日) is said to be a remnant of this bird’s image.

short_description.id: Ачбуудан adalah kuda perang dan tulpar milik Жолой dalam epos Манас; menurut legenda ia lahir dari kuda betina Кула secara gaib, dan dalam satu varian ia berbicara untuk memohon nyawa tuannya.
short_description.en: Ачбуудан is the war horse and tulpar of Жолой in the Манас epic; legend says it was born miraculously of the Кула mare, and in one variant it speaks to beg for its master's life.

long_description.id: Ачбуудан adalah kuda perang Жолой dan tulpar, kuda unggul yang ia pacu dalam lomba, dalam epos Манас. Pada lomba kuda di pesta peringatan Көкөтөй, Ачбуудан tiba di belakang Аккула. Kuda ini dikenal selalu menyelamatkan tuannya dari maut.
long_description.en: Ачбуудан is the war horse of Жолой and the tulpar, the champion steed, he raced in the Манас epic. In the horse race at Көкөтөй's memorial feast, Ачбуудан finished behind Аккула. The horse is known for always saving its master from death.

long_description.id: Legenda Акас мерген menceritakan asal-usulnya. Pada masa perang, ketika sekelompok кыргыз terpencil di pegunungan, kuda betina Кула milik Акас мерген melahirkan anak kuda tanpa kuda jantan, dan para tetua berkata kelahiran itu datang dari alam gaib. Kuda betina yang sama melahirkan tiga tulpar termasyhur: Аккула, Ачбуудан, dan Мааникер.
long_description.en: The legend of Акас мерген tells of its origin. In a time of war, when a group of кыргыз was cut off in the mountains, the Кула mare of Акас мерген foaled without a stallion, and the elders said the births came from the unseen world. The same mare bore three famous tulpars: Аккула, Ачбуудан and Мааникер.

long_description.id: Ачбуудан lahir sebagai anak kuda kelabu berekor pucat. Seorang pedagang membelinya, dan di pasar Жолой membelinya dari pedagang itu dan menamainya. Legenda itu juga menyebut bahwa suatu ketika seekor kuda jantan biru keluar dari danau dan mendekati kuda betina Кула.
long_description.en: Ачбуудан was born as a grey colt with a pale tail. A merchant bought it and led it away, and at the bazaar Жолой bought it from him and gave it its name. The legend also tells that at one point a blue stallion came out of a lake and approached the Кула mare.

long_description.id: Dalam satu varian epos, ketika Манас menawan Жолой dan hendak membunuhnya, Ачбуудан tiba-tiba dapat berbicara dan memohon nyawa tuannya. Setelah itu ia masuk ke dalam api yang berkobar dan lenyap. Kisah ini menjadi contoh hewan yang berbicara dan berpikir seperti manusia, citra yang sering muncul dalam epos.
long_description.en: In one variant of the epic, when Манас captured Жолой and was about to kill him, Ачбуудан suddenly gained speech and begged for its master's life. It then plunged into the blazing fire and vanished. The episode is an example of an animal that speaks and thinks like a human, an image that often appears in epics.

statement.id: Dalam satu varian, ketika Манас hendak membunuh Жолой, Ачбуудан mendadak bisa berbicara (тил бүтүп) dan memohon darah (канын) Жолой, yakni nyawanya.
statement.en: In one variant, when Манас is about to kill Жолой, Ачбуудан gains the power of speech (тил бүтүп) and begs for Жолой's blood (канын), that is, his life.

claims.quote: Акас мерген — уламыш боюнча атактуу тулпарлар Аккула, Ачбуудан, Мааникерди тууган Кула бээнин ээси.

statement.id: Menurut legenda (уламыш), Акас мерген adalah pemilik kuda betina Кула yang melahirkan tulpar termasyhur Аккула, Ачбуудан, dan Мааникер.
statement.en: According to legend (уламыш), Акас мерген owned the Кула mare that foaled the famous tulpars Аккула, Ачбуудан and Мааникер.

claims.quote: Айгыр жок туруп эле Кула бээнин Кула кулун тууп коюшу, элди кубандырат, бир чети таң калтырат. Айылдагы акылман аксакалдар Кула бээ кайыптан тууду деп айтышат.

statement.id: Kuda betina Кула melahirkan anak kuda tanpa ada kuda jantan (Айгыр жок), sehingga orang heran; para tetua bijak berkata ia melahirkan dari alam gaib (кайыптан).
statement.en: The Кула mare foaled with no stallion present (Айгыр жок), to people's wonder; the wise elders said she had foaled from the unseen world (кайыптан).

claims.quote: Кийинки жазда да Кула бээ куйругу агыш Сур кулун тууйт.

statement.id: Musim semi berikutnya kuda betina Кула melahirkan anak kuda kelabu (Сур кулун) berekor pucat (куйругу агыш).
statement.en: The following spring the Кула mare foaled a grey (Сур кулун) colt with a pale tail (куйругу агыш).

claims.quote: Ач куйрук тайды (сур тай) кулундуу он беш бээ, он беш атка бир соодагер сатып алып ... Базардан соодагер жетелеп турган ач куйрукту Жолой сатып алып, атын

statement.id: Seorang pedagang (соодагер) membeli anak kuda ekor pucat (Ач куйрук, сур тай) itu seharga lima belas kuda betina beranak dan lima belas kuda; kemudian Жолой membelinya dari pedagang itu di pasar dan memberinya nama.
statement.en: A merchant (соодагер) bought the pale-tailed (Ач куйрук, сур тай) colt for fifteen mares with foals and fifteen horses; then Жолой bought it from the merchant at the bazaar and named it.

claims.quote: Бир маалда көлдөн көпкөк айгыр чыгып келип Кула бээни жыттагылап калат.

statement.id: Suatu ketika seekor kuda jantan biru (көпкөк айгыр) keluar dari danau (көлдөн) dan mendekati kuda betina Кула.
statement.en: At one point a blue stallion (көпкөк айгыр) came out of the lake (көлдөн) and sniffed at the Кула mare.

claims.quote: Жоокерчилик заманда калмактар кыргызга кол салып, аларды туш тарапка таратканда 10 түтүн кыргыз бөлүнүп, тоо арасында калып калат.

statement.id: Legenda ini berlatar masa perang ketika калмактар menyerang кыргыз dan sepuluh keluarga (10 түтүн) кыргыз terpisah dan tinggal di pegunungan.
statement.en: The legend is set in a time of war when the калмактар attacked the кыргыз and ten households (10 түтүн) of кыргыз were cut off and stayed in the mountains.

claims.quote: Манас Жолойду колго түшүргөндө, Ачбуудан Манастан ээсинин жанын сурайт:

statement.id: Ketika Манас menawan Жолой, Ачбуудан memohon kepada Манас nyawa (жанын) tuannya.
statement.en: When Манас captured Жолой, Ачбуудан begged Манас for its master's life (жанын).

claims.quote: деп алоолонгон отко түшүп кайып болуп кетет. Ошондой эле эпосто мындай образдар көп кездешет.

statement.id: Setelah berkata demikian, kuda itu masuk ke dalam api yang berkobar (алоолонгон отко) dan lenyap (кайып болуп); citra seperti ini banyak dijumpai dalam epos (эпосто).
statement.en: Having said this, the horse plunged into the blazing fire (алоолонгон отко) and vanished (кайып болуп); such images are common in the epic (эпосто).

claims.quote: эпостордо жан-жаныбарлар (айбанат, канаттуу) жана жансыз нерселер (тооташ, суу, өсүмдүктөр) адамча сүйлөп, ойлоп кишидеги касиетке да ээ болушат.

statement.id: Dalam epos (эпостордо), hewan dan benda mati dapat berbicara dan berpikir seperti manusia (адамча сүйлөп) serta memiliki sifat manusia; artikel ketiga membahas Ачбуудан sebagai contohnya.
statement.en: In epics (эпостордо), animals and inanimate things speak and think like humans (адамча сүйлөп) and gain human qualities; the third article discusses Ачбуудан as an example.

short_description.id: Jing adalah makhluk gaib dalam tradisi Tiongkok: roh yang dipercaya muncul pada hewan, tumbuhan, bahkan benda mati yang sudah sangat tua, dan sebagian dapat berubah wujud.
short_description.en: Jing is a supernatural being in Chinese tradition: a spirit believed to arise in very old animals, plants and even objects, some of which can change form.

long_description.id: Jing (精) adalah kategori makhluk gaib dalam tradisi Tiongkok. Makhluk hidup dan benda dapat mengembangkan roh semacam itu seiring waktu: secara umum dipercaya bahwa benda yang hidup atau tersimpan seratus atau seribu tahun lebih menyerap sari alam dan menjadi jing, yang juga disebut jingguai. Contohnya meliputi roh rubah, ular, pohon, dan bunga.
long_description.en: Jing (精) is a category of supernatural being in Chinese tradition. Living beings and objects may develop such spirits over time: it is widely believed that things that live or are kept for a hundred or a thousand years or more absorb the essence of nature and become jing, also called jingguai. Examples include fox, snake, tree and flower spirits.

long_description.id: Sebagian jing digambarkan dapat berubah wujud. Dalam Baopuzi, jing semua benda tua dapat menyamar sebagai manusia untuk menyilaukan dan menguji orang, tetapi tidak dapat mengubah wujud aslinya di cermin; karena itu daoshi yang masuk gunung menggantungkan cermin di punggung mereka. Jika yang datang adalah makhluk burung atau hewan, wujudnya tampak di cermin, dan siluman tua yang pergi berjalan mundur dan tidak punya tumit.
long_description.en: Some jing are described as changing form. In the Baopuzi the jing of all aged things can take human form to dazzle and test people, but cannot change their true form in a mirror; so Daoists entering the mountains hung mirrors on their backs. If the visitor is a bird- or beast-spirit its form shows in the mirror, and an old spirit leaves walking backwards and has no heels.

long_description.id: Artikel Wikipedia menyebut bahwa Soushenji menganggap segala sesuatu berjiwa dan lama-kelamaan menjadi siluman, bahwa jing dalam Tiongkok memiliki silsilah menurut Baize Jingguai Tu, dan bahwa Jepang memiliki konsep serupa seperti tsukumogami. Soushenji sendiri mengutip Baize Tu tentang jing anak kecil bernama Xinang di antara dua gunung.
long_description.en: The Wikipedia article says the Soushenji holds that all things have spirits and over time turn into monsters, that Chinese jing have a genealogy according to the Baize Jingguai Tu, and that Japan has a similar concept such as tsukumogami. The Soushenji itself quotes the Baize Tu about a child-like jing named Xinang between two mountains.

cultural_context.id: Sebuah artikel ensiklopedia menyebut bahwa gagasan jing dipengaruhi pandangan bahwa segala sesuatu berjiwa.
cultural_context.en: An encyclopedia article says the idea of jing is influenced by the view that all things have spirits.

claims.quote: 东晋干宝搜神记认为万物有灵，久了就会化作妖怪。中国的精，依《白泽精怪图》等书的记载有一个完整的谱系，其中印度的传入也汇进这个谱系。同时，中国的精除动植物之外，也有非生物包括器具，日本的精有较多受中国影响。

statement.id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia berbahasa Mandarin ini, Soushenji menganggap segala sesuatu memiliki roh yang lama-kelamaan menjadi siluman; jing dalam Tiongkok memiliki silsilah lengkap menurut Baize Jingguai Tu dan sejenisnya, dan selain hewan serta tumbuhan juga mencakup benda mati seperti perkakas.
statement.en: According to this Chinese Wikipedia article, the Soushenji holds that all things have spirits which over time turn into monsters; Chinese jing have a complete genealogy according to works such as the Baize Jingguai Tu, and include non-living things such as utensils besides animals and plants.

claims.quote: 普遍认为各种事物包括生物和非生物，只要活或保存百年、千年以上时间就会吸收自然界的精华成精，亦稱為精怪。

statement.id: Secara umum dipercaya bahwa segala hal, hidup maupun tidak, yang hidup atau tersimpan seratus atau seribu tahun lebih akan menyerap sari alam dan menjadi jing, yang juga disebut jingguai.
statement.en: It is widely believed that all things, living or not, that live or are kept for a hundred or a thousand years or more absorb the essence of nature and become jing, also called jingguai.

claims.quote: 中国传说认为包括与人有关的怪异现象可能有些是精怪影响的，传说精怪会包括变身、幻术等不同能力，还会寄宿在一些物体上。

statement.id: Menurut legenda Tiongkok, sebagian kejadian ganjil yang berkaitan dengan manusia mungkin dipengaruhi jingguai; legenda menyebut jingguai memiliki kemampuan seperti berubah wujud dan ilmu ilusi, serta dapat bersemayam pada benda-benda tertentu.
statement.en: According to Chinese legend, some strange phenomena involving people may be influenced by jingguai; the legends say they have abilities such as transformation and illusion arts and may lodge in certain objects.

claims.quote: 除了中国，其他一些地区如日本亦有类似成精的概念，如陈旧器具变「付喪神」的传说。

statement.id: Selain Tiongkok, Jepang juga memiliki konsep serupa, misalnya legenda perkakas tua yang menjadi tsukumogami.
statement.en: Besides China, regions such as Japan have a similar concept, for example the legend of old utensils becoming tsukumogami.

claims.quote: 在东方文化妖怪有时也叫妖精，在口語中，「妖」、「精」、「怪」幾個字經常連用，有時候還能相互替換。

statement.id: Dalam budaya Timur, yaoguai kadang disebut yaojing, dan dalam percakapan huruf yao, jing, dan guai sering dipakai bersama atau saling menggantikan.
statement.en: In Eastern cultures a yaoguai is sometimes called a yaojing, and in speech the characters yao, jing and guai are often used together and sometimes interchangeably.

claims.quote: 然后变成其他生物、非生物或人形态。（如西游记孙悟空就石头成精变猴子）

statement.id: Contoh yang disebut: Sun Wukong dalam Xiyouji adalah batu yang menjadi jing lalu berubah menjadi monyet.
statement.en: The example given is Sun Wukong in the Xiyouji, a stone that became a jing and turned into a monkey.

claims.quote: 又萬物之老者，其精悉能假讬人形，以眩惑人目而常試人，唯不能於鏡中易其真形耳。

statement.id: Menurut Baopuzi, jing semua benda yang sudah tua dapat menyamar sebagai manusia untuk menyilaukan mata dan terus menguji orang, tetapi tidak dapat mengubah wujud aslinya di dalam cermin.
statement.en: According to the Baopuzi, the jing of all aged things can all assume human form to dazzle people's eyes and constantly test them, but cannot change their true form in a mirror.

claims.quote: 是以古之入山道士，皆以明鏡徑九寸已上，懸於背後，則老魅不敢近人。

statement.en: According to the Baopuzi, ancient Daoists entering the mountains hung a bright mirror nine cun or more in diameter behind their backs, so that the old spirits (laomei) dared not come near people.

short_description.id: Yayu adalah dewa serta monster legendaris Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Yayu is a Chinese legendary deity and monster.

long_description.id: Yayu adalah dewa serta monster legendaris Tiongkok. Kitab Gunung dan Laut memberi dewa aslinya tubuh ular serta wajah manusia sebelum dibunuh.
long_description.en: Yayu is a Chinese legendary deity and monster. The Classic of Mountains and Seas gives the original deity a serpent body and human face before being killed.

long_description.id: Setelah dihidupkan kembali ia menjadi hewan merah berwajah manusia, berkaki mirip kuda, dan bersuara mirip bayi. Yi mengalahkan monster pemakan manusia atas perintah Yao.
long_description.en: After revival it becomes a red beast with a human face, horselike feet and an infantlike cry. Yi defeats the man-eating monster on Yao’s orders.

long_description.id: Kitab Gunung dan Laut menyebut Yayu dalam beberapa bagian dengan wujud berbeda. Di bagian Gunung Utara ia adalah binatang berbentuk seperti sapi bertubuh merah, berwajah manusia, dan berkaki kuda yang bersuara seperti bayi dan memakan manusia; di bagian Laut Dalam Barat ia bertubuh ular dan berwajah manusia, dibunuh oleh menteri Erfu, dan jasadnya dijaga para dukun yang memegang obat tak-mati. Huainanzi memasukkan Yayu (猰貐) ke dalam daftar makhluk yang mencelakai rakyat pada masa Yao.
long_description.en: The Classic of Mountains and Seas mentions Yayu in several sections with different forms. In the Northern Mountains section it is an ox-shaped beast with a red body, human face and horse feet that cries like an infant and eats people; in the Western Interior section it has a serpent body and human face, was killed by Erfu's minister, and its corpse is flanked by shamans holding medicine of immortality. The Huainanzi lists Yayu (猰貐) among the creatures that harmed the people in Yao's time.

short_description.id: Chaofeng (嘲風) adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga yang digambarkan menyerupai feniks; ia gemar bahaya, dan sosoknya diletakkan di sudut atap dan sudut istana.
short_description.en: Chaofeng (嘲風) is one of the dragon's nine sons, depicted as phoenix-like; it likes danger, and its likeness is placed at roof edges and palace corners.

long_description.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, Chaofeng adalah salah satu putra naga dalam uraian Li Dongyang di 懐麓堂集. Wujudnya menyerupai feniks (鳳凰), penjelmaan burung. Ia konon menyukai tempat terjal dan memandang jauh, sehingga diletakkan di tepi atap bangunan.
long_description.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, Chaofeng is one of the dragon's sons in Li Dongyang's account in the 懐麓堂集. It resembles a phoenix (鳳凰), an incarnation of a bird. It is said to like steep places and distant views, which is why it is placed on the eaves of roofs.

long_description.id: Beberapa teks Ming mencatat daftar putra naga yang "tidak menjadi naga, masing-masing punya kegemaran". Dalam Shuo Lüe karya Gu Qiyuan, 嘲風 gemar bahaya dan berada di sudut istana; dalam Yangsheng fuyu karya Chen Jiru, ia gemar bahaya sepanjang hidupnya dan binatang-binatang yang berlari di sudut istana adalah sosoknya. Shuo Lüe menambahkan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi kaisar menanyakan nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang, yang memperoleh keterangannya dari catatan lama yang asal-usulnya tidak diketahui.
long_description.en: Several Ming texts record a list of dragon sons that "did not become dragons, each with its own fondness". In Gu Qiyuan's Shuo Lüe, 嘲風 likes danger and is at palace corners; in Chen Jiru's Yangsheng fuyu, it liked danger all its life and the running beasts on palace corners are its likeness. The Shuo Lüe adds that in the Hongzhi period the emperor asked Li Dongyang for the names of the nine sons, and that Li obtained his information from an old register whose origin is unknown.

long_description.id: Penulis Shuo Lüe sendiri meragukan daftar itu: setelah memeriksa catatan, ia menilai teori tersebut tidak berdasar dan menyisihkan 囚牛, 嘲風, dan 霸下 sebagai nama yang menunggu penelitian. Yŏrha ilgi membandingkan beberapa teks: Duilei zonggui menyebut 嘲風 berdiri di sudut istana, sedangkan Bowuzhi yipian menyebut 螭吻 (Chiwen) yang berdiri di sudut istana. Penulisnya bertanya bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui, dan menyebut teori kuno semacam itu banyak yang dibuat-buat.
long_description.en: The author of the Shuo Lüe himself doubts the list: after examining records he judged the theory unfounded and set 囚牛, 嘲風 and 霸下 aside as names awaiting investigation. The Yŏrha ilgi compares several texts: the Duilei zonggui has 嘲風 standing at the palace corner, while the Bowuzhi yipian has 螭吻 (Chiwen) standing at the palace corner. Its author asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known, and calls old theories of this kind mostly embellishment.

claims.quote: 龍生九子，不成龍，各有所好。囚牛，好音樂，以飾胡琴。睚眦，好殺，以飾刀柄。嘲風，好險，在殿角。蒲牢，好鳴，取為鐘紐。狻猊，好座，取為佛座。霸下，好負重，為碑座。狴犴，好訟，為獄門。屓屭，好文，在碑兩傍。蚩吻，好吞，在殿脊。弘治間，泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽，李不能悉，詢於吏部劉員外績，乃得其說，於故冊面上所錄，然亦不知所從出，因據以復。

statement.id: Dalam Shuo Lüe (說略, karya Gu Qiyuan, Ming), daftar sembilan putra naga yang "tidak menjadi naga, masing-masing punya kegemaran" memuat 嘲風 yang gemar bahaya (好險) dan berada di sudut istana (在殿角). Teksnya menambahkan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi (弘治) kaisar (泰陵) menyuruh seorang kasim menanyakan nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang (李東陽); Li tidak dapat menyebut semuanya, bertanya kepada Liu Ji (劉績), dan memperoleh keterangannya dari catatan lama yang asal-usulnya pun tidak diketahui.
statement.en: In the Shuo Lüe (說略, by Gu Qiyuan, Ming), the list of the dragon's nine sons that "did not become dragons, each with its own fondness" includes 嘲風, which likes danger (好險) and is at palace corners (在殿角). The text adds that in the Hongzhi (弘治) period the emperor (泰陵) had a eunuch ask Li Dongyang (李東陽) for the names of the nine sons; Li could not give them all, asked Liu Ji (劉績), and obtained the account from an old register whose origin was also unknown.

claims.quote: 余憶十一、二時，曾見其說於《對類總龜》中，近因歴考傳記，乃知其說為不經。 ... 已上都不見有龍子之說，囚牛、嘲風、霸下，俟考。

statement.id: Penulis Shuo Lüe mengingat pernah melihat teori itu dalam Duilei zonggui (對類總龜) ketika berusia sebelas atau dua belas tahun, tetapi setelah memeriksa catatan ia menyimpulkan teori itu tidak berdasar (不經). Dari nama-nama yang dibahasnya, tak satu pun ia temukan dalam catatan sebagai putra naga; 囚牛, 嘲風 (Chaofeng), dan 霸下 ia tinggalkan sebagai "menunggu penelitian" (俟考).
statement.en: The author of the Shuo Lüe recalls seeing the theory in the Duilei zonggui (對類總龜) when he was eleven or twelve, but after examining records he concluded that it was not canonical (不經). Of the names he discusses, he found none in records described as a dragon's son; 囚牛, 嘲風 (Chaofeng) and 霸下 he left as "to be examined" (俟考).

claims.quote: 對類總龜謂龍產九子。一名嘲風。好險。立殿角。一名蚩吻。好呑。立殿脊。博物志逸篇云。螭吻。形似獸。性好望。故立殿角。 ... 諸說亦各不同。龍子名號及性情。何以知之。古說傅會多此類。

statement.id: Dalam Yŏrha ilgi (熱河日記): Duilei zonggui (對類總龜) menyebut salah satu putra naga bernama 嘲風 yang gemar bahaya (好險) dan berdiri di sudut istana, serta 蚩吻 yang gemar menelan; Bowuzhi yipian (博物志逸篇) justru menyebut 螭吻 (Chiwen) yang gemar memandang berdiri di sudut istana. Penulisnya menyatakan pendapat-pendapat itu berbeda-beda, mempertanyakan bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui, dan menyebut teori kuno semacam itu banyak yang dibuat-buat.
statement.en: In the Yŏrha ilgi (熱河日記): the Duilei zonggui (對類總龜) names one of the dragon's sons 嘲風, which likes danger (好險) and stands at palace corners, and another, 蚩吻, which likes swallowing; the Bowuzhi yipian (博物志逸篇) instead says that 螭吻 (Chiwen), which likes to look out, stands at the palace corner. The author says the accounts differ, asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known, and says old theories of this kind are mostly embellishment.

claims.quote: 嘲風，平生好險，今殿角走獸是。蒲牢，平生好鳴，今鐘上獸紐是。狻猊，平生好坐，今佛座獅子是。

statement.id: Dalam Yangsheng fuyu (養生膚語, karya Chen Jiru, Ming), 嘲風 disebut gemar bahaya sepanjang hidupnya (平生好險), dan binatang-binatang yang berlari di sudut istana adalah sosoknya (今殿角走獸是).
statement.en: In the Yangsheng fuyu (養生膚語, by Chen Jiru, Ming), 嘲風 is said to have liked danger all its life (平生好險), and the running beasts on palace corners are its likeness (今殿角走獸是).

short_description.id: 䍺 (Huan) adalah hewan legendaris Tiongkok. Shan Hai Jing menggambarkannya seperti domba tanpa mulut yang tidak dapat dibunuh, sedangkan Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menyebutnya lahir dari kesusahan para narapidana.
short_description.en: 䍺 (Huan) is a legendary Chinese animal. The Shan Hai Jing describes it as a sheep-like beast without a mouth that cannot be killed, while Japanese Wikipedia says it was born from the distress of imprisoned people.

long_description.id: Dalam Shan Hai Jing (bagian 南山經), 䍺 adalah hewan di gunung 洵 yang bentuknya seperti domba tetapi tanpa mulut dan tidak dapat dibunuh. Catatan tafsir pada teks itu memberi bunyi namanya sebagai 還 atau 患. Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa juga menyebutnya 患 (羊患), makhluk legendaris Tiongkok kuno yang tercatat dalam Shan Hai Jing.
long_description.en: In the Shan Hai Jing (the 南山經 section), 䍺 is a beast on Xun mountain (洵) shaped like a sheep but without a mouth, and it cannot be killed. The commentary on the text gives the sound of its name as 還 or 患. Chinese Wikipedia also calls it 患 (羊患), a legendary creature of ancient China recorded in the Shan Hai Jing.

long_description.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang memberi gambaran lain: 䍺 adalah hewan legendaris yang lahir dari kesusahan para narapidana yang dikurung di penjara. Tubuhnya digambarkan seperti kambing dengan mata biru, tingginya tujuh sampai delapan meter pada yang kecil dan lebih dari sepuluh meter pada yang besar, dan kakinya tertanam di tanah sehingga tidak dapat digerakkan oleh tenaga manusia.
long_description.en: Japanese Wikipedia gives a different picture: 䍺 is a legendary animal born from the distress of convicts shut up in prison. Its body is described as goat-like with blue eyes, seven to eight metres tall for the smaller ones and over ten metres for the larger, and its feet are sunk into the ground so that human strength cannot move it.

long_description.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang mengaitkannya dengan kisah Kaisar Wu dari dinasti Han: makhluk raksasa menghalangi rombongan, dan Dongfang Shuo mengenalinya lalu menyiramnya dengan banyak arak hingga lenyap. Kisah serupa dalam Taiping guangji, yang dikutip dari Soushenji, menggambarkan sesuatu seperti sapi di Celah Hangu yang lenyap setelah disiram arak, karena menurut Dongfang Shuo ia terlahir dari kesusahan dan arak membuat orang melupakan kekhawatiran.
long_description.en: Japanese Wikipedia links it with a story of Emperor Wu of the Han dynasty: a giant creature blocked the party, and Dongfang Shuo recognised it and poured a great deal of wine over it until it vanished. A similar tale in the Taiping guangji, quoted from the Soushenji, describes an ox-shaped thing at Hangu Pass that vanished when wine was poured on it, because according to Dongfang Shuo it was born of affliction and wine makes people forget worry.

who.en: A legendary Chinese animal named 䍺 (Huan), also written 患.

famous_for.en: Known from the Shan Hai Jing's account of a beast that cannot be killed and from Dongfang Shuo's tale of the wine.

description.en: In the tale of Emperor Wu, the giant creature vanished after a large quantity of wine was poured over it, because wine makes one forget worry.

summary.en: As Emperor Wu toured, a giant creature blocked the road. Dongfang Shuo recognised it and poured a large amount of wine over it until it vanished, reasoning that wine dispels the worry that produced it.

claims.quote: 䍺（かん）は、中国に伝わる伝説上の動物。監獄に閉じ込められた罪人達の憂いの気より誕生したとされる。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, Huan adalah hewan legendaris Tiongkok yang konon lahir dari kesusahan orang-orang yang dipenjara.
statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, Huan is a legendary Chinese animal said to be born from imprisoned people’s distress.

claims.quote: 山羊をあわせた身体に青い目を持ち、身長は小さいもので7から8メートル、大きいものでは10mを超える。また足が地面にめり込んでおり、人間の力では動かせないとされる。

statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, the account gives it a huge goatlike body, blue eyes and feet fixed in the ground.

claims.quote: 漢代に武帝が巡幸した際、一行の前に巨大な山羊が現れ行く手を阻んだ。武帝の側近で博識で知られた東方朔（とうほうさく）は、それが䍺であることに気付き、䍺の憂いを晴らすために大量の酒をかけたところ䍺は消滅したという。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, Dongfang Shuo melenyapkan makhluk itu dengan arak ketika ia menghalangi perjalanan Kaisar Wu.
statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, Dongfang Shuo dispels the creature with wine when it blocks Emperor Wu’s journey.

claims.quote: 洵一作「旬」山，其陽多金，其陰多玉。有獸焉，其狀如羊而無口，不可殺也，〈稟氣自然〉其名曰䍺。

statement.id: Dalam Shan Hai Jing (南山經), di gunung 洵 ada hewan yang bentuknya seperti domba tetapi tanpa mulut dan tidak dapat dibunuh (catatan tafsir: 稟氣自然); namanya 䍺.
statement.en: In the Shan Hai Jing (南山經), on Xun mountain (洵) there is a beast shaped like a sheep but without a mouth, which cannot be killed (commentary: 稟氣自然); it is named 䍺.

claims.quote: 有獸焉，其狀如羊而無口，不可殺也，〈稟氣自然〉其名曰䍺。〈音還，或音患〉

statement.id: Catatan tafsir pada teks itu memberi bunyi nama 䍺 sebagai 還, atau 患.
statement.en: The commentary on the text gives the sound of the name 䍺 as 還, or 患.

claims.quote: 漢武帝東遊，至函谷關，有物當道，其身長數丈，其狀象牛。青眼而曜精，四足入土，動而不徙。

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang dikutip Taiping guangji dari Soushenji (搜神記): ketika Kaisar Wu dari Han berkeliling ke timur dan tiba di Celah Hangu (函谷關), sesuatu menghalangi jalan; panjang tubuhnya beberapa zhang, bentuknya seperti sapi, bermata biru yang berkilau, dan keempat kakinya masuk ke tanah; ia bergerak tetapi tidak berpindah.
statement.en: In a tale quoted in the Taiping guangji from the Soushenji (搜神記): when Emperor Wu of Han travelled east and reached Hangu Pass (函谷關), something blocked the road; its body was several zhang long, it was shaped like an ox, with gleaming blue eyes, and its four feet were sunk into the earth; it moved but did not shift.

claims.quote: 百官驚懼，東方朔乃請酒灌之，灌之數十斛而消。帝問其故，答曰：「此名憂，患之所生也。此必是秦之獄地。不然，罪人徙作地聚。夫酒忘憂，故能消之也。」

statement.id: Para pejabat ketakutan; Dongfang Shuo meminta arak untuk disiramkan ke makhluk itu, dan setelah beberapa puluh hu makhluk itu lenyap. Ia menjelaskan bahwa makhluk itu bernama 憂 (kekhawatiran), terlahir dari 患 (kesusahan); tempat itu pasti bekas penjara Qin, dan karena arak membuat orang melupakan kekhawatiran, arak dapat melenyapkannya.
statement.en: The officials were frightened; Dongfang Shuo asked for wine to be poured on it, and after several dozen hu it vanished. He explained that it is named 憂 (worry), something produced by 患 (affliction); the place must be a Qin prison site, and since wine makes one forget worry, wine could dispel it.

claims.quote: 患（羊患）是中國古代的傳說生物，於《山海经》有记载。 ... 《山海經·南山經》：「又東四百里，曰洵山，其陽多金，其陰多玉。有獸焉，其狀如羊而無口，不可殺也，其名曰䍺。」

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyebut 患 (羊患) sebagai makhluk legendaris Tiongkok kuno yang tercatat dalam Shan Hai Jing, dan mengutip kalimat 南山經 tentang hewan seperti domba tanpa mulut bernama 䍺.
statement.en: Chinese Wikipedia calls 患 (羊患) a legendary creature of ancient China recorded in the Shan Hai Jing, and quotes the 南山經 line about the sheep-like beast without a mouth named 䍺.

topic.en: The form and identity of 䍺

summary.en: Shan Hai Jing: a sheep-like beast without a mouth that cannot be killed, named 䍺.

summary.en: Japanese Wikipedia: an animal with a goat-like body, blue eyes and feet sunk into the ground, born of convicts' distress and linked with the Dongfang Shuo tale.

summary.id: Teks Soushenji dalam Taiping guangji: sesuatu seperti sapi, bermata biru, bernama 憂 dan lahir dari 患; teks itu tidak menyebut nama 䍺.
summary.en: Soushenji text in the Taiping guangji: an ox-shaped thing with blue eyes, named 憂 and born of 患; the text does not mention the name 䍺.

gaps.searched: Belum ada berkas Wikimedia Commons yang diperiksa untuk entri ini.

Wikipedia bahasa Jepang dan Tionghoa, teks Shan Hai Jing dan Taiping guangji di Wikisource dibaca; buku 草野巧 『幻想動物事典』 yang dirujuk Wikipedia bukan sumber terbuka sehingga tidak dipakai. short_description.id: White River Monster, yang oleh warga setempat dijuluki "Whitey", adalah makhluk besar yang dilaporkan terlihat di tepi White River dekat Newport, Arkansas timur laut. Penampakan dimulai pada 1915 dan sejak 1973 ia dilindungi oleh suaka resmi.
short_description.en: The White River Monster, locally nicknamed "Whitey", is a large creature reportedly spotted by the White River near Newport in northeastern Arkansas. Sightings began in 1915 and since 1973 it has had an official refuge.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Arkansas, White River Monster adalah makhluk besar yang dilaporkan pertama kali terlihat di tepi White River dekat Newport, di timur laut Arkansas. Meski disebut "monster" di pers, ia dikabarkan sangat disayangi warga sekitar bagian sungai itu, yang menyebutnya "Whitey".
long_description.en: Arkansas folklore describes the White River Monster as a big creature first reported along the banks of the White River near Newport, in the northeast of the state. Although called a "monster" in the press, it is said to be dearly loved by residents near that stretch of the river, who call it "Whitey".

long_description.id: Menurut ensiklopedia itu, penampakan dimulai pada 1915 tetapi jarang sampai 1937, ketika Bramlett Bateman, pemilik perkebunan dekat sungai, melihatnya dan menyebutnya berkulit abu-abu, selebar mobil dan sepanjang tiga mobil. Dibuatlah jaring tali raksasa dan seorang penyelam dikerahkan, tetapi Whitey tidak tertangkap. Pada 1971 penampakan muncul lagi: makhluk abu-abu bertanduk di dahi dan berpunggung berduri, disusul jejak tapak bertiga jari sepanjang empat belas inci.
long_description.en: According to the encyclopedia, sightings began in 1915 but were sporadic until 1937, when Bramlett Bateman, a plantation owner near the river, saw it and described gray skin, as wide as a car and three cars long. A huge rope net was built and a diver brought in, but Whitey was not caught. In 1971 sightings returned: a gray creature with a horn on its forehead and a spiny back, followed by a trail of three-toed, fourteen-inch prints.

long_description.id: Pada 1973, Majelis Umum Arkansas mengesahkan Resolusi Senat 23 yang membentuk Suaka Monster White River; merugikan monster itu di dalam suaka dinyatakan melanggar hukum. Penjelasan yang diajukan meliputi ikan raksasa, anjing laut gajah (pendapat biolog Roy Mackal), manatee Florida (usul Nickell), dan ikan aligator gar besar.
long_description.en: In 1973 the Arkansas General Assembly passed Senate Resolution 23, creating the White River Monster Refuge; harming the monster within the refuge is illegal. Proposed explanations include a huge fish, an elephant seal (biologist Roy Mackal's view), Florida manatees (Nickell's proposal) and a large alligator gar.

claims.quote: In Arkansas folklore, the White River Monster is a large creature reportedly first spotted off the banks of the White River near Newport in northeastern Arkansas.

statement.en: In Arkansas folklore, the White River Monster is a large creature reportedly first spotted off the banks of the White River near Newport.

claims.quote: Although reported in the press as a "monster", it is reported to be deeply loved by neighborhood residents near this portion of the White River, and the monster is referred to locally as "Whitey".

statement.id: Meski diberitakan sebagai monster, makhluk ini disayangi warga sekitar dan dijuluki Whitey oleh penduduk setempat.
statement.en: Although reported as a monster, it is loved by neighborhood residents and referred to locally as Whitey.

statement.id: Merupakan tindakan melanggar hukum untuk mencelakai monster tersebut di dalam kawasan suaka.
statement.en: It is illegal to harm the monster inside the refuge.

claims.quote: Sightings of “Whitey” began in 1915 but were sporadic until 1937. On July 1 of that year, Bramlett Bateman, owner of a plantation near the river, saw the monster.

statement.id: Penampakan "Whitey" dimulai pada 1915 tetapi jarang sampai 1937. Pada 1 Juli tahun itu, Bramlett Bateman, pemilik perkebunan di dekat sungai, melihat monster itu.
statement.en: Sightings of "Whitey" began in 1915 but were sporadic until 1937. On July 1 of that year, Bramlett Bateman, owner of a plantation near the river, saw the monster.

claims.quote: He reported it as having gray skin and being “as wide as a car and three cars long.”

statement.id: Ia melaporkannya berkulit abu-abu dan "selebar mobil dan sepanjang tiga mobil".
statement.en: He reported it as having gray skin and being "as wide as a car and three cars long".

claims.quote: As news spread, construction of a huge rope net to capture the monster began. The monster had been seen in an eddy, so a diver was brought in to search for it.

statement.id: Ketika kabar menyebar, pembuatan jaring tali raksasa untuk menangkap monster itu dimulai. Monster itu terlihat di pusaran air, sehingga seorang penyelam didatangkan untuk mencarinya.
statement.en: As news spread, construction of a huge rope net to capture the monster began. The monster had been seen in an eddy, so a diver was brought in to search for it.

claims.quote: In 1971, the sightings began again when someone reported seeing a gray creature with a horn sticking out from its forehead. Other witnesses described it as having a spiny back twenty feet long.

statement.id: Pada 1971 penampakan dimulai lagi ketika seseorang melaporkan makhluk abu-abu dengan tanduk mencuat dari dahinya. Saksi lain menggambarkannya berpunggung berduri sepanjang dua puluh kaki.
statement.en: In 1971 sightings began again when someone reported a gray creature with a horn sticking out of its forehead. Other witnesses described a spiny back twenty feet long.

claims.quote: Later, a trail of three-toed, fourteen-inch prints was found in the White River area.

statement.id: Kemudian ditemukan jejak tapak bertiga jari sepanjang empat belas inci di kawasan White River.
statement.en: Later, a trail of three-toed, fourteen-inch prints was found in the White River area.

statement.en: In 1973, the Arkansas General Assembly passed Senate Resolution 23, creating the White River Monster Refuge along the White River.

claims.quote: While there have been no recent sightings, theories about Whitey abound. It is hypothesized to be anything from a huge fish to an elephant seal, though none of the theories fully explain Whitey.

statement.id: Meski belum ada penampakan terbaru, teori tentang Whitey berlimpah. Ia diduga apa saja, dari ikan raksasa sampai anjing laut gajah, tetapi tak satu teori pun menjelaskannya sepenuhnya.
statement.en: Although there have been no recent sightings, theories about Whitey abound. It is hypothesized to be anything from a huge fish to an elephant seal, though none of the theories fully explain Whitey.

claims.quote: Nickell proposed that the monster(s) were likely Florida manatees, also known as "sea cows".

statement.id: Nickell mengusulkan bahwa monster itu kemungkinan besar manatee Florida, juga disebut "sapi laut".
statement.en: Nickell proposed that the monster(s) were likely Florida manatees, also known as "sea cows".

claims.quote: Biologist Roy Mackal was persuaded that the monster was an elephant seal, but Nickell disagreed with this hypothesis due to the White River being well out of the range of that species.

statement.id: Biolog Roy Mackal yakin bahwa monster itu anjing laut gajah, tetapi Nickell tidak setuju karena White River jauh di luar jangkauan spesies itu.

short_description.id: White Tiger adalah Harimau Putih dalam Empat Lambang rasi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: White Tiger belongs to the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations.

long_description.id: White Tiger adalah Harimau Putih dalam Empat Lambang rasi Tiongkok. Harimau Putih berhubungan dengan arah barat dan musim gugur.
long_description.en: White Tiger belongs to the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations. The White Tiger corresponds to west and autumn.

long_description.id: Nama lintas bahasanya meliputi Byakko di Jepang dan Baekho di Korea. Wilayah rasi Harimau Putih mencakup tujuh kedudukan bulan.
long_description.en: Its names in neighboring traditions include Japanese Byakko and Korean Baekho. The White Tiger's constellation region contains seven lunar mansions.

long_description.id: Huainanzi bab Tianwen xun mengaitkan barat dengan logam dan menyebut Harimau Putih sebagai binatang arah itu, sedangkan Liji bab Quli shang menempatkannya di sisi kanan dengan Naga Biru di sisi kiri. Dalam bacaan Werner, Naga Biru dan Harimau Putih menjalankan di kuil Tao tugas yang di kuil Buddha dijalankan Heng dan Ha di gerbang. Werner juga menceritakan Yin Ch'eng-hsiu, yang gugur ketika berusaha membalas ayahnya dan kemudian diangkat sebagai Roh Bintang Harimau Putih.
long_description.en: The Huainanzi chapter Tianwen xun associates the west with metal and names the White Tiger as the beast of that direction, while the Liji chapter Quli shang places it on the right with the Azure Dragon on the left. In Werner's account, the Blue Dragon and White Tiger discharge in Taoist temples the functions that Heng and Ha discharge at Buddhist temple gates. Werner also tells of Yin Ch'eng-hsiu, who died trying to avenge his father and was later canonized as the Spirit of the White Tiger Star.

claims.quote: 西方，金也，其帝少昊，其佐蓐收，執矩而治秋。其神為太白，其獸白虎，其音商，其日庚辛。

statement.id: Huainanzi bab Tianwen xun (天文訓) menyebut bahwa arah barat adalah logam (金), kaisarnya Shaohao (少昊), pembantunya Rushou (蓐收) yang memegang penyiku dan mengatur musim gugur (治秋); rohnya adalah Taibai (太白) dan binatangnya (獸) adalah Harimau Putih (白虎).
statement.en: The Huainanzi chapter Tianwen xun (天文訓) says the west is metal (金), its emperor is Shaohao (少昊) and its assistant Rushou (蓐收), who holds the square and governs autumn (治秋); its spirit is Taibai (太白) and its beast (獸) is the White Tiger (白虎).

claims.quote: 左青龍而右白虎，招摇在上，急繕其怒。進退有度，左右有局，各司其局。

statement.id: Liji bab Quli shang (曲禮上) menempatkan Naga Biru (青龍) di sisi kiri dan Harimau Putih (白虎) di sisi kanan, dengan 招摇 (Zhaoyao) di atas; gerak maju-mundur berpedoman pada aturan dan tiap bagian memegang tugas masing-masing.
statement.en: The Liji chapter Quli shang (曲禮上) puts the Azure Dragon (青龍) on the left and the White Tiger (白虎) on the right, with 招摇 (Zhaoyao) above; advance and retreat follow rules and each part keeps its own post.

claims.quote: The functions discharged by Heng and Ha at the gates of Buddhist temples are in Taoist temples discharged by Blue Dragon and White Tiger.

statement.id: Werner menulis bahwa tugas yang dijalankan Heng dan Ha di gerbang kuil Buddha dijalankan di kuil Tao oleh Blue Dragon (Naga Biru) dan White Tiger (Harimau Putih).
statement.en: Werner writes that the functions discharged by Heng and Ha at the gates of Buddhist temples are discharged in Taoist temples by Blue Dragon and White Tiger.

claims.quote: The Spirit of the White Tiger Star is Yin Ch'eng-hsiu. His father, Yin P'o-pai, a high courtier of the tyrant Chou Wang, was sent to negotiate peace with Chiang Tzu-ya, but was seized and put to death by Marquis Chiang Wen-huan.

statement.id: Werner menyebut bahwa Roh Bintang Harimau Putih adalah Yin Ch'eng-hsiu, putra Yin P'o-pai, pejabat tinggi istana tiran Chou Wang yang dikirim berunding damai dengan Chiang Tzu-ya tetapi ditangkap dan dihukum mati oleh Marquis Chiang Wen-huan.
statement.en: Werner states that the Spirit of the White Tiger Star is Yin Ch'eng-hsiu, whose father Yin P'o-pai, a high courtier of the tyrant Chou Wang, was sent to negotiate peace with Chiang Tzu-ya but was seized and put to death by Marquis Chiang Wen-huan.

claims.quote: His son, attempting to avenge his father's murder, was pierced by a spear, and his head was cut off and carried in triumph to Chiang Tzu-ya. As compensation he was, though somewhat tardily, canonized as the Spirit of the White Tiger Star.

statement.id: Menurut Werner, putra itu berusaha membalas kematian ayahnya tetapi ditombak dan kepalanya dipenggal serta dibawa dengan kemenangan kepada Chiang Tzu-ya; sebagai ganti rugi ia, meski agak terlambat, diangkat sebagai Roh Bintang Harimau Putih.
statement.en: According to Werner, the son, trying to avenge his father's murder, was pierced by a spear and his head was cut off and carried in triumph to Chiang Tzu-ya; as compensation he was, though somewhat tardily, canonized as the Spirit of the White Tiger Star.

short_description.id: La Xtabay adalah kisah rakyat Maya Yukatek tentang perempuan iblis yang memikat dan memangsa lelaki di Semenanjung Yucatán. Ia digambarkan cantik berambut hitam panjang dan berpakaian putih, menunggu di balik pohon ceiba.
short_description.en: La Xtabay is a Yucatec Maya folk tale about a demonic femme fatale who preys on men in the Yucatán Peninsula. She is pictured as a beautiful woman with long black hair and a white dress, waiting behind a ceiba tree.

long_description.id: La Xtabay adalah kisah rakyat Maya Yukatek tentang perempuan iblis yang memangsa lelaki di Semenanjung Yucatán. Konon ia tinggal di hutan dan memikat lelaki menuju kematian dengan kecantikannya yang tiada tanding. Ia digambarkan berambut hitam berkilau yang jatuh hingga mata kaki dan berpakaian putih, menunggu di balik pohon ceiba dan menyisir rambutnya dengan duri kaktus Tzacam.
long_description.en: La Xtabay is a Yucatec Maya folk tale of a demonic seductress who hunts men on the Yucatán Peninsula. She is said to live in the forest and draw men to their deaths with her matchless beauty. She is described with shining black hair falling to her ankles and a white dress, waiting behind a ceiba tree and combing her hair with the spines of the Tzacam cactus.

long_description.id: Menurut asal-usulnya, dua perempuan cantik, Xkeban dan Utz-colel, tinggal di sebuah desa. Xkeban diperlakukan buruk karena perilakunya yang dianggap bebas, sedangkan Utz-colel dianggap berbudi luhur karena membujang. Xkeban kemudian berubah menjadi bunga xtabentún, sementara Utz-colel, yang digerakkan iri dan amarah, menjadi iblis Xtabay yang tampak cantik tetapi kejam di dalam hati.
long_description.en: According to the origin story, two beautiful women, Xkeban and Utz-colel, lived in a village. Xkeban was mistreated because of her promiscuous conduct, whereas Utz-colel was thought virtuous because she stayed celibate. Xkeban was later transformed into the xtabentún flower, while Utz-colel, driven by jealousy and rage, became the demon Xtabay, beautiful outside but cruel at heart.

long_description.id: Ada pula versi lain: Xtabay dapat tampil dalam wujud atau jenis kelamin apa pun untuk memancing korbannya, atau di Quintana Roo ia menjadi penghukum pemabuk, pencuri, dan penjahat kekerasan. Di Yucatán, legenda ini dipakai para ibu dan nenek untuk menanamkan perilaku baik pada anak, dan sebuah artikel Yucatán Today mencatat monumen Xtabay di Mérida serta penjelasan bahwa legenda ini diubah pada masa kolonisasi.
long_description.en: There are other versions: Xtabay can appear in any form or sex to lure her victims, or, in Quintana Roo, she is the punisher of drunks, thieves and violent criminals. In Yucatán the legend is used by mothers and grandmothers to instill good behavior in children, and a Yucatán Today article notes a Xtabay monument in Mérida and an explanation that the legend was modified in the colonial period.

cultural_context.id: Di Semenanjung Yucatán, kata Xtabay melambangkan perilaku buruk pada perempuan dan laki-laki, dan legenda ini dipakai untuk menanamkan perilaku baik pada anak. Seorang guru setempat yang dikutip Yucatán Today menjelaskan bahwa legenda ini diubah oleh para pastor masa kolonisasi, sehingga dianggap "mestizo", perpaduan budaya pribumi dan Spanyol.
cultural_context.en: On the Yucatán Peninsula the word Xtabay stands for undesirable conduct in women and men, and the legend is used to instill good conduct in children. A local teacher quoted by Yucatán Today explains that the legend was modified by the priests of the colonization, so it is considered "mestizo", a combination of indigenous and Spanish culture.

literal_meaning.id: Istilah "Xtab" dipakai untuk merujuk pada dewi Maya kuno Ixtab, dewi bunuh diri dengan menggantung diri.
literal_meaning.en: The term "Xtab" was used to refer to the ancient Maya goddess Ixtab, goddess of suicide by hanging.

short_description.id: Yako atau nogitsune adalah jenis kitsune (roh rubah) liar berpangkat rendah yang dikisahkan di Kyūshū, dikenal merasuki orang dan menjelma manusia.
short_description.en: Yako, or nogitsune, is a type of low-ranking wild kitsune (fox spirit) told about in Kyūshū, known for possessing people and taking human form.

long_description.id: Yako atau nogitsune (野狐) adalah jenis kitsune (roh rubah) yang dikisahkan di Kyūshū. Kerasukannya disebut yako-tsuki. Kata 野狐 juga dipakai bagi rubah liar secara umum. Menurut Yokai.com, istilah ini merujuk pada kitsune liar berpangkat rendah yang bukan utusan dewa.
long_description.en: Yako or nogitsune (野狐) is a type of kitsune (fox spirit) told about in Kyūshū. Possession by it is called yako-tsuki. The word 野狐 is also used for wild foxes in general. According to Yokai.com the term refers to low-ranking wild kitsune who are not messengers of the gods.

long_description.id: Rupanya hampir selalu sama dalam semua legenda: hitam atau putih, sedikit lebih besar dari tikus dan lebih kecil dari kucing. Yako asli dikatakan tak terlihat mata. Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune dikenal menjelma manusia, memerlukan benda sihir seperti tulang sapi atau kuda untuk berubah wujud, dan sering merasuki orang.
long_description.en: Its appearance is almost completely consistent among all legends: black or white, a little bigger than a mouse yet smaller than a cat. Legends also say the first yako cannot be seen by the eye. According to Yokai.com, nogitsune are known for transforming into humans, need a magical focus such as a cow or horse bone to change shape, and often possess people.

long_description.id: Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune takut pada cahaya terang, benda tajam, dan anjing, serta menyelinap ke permukiman pada malam hari untuk mencuri lilin, minyak lampu, pernis, alkohol, dan tahu goreng. Wikipedia mencatat bahwa di Kyūshū selatan garis keluarga dapat dirasuki yako dan di Pulau Iki yako yang menyerupai musang dikatakan bersembunyi di ketiak orang.
long_description.en: According to Yokai.com, nogitsune fear bright light, bladed objects and dogs, and sneak into inhabited areas at night to steal candles, lamp oil, lacquer, alcohol and fried tofu. Wikipedia notes that in Southern Kyūshū family lines can be possessed by yako and on Iki Island weasel-like yako are said to hide under people's armpits.

description.en: According to Yokai.com, nogitsune are particularly known for transforming into humans, using a magical focus such as a cow or horse bone.

note.id: Yako atau nogitsune adalah jenis kitsune.
note.en: Yako or nogitsune is a type of kitsune.

claims.quote: Yako or nogitsune (野狐) is a type of kitsune (fox spirit), as told in Kyūshū.

statement.id: Yako adalah roh rubah dalam cerita dari Kyūshū.
statement.en: Yako is a fox spirit in stories from Kyūshū.

claims.quote: To be possessed by it is called "yako-tsuki" (野狐憑き).

statement.id: Kerasukan roh ini disebut yako-tsuki.
statement.en: Possession by this spirit is called yako-tsuki.

claims.quote: is also used for foxes in the wild in general.

statement.id: Bentuk tulis namanya juga dapat berarti rubah liar biasa.
statement.en: Its written name can also mean an ordinary wild fox.

claims.quote: The appearance of a yako is almost completely consistent among all legends; they are black or white, are slightly larger than a mouse, and smaller than a cat.

statement.id: Menurut kisah, tubuhnya kecil dan berwarna hitam atau putih.
statement.en: Accounts give it black or white coloring and a small body.

claims.quote: Nogitsune, also frequently called yako, are a type of kitsune-magical foxes found in East Asian folklore. Specifically the term refers to low ranking, wild kitsune that do not have a divine soul or serve as messengers of the gods.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune, yang sering juga disebut yako, adalah jenis kitsune; istilah ini merujuk pada kitsune liar berpangkat rendah yang tidak memiliki jiwa ilahi dan bukan utusan dewa.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, nogitsune, also frequently called yako, are a type of kitsune; the term refers to low-ranking wild kitsune that have no divine soul and are not messengers of the gods.

claims.quote: They are particularly known for transforming into humans. In folktales where humans are tormented, tricked, or possessed by kitsune, the culprit is almost always a nogitsune.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune terutama dikenal karena menjelma manusia, dan dalam dongeng tentang manusia yang disiksa, ditipu, atau dirasuki kitsune, pelakunya hampir selalu nogitsune.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, nogitsune are particularly known for transforming into humans, and in folktales where humans are tormented, tricked or possessed by kitsune, the culprit is almost always a nogitsune.

claims.quote: They dislike bright light, and hide from the sun during the daytime. They are also afraid of bladed objects, and will avoid swords and knives. They are frightened of dogs as well.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune tidak suka cahaya terang dan bersembunyi dari matahari di siang hari, takut pada benda tajam seperti pedang dan pisau, dan takut pada anjing.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, nogitsune dislike bright light and hide from the sun by day, fear bladed objects such as swords and knives, and are frightened of dogs.

claims.quote: In order to change its shape, a nogitsune requires a magical focus of some kind; usually a bone from a cow or a horse. Kitsunetsuki-possession by a fox spirit-is also commonly performed by nogitsune.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, untuk berubah wujud nogitsune memerlukan benda sihir, biasanya tulang sapi atau kuda; kitsunetsuki (perasukan oleh roh rubah) juga sering dilakukan nogitsune.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, to change shape a nogitsune needs a magical focus, usually a bone from a cow or horse; kitsunetsuki, possession by a fox spirit, is also commonly performed by nogitsune.

claims.quote: they like to sneak into human-inhabited areas at night to steal some of their favorite foods: wax candles, lamp oil, lacquer, alcohol, and fried tofu.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune menyelinap ke permukiman manusia pada malam hari untuk mencuri makanan kesukaan mereka: lilin, minyak lampu, pernis, alkohol, dan tahu goreng.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, nogitsune sneak into human-inhabited areas at night to steal favourite foods: wax candles, lamp oil, lacquer, alcohol and fried tofu.

claims.quote: The most common one-yako-is simply another reading of the kanji in its name. The name yakan (野干) is more archaic, and has its origins in a different animal.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, yako hanyalah cara baca lain kanji nama nogitsune, sedangkan nama yakan (野干) lebih arkais dan berasal dari hewan yang berbeda.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, yako is simply another reading of the kanji of its name, while the name yakan (野干) is more archaic and originates from a different animal.

claims.quote: Nogitsune 野狐 のぎつね Translation: wild fox Alternate names: yako, yakan

statement.id: Yokai.com menulis 野狐 (のぎつね) dengan terjemahan "rubah liar" dan nama lain yako dan yakan.
statement.en: Yokai.com gives 野狐 (のぎつね) with the translation "wild fox" and the alternate names yako and yakan.

claims.quote: The original yako is said to be invisible to the eye. In Hirado, Nagasaki Prefecture, they normally bring along a great crowd that walks with them

statement.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa yako asli dikatakan tak terlihat mata, dan di Hirado, Prefektur Nagasaki, mereka biasanya membawa serombongan besar yang berjalan bersama mereka.
statement.en: Wikipedia notes that the original yako is said to be invisible to the eye, and that in Hirado, Nagasaki Prefecture, they normally bring along a great crowd that walks with them.

claims.quote: In Southern Kyūshū, family lines would get possessed by a yako, and family lines that raised yako (possessed by a yako) would have their progeny possessed, and if they were no longer able to support it, it would possess its cattle and horses.

statement.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa di Kyūshū selatan garis keluarga dapat dirasuki yako, keturunannya ikut dirasuki, dan bila tak sanggup lagi memeliharanya, yako merasuki ternak dan kuda mereka.
statement.en: Wikipedia notes that in Southern Kyūshū family lines would get possessed by a yako, their progeny would be possessed, and if they could no longer support it, it would possess their cattle and horses.

claims.quote: On Iki Island, they are also called yako, and since they resemble weasels, it is said that when one of them conceals themselves under a person's armpits, that person would become possessed by a yako.

statement.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa di Pulau Iki mereka juga disebut yako dan menyerupai musang; bila salah satunya bersembunyi di ketiak seseorang, orang itu dikatakan dirasuki yako.
statement.en: Wikipedia notes that on Iki Island they are also called yako and resemble weasels; when one conceals itself under a person's armpits, that person is said to become possessed by a yako.

short_description.id: Yakusanoikazuchi adalah nama kolektif delapan kami petir dalam mitologi, yang menurut Kojiki bersemayam di jasad Izanami di Yomi dan mengejar Izanagi.
short_description.en: Yakusanoikazuchi is the collective name of the eight thunder kami in mythology, which in the Kojiki dwell in Izanami's corpse in Yomi and pursue Izanagi.

long_description.id: Yakusanoikazuchi adalah nama kolektif delapan kami petir. Para dewa itu mewakili berbagai bentuk badai. Unsur ikazuchi (雷) berarti petir. Delapan kami ini mencakup, antara lain, Fusu-ikazuchi, Hono-ikazuchi, dan Ō-ikazuchi.
long_description.en: Yakusanoikazuchi is the collective name of eight thunder kami. The deities represent different forms of storm. The element ikazuchi (雷) means thunder. The eight include Fusu-ikazuchi, Hono-ikazuchi and Ō-ikazuchi, among others.

long_description.id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Shinto, kedelapan kami petir membusuk di dalam jasad Izanami seperti dilihat Izanagi di Yomi. Kojiki menempatkan petir pada kepala, dada, perut, kemaluan, kedua tangan, dan kedua kaki Izanami, sedangkan satu tulisan alternatif Nihongi memberi penempatan dan sebagian nama yang berbeda. Satu tafsir menyejajarkan kelahiran delapan petir ini dengan delapan kami dari tubuh Kagutsuchi.
long_description.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, the eight thunder kami festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by Izanagi in Yomi. The Kojiki places thunders in Izanami's head, breast, belly, genitals, both hands and both legs, while an alternate writing in the Nihongi gives a different placement and some different names. One interpretation parallels the birth of these eight thunders with the eight kami from the body of Kagutsuchi.

long_description.id: Menurut beberapa penuturan, para dewa itu berasal dari belatung jasad Izanami yang membusuk. Setelah Izanagi melihat jasad Izanami dan melarikan diri ketakutan, Izanami mengirim Yomotsu-shikome, 150 pendekar, dan delapan kami petir mengejarnya. Menurut ensiklopedia, Izanagi melempar buah persik gaib di Yomotsuhirasaka dan mengusir para pengejar. Kojiki menempatkan Petir Hitam di perut Izanami, sedangkan Nihon Shoki menempatkannya di dubur.
long_description.en: Some tellings say the eight deities came from the maggots of Izanami's rotting corpse. After Izanagi saw Izanami's corpse and escaped in horror, Izanami dispatched the Yomotsu-shikome, 150 warriors, together with the eight thunder kami to pursue him. According to the encyclopedia, Izanagi threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka and dispersed his pursuers. The Kojiki places Black Thunder in Izanami's belly, while the Nihon Shoki places it in her rectum.

cultural_context.id: Menurut ensiklopedia, delapan adalah angka suci tetapi di sini mungkin berarti "sangat banyak", dan delapan petir sejajar dengan delapan kami dari tubuh Kagutsuchi.
cultural_context.en: According to the encyclopedia, eight is a sacred number but here may mean "a great many", and the eight thunders parallel the eight kami from Kagutsuchi's body.

note.en: The eight thunders from Izanami's corpse are paralleled with the eight kami from the dismembered body of Kagutsuchi.

note.id: Salah satu dari delapan petir; menurut Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki berasal dari kepala Izanami.
note.en: One of the eight thunders; the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki say it came from Izanami's head.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa Kojiki dan Nihongi menempatkan petir pada bagian tubuh Izanami yang berbeda?
learning_questions.en: Why do the Kojiki and the Nihongi place the thunders on different parts of Izanami's body?

claims.quote: Yakusanoikazuchi or ikazuchi is a collective name for the eight kami of thunder in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Yakusanoikazuchi adalah nama kolektif delapan kami petir.
statement.en: Yakusanoikazuchi is the collective name of eight thunder kami.

claims.quote: Each one represents a different type of storm.

statement.id: Para dewa itu mewakili berbagai bentuk badai.
statement.en: The deities represent different forms of storm.

claims.quote: Ikazuchi (雷) literally means thunder in Japanese.

statement.id: Unsur ikazuchi berarti petir.
statement.en: The element ikazuchi means thunder.

claims.quote: Some tellings say that the eight deities were from the maggots of Izanami's rotting corpse.

statement.id: Beberapa penuturan menyebut kedelapan dewa itu berasal dari belatung jasad Izanami yang membusuk.
statement.en: Some tellings say the eight deities came from the maggots of Izanami's rotting corpse.

claims.quote: Many versions of the Nihon Shoki and the Kojiki state that after Izanagi saw his wife in such a state and fled in terror, Izanami sent the Yomotsu-shikome, 150 warriors, and the eight thunder kami after him.

statement.id: Mereka mengejar Izanagi ketika ia melarikan diri dari alam kematian.
statement.en: They pursue Izanagi when he flees the underworld.

claims.quote: Kuro-ikazuchi: (Black thunder) The Kojiki says that this deity came from Izanami's belly.

statement.id: Kojiki menempatkan Petir Hitam di perut Izanami.
statement.en: The Kojiki places Black Thunder in Izanami’s belly.

claims.quote: However, the Nihon Shoki says that Kuro-ikazuchi was in Izanami's rectum.

statement.id: Nihon Shoki justru menempatkan Petir Hitam di duburnya.
statement.en: The Nihon Shoki instead places Black Thunder in her rectum.

claims.quote: [Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami] (Kojiki) The "eight kinds of thunder kami" that festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by her consort Izanagi in the underworld of Yomi.

statement.id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Shinto, Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami dalam Kojiki adalah "delapan jenis kami petir" yang membusuk di dalam jasad Izanami, seperti dilihat suaminya Izanagi di dunia bawah Yomi.
statement.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, the Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami of the Kojiki are the "eight kinds of thunder kami" that festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by her consort Izanagi in the underworld of Yomi.

claims.quote: According to Kojiki, in her head was the "great thunder," in her breast was the "fire thunder," in her belly was the "black thunder," in her genitals was the "cleft thunder," in her left hand was the "young thunder," in the right hand was the "earth thunder," in her left leg was the "sounding thunder," and in her right leg was the "reposing thunder."

statement.id: Menurut Kojiki, kedelapan petir itu berada di kepala (petir besar), dada (petir api), perut (petir hitam), kemaluan (petir belah), tangan kiri (petir muda), tangan kanan (petir tanah), kaki kiri (petir bergema), dan kaki kanan (petir beristirahat) Izanami.
statement.en: According to the Kojiki, the eight thunders were in the corpse's head (great thunder), breast (fire thunder), belly (black thunder), genitals (cleft thunder), left hand (young thunder), right hand (earth thunder), left leg (sounding thunder) and right leg (reposing thunder).

claims.quote: An "alternate writing" transmitted by Nihongi, however, states that "great thunder" was in her head, "fire thunder" was in her breast, "earth thunder" was in her belly, "young thunder" was in her back, "black thunder" was in her rectum, "mountain thunder" was in her hands, "field thunder" was in her feet, and "cleft thunder" was in her genitals.

statement.id: Satu "tulisan alternatif" dalam Nihongi menyebut petir besar di kepala, petir api di dada, petir tanah di perut, petir muda di punggung, petir hitam di dubur, petir gunung di tangan, petir ladang di kaki, dan petir belah di kemaluan.
statement.en: An "alternate writing" transmitted by the Nihongi states that great thunder was in her head, fire thunder in her breast, earth thunder in her belly, young thunder in her back, black thunder in her rectum, mountain thunder in her hands, field thunder in her feet and cleft thunder in her genitals.

claims.quote: Of the eight thunders, three have the same name and place in the two accounts, three agree in name only, and the remaining two are different.

statement.id: Dari delapan petir itu, tiga memiliki nama dan tempat yang sama dalam dua catatan, tiga hanya sama namanya, dan dua sisanya berbeda.
statement.en: Of the eight thunders, three have the same name and place in the two accounts, three agree in name only, and the remaining two are different.

claims.quote: The fact that eight thunders were produced in Izanami's dead body parallels the fact that eight kami were produced from the dismembered body of the fire kami Kagutsuchi. While eight is considered a sacred number, it is here likely used merely to denote "a great many."

statement.id: Lahirnya delapan petir dari jasad Izanami disamakan dengan lahirnya delapan kami dari tubuh Kagutsuchi yang terpotong; delapan dianggap angka suci, tetapi di sini mungkin hanya berarti "sangat banyak".
statement.en: The eight thunders produced in Izanami's dead body parallel the eight kami produced from the dismembered body of the fire kami Kagutsuchi; eight is considered a sacred number but is here likely used merely to denote "a great many".

claims.quote: According to the various Kojiki and Nihongi accounts mentioned above, Izanami ordered the "hags of Yomi" and the eight thunder kami to chase Izanagi ... Izanagi, however, threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka (the "Even Pass of Yomi"), and thus dispersed his pursuers.

statement.id: Menurut berbagai catatan Kojiki dan Nihongi, Izanami memerintahkan "nenek-nenek Yomi" dan delapan kami petir mengejar Izanagi; Izanagi melempar buah persik gaib di Yomotsuhirasaka dan mengusir para pengejarnya.
statement.en: According to the various Kojiki and Nihongi accounts, Izanami ordered the "hags of Yomi" and the eight thunder kami to chase Izanagi; Izanagi threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka and thus dispersed his pursuers.

claims.quote: Fusu-ikazuchi: (Couchant thunder) Hono-ikazuchi: (Fire thunder) the Kojiki says that this kami came from Izanami's breasts.

statement.id: Daftar Wikipedia mencantumkan Fusu-ikazuchi (petir berbaring) dan Hono-ikazuchi (petir api); Kojiki menyebut Hono-ikazuchi berasal dari dada Izanami.
statement.en: The Wikipedia list gives Fusu-ikazuchi (couchant thunder) and Hono-ikazuchi (fire thunder); the Kojiki says Hono-ikazuchi came from Izanami's breasts.

claims.quote: Ō-ikazuchi: (Great thunder) both the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki state that Ō-ikazuchi came from Izanami's head.

statement.id: Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki sama-sama menyebut Ō-ikazuchi (petir besar) berasal dari kepala Izanami.
statement.en: Both the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki state that Ō-ikazuchi (great thunder) came from Izanami's head.

summary.id: Kojiki menyebut perut.
summary.en: The Kojiki names the belly.

summary.id: Nihon Shoki menyebut dubur.
summary.en: The Nihon Shoki names the rectum.

topic.id: Letak delapan petir pada tubuh Izanami
topic.en: Placement of the eight thunders on Izanami's body

summary.id: Kojiki: kepala, dada, perut, kemaluan, tangan kiri, tangan kanan, kaki kiri, kaki kanan.
summary.en: Kojiki: head, breast, belly, genitals, left hand, right hand, left leg, right leg.

summary.id: Tulisan alternatif Nihongi: kepala, dada, perut, punggung, dubur, tangan, kaki, kemaluan, dengan sebagian nama berbeda; tiga cocok penuh, tiga hanya namanya, dua berbeda.
summary.en: Nihongi alternate writing: head, breast, belly, back, rectum, hands, feet, genitals, with some different names; three match fully, three in name only, two differ.
